"We have sustained our growth momentum in the second quarter, with most of the businesses 
growing in double digits. Demand held up well across our end-markets, as the affordability 
benefits of GST rationalisation continued. We were further aided by favourable seasonal 
demand for Home UPS business. Growth opportunities remain encouraging across Automotive 
OEMs, Replacement, Home Inverters, Solar, Infrastructure and Exports. 
 
The Automotive OEM business grew by over 25% for the fourth consecutive quarter, and the 
2W/4W Replacement business sustained its double-digit growth. Home Inverters and Solar also 
had a strong quarter, growing over 20%. Exports grew by over 20% YoY on a low base, and our 
long-term strategic cooperation agreement with ExCom Energy Solutions GmbH, Germany, 
strengthens our presence in the European Economic Area. 
 
Input costs remained elevated vs last year, due to prolonged geopolitical challenges, especially 
across West Asia. Crude oil prices went up significantly, resulting in an overall inflationary 
environment. On a sequential quarter basis, the full benefits of softer Lead LME and antimony 
prices could not be fully realized due to continuous weakening of Rupee against US Dollar. 
 
The Company undertook various cost optimisation initiatives to absorb this cost pressure. 
Further, calibrated price increase and operating leverage enabled EBITDA margin expansion in 
Q2 and H1 of FY27. 
 
We enter the festive season with healthy demand indicators. At the same time, we remain 
mindful of the high base of last year's post-GST demand surge as well as continue to closely 
monitor input costs.

completed the commissioning of 6 GWh of lithium-ion cell gigafactory in Bengaluru. Our focus 
over the coming quarters is on stabilising the lines, improving yields and completing customer 
qualifications. These achievements reinforce our confidence in building a strong foundation in 
the New Energy business."

About Exide Industries Limited 
For close to eight decades, Exide has been one of India's most reliable battery brands, enjoying 
strong reputation and brand recall. Exide designs, manufactures, markets, and sells the widest 
range of lead acid storage batteries in the world from 2.5Ah to 20,200Ah capacity, to cover the 
broadest spectrum of applications. The batteries are manufactured for Automotive, Power, 
Telecom, Infrastructure projects, UPS systems as well as for Railways, Mining, and Defence 
sectors. The company enjoys leadership position in India and its exports span 70+ countries 
across six continents. 
Exide, through its wholly owned subsidiary, Exide Energy Solutions Limited (“EESL”), completed 
the commissioning of 6 GWh of its greenfield lithium-ion cell manufacturing facility in Bengaluru 
in September 2026. The project is scalable up to 12 GWh catering to both LFP and NMC 
chemistries. The facility is designed to serve India’s electric mobility and stationary energy 
storage markets. Its existing module and pack facility at Prantij, Gujarat has helped build early 
market presence and customer engagement in lithium-ion solutions.

About Dr Lal PathLabs Limited 
Dr Lal PathLabs is a provider of diagnostic and related healthcare tests and services in India. Through 
its’ integrated, nationwide network, the company offer patients and healthcare providers a broad range 
of diagnostic and related healthcare tests and services for use in core testing, patient diagnosis and the 
prevention, monitoring and treatment of disease and other health conditions. 
 
As on March 31, 2026 the company has 312 clinical laboratories (including National Reference Lab 
at Delhi, Regional Reference Lab at Kolkata, Bangalore & Mumbai), 7,727 Patient Service Centers 
(PSCs) and 13,935 Pick-up Points (PUPs). Its’ customers include individual patients, hospitals and 
other healthcare providers and corporate customers.

leadership and continued investments in innovation and 
advanced diagnostics, we remain committed to supporting 
India's healthcare journey while improving access to reliable 
diagnostics across the country.”

About Dr. Lal PathLabs Limited (DLPL)
Dr. Lal PathLabs Limited is one of India’s leading consumer healthcare brand in diagnostic services.
It has an integrated nationwide network, where patients and healthcare providers are offered a broad 
range of diagnostic and related healthcare tests and services for use in core testing, patient diagnosis 
and the prevention, monitoring and treatment of disease and other health conditions. The services of 
DLPL are aimed at individual patients, hospitals and other healthcare providers and corporates. The 
catalogue of services includes 525 test panels, 3,130 pathology tests and 1,173 radiology and  
cardiology tests as on March 31, 2026.
As on March 31, 2026, DLPL’s has 312 clinical labs (including National Reference Lab at Delhi & Regional 
Reference Lab at Kolkata, Bangalore & Mumbai), 7,727 Patient Service Centers (PSCs) and 13,935 Pick-up 
Points (PUPs). In FY26 & FY25, DLPL collected and processed approximately 94.5 million samples and 
85.6 million samples from 30.3 million and 28.8 million patients, respectively.

About Dr. Lal PathLabs Limited (DLPL)
Dr. Lal PathLabs Limited is one of India’s leading consumer healthcare brand in diagnostic services.
It has an integrated nationwide network, where patients and healthcare providers are offered a broad 
range of diagnostic and related healthcare tests and services for use in core testing, patient diagnosis 
and the prevention, monitoring and treatment of disease and other health conditions. The services of 
DLPL are aimed at individual patients, hospitals and other healthcare providers and corporates. The 
catalogue of services includes 525 test panels, 3,130 pathology tests and 1,173 radiology and  
cardiology tests as on March 31, 2026.
As on March 31, 2026, DLPL’s has 312 clinical labs (including National Reference Lab at Delhi & Regional 
Reference Lab at Kolkata, Bangalore & Mumbai), 7,727 Patient Service Centers (PSCs) and 13,935 Pick-up 
Points (PUPs). In FY26 & FY25, DLPL collected and processed approximately 94.5 million samples and 
85.6 million samples from 30.3 million and 28.8 million patients, respectively.

2015 (“the Listing Regulations”) 
 
Dear Sir/ Madam, 
 
Please take note that the Board of Directors in their meeting held today i.e. November 04, 2026, 
inter-alia considered, noted and approved the following(s): 
 
Financial Results 
 
1. Un-audited (Standalone & Consolidated) Financial Results of the Company for the Quarter and 
Half Year ended September 30, 2026. 
 
A signed copy of the above Financial Results (Standalone & Consolidated) along with Limited 
Review Report issued by Statutory Auditors thereon under Regulation 33 of the Listing 
Regulations is attached herewith as “Annexure- A”. 
 
Interim Dividend 
 
2. Declaration of 2nd Interim Dividend of INR 5/- per equity share (@ 50% on a face value of INR 
10/- each) for the financial year 2026-27. The record date for the purpose of payment of 2nd 
Interim Dividend shall be November 11, 2026. 
 
The 2nd Interim Dividend will be paid within 30 days of its declaration. 
 
Appointment of Director 
 
3. Based on the recommendation of Nomination and Remuneration Committee, the Appointment 
of Ms. Vasuta Agarwal (DIN: 07480674) as an Additional Director designated as a Non-
Executive Independent Director on the Board of the Company, for a term of three (3) consecutive 
years commencing from November 04, 2026, subject to approval of Members of the Company 
through postal ballot. 
 
Please also take note that Ms. Vasuta Agarwal is not debarred from holding the office of Director 
by virtue of any order of Securities and Exchange Board of India or any other such Authority. 
 
The disclosure(s) as required under Regulation 30 of the Listing Regulations read with SEBI 
Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2023/123 dated July 13, 2023, as amended from 
time to time are enclosed herewith as “Annexure – B”. 

Further investment in Subsidiary Company 
4.
Further investment(s) of an amount upto INR 49.5 Crores in Dr. Lal PathLabs FZCO, (“LPL
Dubai”), a Wholly Owned Subsidiary of the Company, in one or more tranches, for meeting its
business and operational requirements, including making further investment in its subsidiary,
Sunshine Healthcare Limited (“SHL”), Ghana.
The disclosure(s) as required under Regulation 30 of the Listing Regulations read with SEBI
Circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/CFD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2023/123 dated July 13, 2023, as amended from
time to time is enclosed herewith as “Annexure – C”.

Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to Schaeffler India Limited Q3 CY26 Earnings 
Conference Call. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode and there 
will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need 
assistance during the conference call, please signal an operator by pressing star then zero on 
your touchtone phone. Please note the conference is being recorded. I now hand the conference 
over to Ms. Gauri from Schaeffler India Limited. Thank you, and over to you, ma'am. 
Gauri Kanikar: 
Good morning everyone, and welcome to Schaeffler India Limited's Earnings Conference Call 
for the third quarter and nine months ended September 2026. Today, we have with us Mr. Harsha 
Kadam our Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer and Ms. Hardevi Vazirani, our 
Director of Finance and Chief Financial Officer. As always, Mr. Kadam will first take us through 
a short presentation on the results, and then we will open the floor for questions. Thank you, and 
over to you, Mr. Kadam. 
Harsha Kadam: 
Good morning, and a very warm welcome to this third quarter and nine months ending business 
performance.  
Hardevi Vazirani: 
Good morning from my side as well. 
Harsha Kadam: 
Yes. Let me briefly take you through the presentation, and I would be covering three broad areas 
as that is indicated on Slide number 3 of the presentation. First would be a little light on the 
economy and the industry. Second would be on the business highlights for the third quarter and 
nine months ending for 2026. And lastly, the financial highlights for the third quarter and nine 
months ending 2026. 
 
Let me draw your attention to Slide number 4, where I will talk a little bit about the economy. 
Now as you can see, a strong performance from an economic standpoint on the Indian economy. 
The estimated growth was at 6.4% in the third quarter. And the numbers that are coming out is 
much stronger than that. However, despite the global uncertainty, the volatility that exists around 
us today, India still has come out stronger. 
 
And the International Monetary Fund recently has upgraded its full year growth forecast to 
average 7% GDP on the back of a very strong robust domestic market and also the booming 
digital services sector as well as the exports business. If one were to look at the Index of 
Industrial Production, strong manufacturing output in the automotive industry, on the back of 
the GST 2.0 drive has helped in terms of beating the targets as well, and it has reached an all-
time high of 7.7% IIP, as you can see there. 
 
The growth is structurally sound, and it is led by heavy manufacturing and also the utility sector 
as well as the power and electricity generation sector, all have done exceedingly well in the 
quarter. The automotive production has been one of the stellar performances. As I mentioned 
already, the GST 2.0 is propelling the growth, bringing in a very strong traction in demand. 
 
And this is, as you can see from a Q3 year-on-year growth standing at close to 31%, 32% and a 
quarter-on-quarter almost at 23%. Passenger vehicles by far leading the pack with 25% growth 
and tractor sector too on a muted monsoon performance, still at 7% growth. A cautionary trend 
is on the inflation. As you can see, the Consumer Price Index, food prices have started to increase 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Schaeffler India Limited 
 
October 29, 2026 
 
Page 3 of 16 
 
PUBLIC 
quarter-on-quarter, and that's the alarming sentiments that are prevailing on the food inflationary 
increases that have happened. With that, I move to the next slide, which is more focused on the 
sectors and what you see is the industrial sectoral performance. 
 
And very clearly, on the back of the focus from the Government of India on the core 
infrastructure sector, we have seen the core industrial sectors such as cement, steel doing it pretty 
well, registering a strong growth there as well. Month-over-month, as you can see over the 
previous years in the bar chart, cement production in the country has been consistently growing 
and average growth rate almost over 9.3%, as you can see over the last year. 
 
Steel, on the other hand, continues to be at the same levels as last year, but marginally again, 
growing at about 3%. Mining and coal production with a clear focus on renewable energy sector. 
So the coal is something that always fluctuates and talk about power generation. 
 
Again, as I said earlier, strong growth in energy demand in the country and which is clearly 
growing at about 8%, very strong focus on the renewable energy and overall, the energy security 
that the government is bringing in a focus as such. Moving to Slide number 6, a little light on 
the automotive sector performance. 
 
Almost all the automotive segments have performed exceedingly well. As you can see, the 2- 
and 3-wheelers also have grown phenomenally and close to 3 million produced only in the month 
of September has consistently shown the growth of the two and three-wheeler business in India. 
And fortunately, with the festival season split between October and November, some of the 
strongest growth months are yet to be crossed. 
 
Passenger vehicles have been one of the strongest performances with a year-to-date growth of 
almost 18% growth, which you are seeing there. Again, once again registering an all-time high 
production level in passenger vehicle segment. Interestingly, the commercial vehicle also has 
registered a very strong 21% growth, as you can see, month after month, continuing to grow. 
Commercial vehicles have always been a cyclical business. And I guess we are seeing the peaks 
of the business, but we'll have to wait and watch how it pans out in 2027. 
 
But for the moment, this year, commercial vehicles too have registered a pretty strong growth 
compared to last year. Tractors have been performing as expected, although on a little bit of 
muted monsoons that we have been hearing. We still have to track and watch what's going to 
happen to tractors in the next 3 months. However, so far, tractors have registered a year-to-date 
growth of 18% over last year, as you can see in the bar chart. That said, I move to Slide number 
8, where I would throw light on the business performance. 
 
On this backdrop, with all the volatility in the market, the uncertainty in the market, the 
challenges in the export market, what we were able to bring into the company was a revenue of 
INR 3,005 crores for the third quarter, which was a 27.4% growth over the same quarter last 
year and a 12.1% growth over the preceding quarter. Almost all the business segments have been 
able to deliver a double-digit growth rate for us in the quarter. 
 
This has resulted into an EBITDA of 18.7% in the quarter of this year compared to the preceding 
quarter of 19.1%. The margins did come under pressure due to the increased input costs as a 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Schaeffler India Limited 
 
October 29, 2026 
 
Page 4 of 16 
 
PUBLIC 
result of the volatility that is existing in the market and also the West Asia crisis, which has 
impacted the energy cost and the fuel prices and some of the cascading impact that it has  had 
on the downstream operations as well. So, with that, our margins came under a bit of pressure, 
and hence, you see a marginal drop from 19.1% to an 18.7%. 
 
The profit after tax, too, came under some challenge with 12.3% in the quarter against the 12.6% 
over the preceding quarter.  It was impacted due to increase in working capital, some that were 
planned and some a little unplanned inventory buildup that we had lined up in our e-mobility 
sector. Some challenges on the price recoveries from our customers due to the inflationary 
increases, which is still work in progress for us and also on the account receivable situation, 
which we still are getting our hands around to address it in the next  in this and the coming 
quarter. 
 
Obviously, with that, we did see some impact of all these coming on to the free cash flow, and 
we registered only INR 41 crores of free cash coming into the system, which was phenomenally 
lower percentage, as compared to the preceding quarter as well. But that is something we are 
focused upon to recover the situation on the free cash flow in the coming quarter, and we will 
try and deliver in line with our expectations as well. The good news is our capex framework still 
remains strong. 
 
In fact, we did have the highest capex spending happening in the third quarter, which I will come 
to in a while. Let me move to Slide number 9. What has kept us going and the revenue growth 
that you see is because of a strong pipeline of new business wins. We continue to keep the focus 
on winning new businesses with our existing customers as well as with new customer 
acquisitions that we do. And as a result, as you can see in the Automotive Technologies space, 
we did have a lot of business in the engine application portfolio such as our lash adjusters, HLA-
RFF, the roller tappets and so on. 
 
We also had some strong business win in the clutch portfolio for the automotive application, 
passenger vehicles in particular, and some of the rocker arm assemblies that go into the engine. 
So we have had some significant business wins, which ensures we continue to keep our top line 
growth going forward as well.

Dear Sirs,  
 
Sub: Outcome of Board Meeting held on November 4, 2026 
 
Pursuant to Regulation 30 of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 
2015 (“Listing Regulations”), we wish to inform you that the Board of Directors at its meeting held 
today, inter alia, considered and approved the following: - 
 
(a) Un-audited Financial Results (Standalone and Consolidated) of the Company for the quarter/ 
half year ended September 30, 2026. 
 
(b) Appointment of Mr. Ravi Kumar Shingari as the Chief Financial Officer (Key Managerial 
Personnel/ Senior Management) of the Company, with effect from November 4, 2026, basis 
the recommendation of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee and the Audit 
Committee. Details required as per Regulation 30 of the Listing Regulations, as amended, 
read with SEBI Master Circular no. HO/49/14/14(7)2025-CFD-POD2/I/3762/2026 dated 
January 30, 2026 are enclosed as Annexure A. 
 
(a) Raising of funds by issue of Non-Convertible Debentures (NCDs) aggregating up to 
Rs.10,000 million to be allotted in one or more tranches, through Private Placement, within 
the borrowing limits approved by the Shareholders under Section 180(1)(c) of the Companies 
Act, 2013, subject to approval of the Shareholders through Postal Ballot. Other details 
pursuant to Regulation 30 of Listing Regulations shall be provided after finalisation by the 
Board or its Committee.

read with SEBI Master Circular no. HO/49/14/14(7)2025-CFD-POD2/I/3762/2026 dated

pursuant to Regulation 30 of Listing Regulations shall be provided after finalisation by the

Dear Sir / Madam, 
Pursuant to Regulation 30 and other applicable provisions of the LODR Regulations, this is to inform 
that SES ESG Research Private Limited (“SES Ratings”) has voluntarily assigned an ESG Rating of 
78.6 to KFin Technologies Limited (“Company”). This rating is based on the Company’s public 
disclosure on the ESG parameters at the standalone level and other information in the public domain. 
As per SEBI’s Master Circular for ESG Rating Providers dated July 11, 2025, in the interest of clarity 
to market participants, it is mandated that ESG ratings shall be provided on a scale of 0 – 100, where 
100 represents the maximum score. 
Details as per BSE’s Circular No. 20230714-34 dated July 14, 2023, and NSE’s Circular No. NSE 
/CML/2023/57 dated July 14, 2023, are as under:

November 03, 2026*

This is for your information and records.

Q2 & H1 FY27 Earnings Conference Call 
October 30, 2026

MANAGEMENT: MR. MAULIK MEHTA – DEPUTY MANAGING DIRECTOR  
 
MR. SANJAY UPADHYAY – DIRECTOR (FINANCE) AND &

MR. SOMSEKHAR NANDA – CFO – DEEPAK NITRITE 
LIMITED  
 
 
 
MODERATOR: 
MR. RANJIT CIRUMALLA – IIFL CAPITAL  
 
 
 

 
Deepak Nitrite Limited 
 
 
October 30, 2026 
 
Page 2 of 20 
 
Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to the Deepak Nitrite Q2 & H1 FY27 Earnings 
Conference Call hosted by IIFL Capital Services Limited. As a reminder, all participant lines 
will be in the listen-only mode and there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after 
the presentation concludes. At the outset, I would like to clarify that certain statements made or 
discussed on the conference call today may be forward-looking in nature, and a disclaimer to 
this effect has been included in the investor communication shared with you earlier. I now hand 
the conference over to Mr. Ranjit Cirumalla from IIFL Capital Services Limited. Thank you, 
and over to you. 
Ranjit Cirumalla: 
Thank you. Good afternoon everyone, and thank you for joining us on Deepak Nitrite's Q2 & 
H1 FY27 Earnings Conference Call. Today, we have with us Mr. Maulik Mehta, Deputy 
Managing Director; Mr. Sanjay Upadhyay, Director Finance and & Group CFO; and Mr. 
Somsekhar Nanda, CFO of Deepak Nitrite Limited. 
 
We will begin the call with opening remarks from the management team, followed by an 
interactive Q&A session. To begin, Mr. Maulik Mehta will share views on the operating 
performance and growth plans of the Company, followed by Mr. Sanjay Upadhyay, who shall 
take us through the financial and segmental performance. The results documents have been 
shared with you earlier and has been posted on the Company's website. 
 
I now invite Mr. Mehta to share his opening comments. Thank you, and over to you, sir. 
Maulik Mehta: 
Thank you. Good afternoon everybody, and a warm welcome to Deepak Nitrite's Q2 & H1 FY27 
Earnings Conference Call. Thank you for your continued interest in the Company.  
Our investor presentation and financial results have already been shared, and I trust you had an 
opportunity to review them. 
 
I will begin by sharing our perspective on the operating environment, business performance and 
strategic developments, following which Mr. Upadhyay will take you through the financial 
results in greater detail. 
 
At the outset, I am delighted to announce that we have achieved the Best Ever Performance in 
Deepak Nitrite's operating history of over 5 decades, delivering record Revenue and EBITDA 
on both a quarterly as well as a half yearly basis. Consolidated revenue from operations for Q2 
FY27 stood at INR 3,091 crore, registering a sequential growth of 19% and year-on-year growth 
of 61%.  
What makes this achievement particularly noteworthy is the challenging environment in which 
it has been accomplished. I would like to congratulate our entire team for its commitment, agility 
and outstanding execution. 
 
The global chemical industry continues to navigate significant volatility arising from 
geopolitical developments, disruptions to international trade, elevated freight and energy costs 
as well as uneven demand across end-use applications. These developments are also influencing 
sourcing preferences, with customers increasingly valuing assured delivery, consistent quality 
as well as reliability of supply.  

 
Deepak Nitrite Limited 
 
 
October 30, 2026 
 
Page 3 of 20 
 
For Deepak, this environment has presented opportunities as well as challenges. Our extensive 
domestic manufacturing footprint, integrated operations and ability to respond swiftly to 
evolving market conditions have enabled us to capitalize on such opportunities while mitigating 
disruptions across our businesses. 
 
On Phenolics, this was our principal driver for the quarter's performance, achieving its highest 
ever topline and profitability. Disruptions to international supply chains, higher landed cost of 
imports and firm domestic demand created a favorable market environment. Importantly, our 
teams were able to capitalize on these conditions through proactive procurement of critical 
feedstocks, maintaining consistently high operating rates and ensuring dependable supplies to 
customers. 
 
Despite challenges in securing our basket of inputs, we sustained high throughputs across the 
Phenolics chain with several assets operating at or above their rated capacity. This reflects the 
quality of our manufacturing infrastructure, operational expertise and the advantages of being a 
large-scale domestic producer. 
 
In Advanced Intermediates, Q2 was a result of buoyant domestic demand of Q1, which, despite 
proactive procurement strategies, we were unable to fully cater to. Consumers saw elevated 
ammonia prices and other raw material prices and imported proactively, which landed up in July. 
This led to lower utilization of some plants despite the moderation in raw material prices. 
 
While this impacted Q2, the current demand scenario as well as ongoing in the upcoming 
quarters shows the value of our emphasis on an integrated ammonia to amines and propylene to 
polycarbonate strategy.  
Our short and medium-term growth prospects remain encouraging. Growth will be supported by 
an improvement in the demand across various product categories, capacity-led expansion in 
select product lines and the gradual ramp-up of recently commissioned facility. 
 
We're also continuing to diversify our product portfolio, customer base as well as geographic 
presence. This approach is intended to reduce dependence on individual products or markets, 
improve our ability to serve customers and create a more resilient earnings base.  
A key priority for us continues to be the development of integrated manufacturing platforms that 
improve raw material security, enhance cost competitiveness and enable greater value addition. 
 
This is over and above best-in-class carbon footprints as well as an overall integrated cost 
platform. The stabilization of our ammonia to amines chain, together with the expansion of our 
nitration as well as hydrogenation capabilities represents an important milestone in this journey. 
These investments strengthen supply security and provide the infrastructure required to develop 
a far broader range of downstream products. 
 
During the quarter, we continued with the ramp-up of recently commissioned assets including 
the nitric acid facility, while progressing with the commercialization as well as scale up for 
manufacturing downstream products such as MIBK, MIBC as well as the derivatives. 

 
Deepak Nitrite Limited 
 
 
October 30, 2026 
 
Page 4 of 20 
 
Moreover, towards the end of the quarter, Deepak Chemtech also commissioned its chlorination, 
which is in addition to the photohalogenation assets as well as specialty chemicals plant in Dahej 
with capital investment of approximately INR 300 crore, including associated utilities and infra. 
The commissioning strengthens the Group's manufacturing footprint and expands the specialty 
chemicals portfolio, enabling Deepak Nitrite to cater to a wider range of customer requirements 
and capture emerging growth opportunities. As the plant ramps up operations, they are expected 
to drive incremental revenues, improve capability, utilization as well as generate operational 
efficiencies. This will also lead to margin improvement as well as strengthening of the overall 
Company's performance.  
As these facilities stabilize and customer requirements translate into commercial volumes, we 
are expected to provide a greater manufacturing flexibility and support optimized cost 
efficiencies.

which is a cash proxy, has crossed INR 106 crores for the quarter. PAT is at INR 66 crores and

Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to the Q2 FY'27 Results Conference Call 
hosted by Motherson Sumi Wiring India Limited. 
As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode and there'll be an 
opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need 
assistance during this conference call, please signal an operator by pressing “*” then “0” 
on your touchtone phone. 
And I will hand the conference over to Mr. V. C. Sehgal, Chairman of the company. Thank 
you and over to you Mr. Sehgal. 
V.C. Sehgal: 
Thank you. Good evening, ladies and gentlemen and thank you for joining us today. I 
warmly welcome you to the Motherson Sumi Wiring India Limited Results Call for the 2nd 
Quarter of FY'27 and I am thankful for your continued confidence in MSWIL. 
I am pleased to announce that the company has delivered a strong performance during 
this quarter. The revenue growth is supported by higher customer volume; new program 
launches and contributions from our Greenfield plants. Our investments in new capacities 
are supporting the increased demand from our customers and while our teams remain 
focused on managing quality related headwinds and improving operations performance. 
We remain confident about the long-term prospects of the automotive industry in India 
and will continue to invest in capabilities and keep capacity in line with our customers' 
evolving requirements. 
With that I would request Vaaman to take over and take you through the performance of 
our company and also introduce the other members in the call. 
Laksh Vaaman Sehgal: 
Thank you, Papa. Good evening, everyone. 
We are pleased to report a strong performance this quarter with the revenue growing 47% 
year-on-year and 19% sequentially. EBITDA increased 34% year-on-year and 45% 
sequentially while profit after tax registered growth of 35% and 54% respectively. 
Let me take you through the key drivers of our performance: 
The passenger vehicle industry continued to witness healthy growth with volumes 
increasing 25% year-on-year and 14% sequentially. We grew ahead of the industry 
reflecting the continued trust of our customers and our ability to capture growth 
opportunities. Vehicle premiumization which is driving higher content per vehicle along 
with our participation in new model launches across both EV and ICE platforms supported 
our performance. EVs accounted for 10% of our revenue during the quarter and 9.3% for 
the first half of the year. Our three Greenfield plants also contributed meaningfully to 

 
Motherson Sumi Wiring India Limited 
Oct 30, 2026 
 
 
Page 3 of 11 
growth, enabling us to support higher customer volumes. The ramp-ups have progressed 
well with the plants now operating at an optimal utilization level. 
Moving to margins: 
EBITDA margins stood at 9.2% improving from 7.6% in Q1 through continued focus on 
operational efficiencies which led to a resilient performance while headwinds from higher 
copper prices, minimum wage revisions and other inflationary pressures remain. Copper 
prices increased by approximately 6% sequentially and 54% year-on-year. As we have 
highlighted previously, copper is a pass-through item with a typical time lag of about three 
months for recovery from majority of the customers. We are continuously engaging in 
constructive discussions with our customers to recover these increment costs. 
Now let's look at the outlook: 
Passenger vehicle demand remained strong during the quarter. However, the second half 
of the year will be compared against a higher base following the GST reduction 
implemented last year. Based on current visibility, we expect the industry to continue 
registering healthy growth. The combination of healthy industry growth, continued 
premiumization, driving higher content per new vehicle and new model launches provide 
a favorable backdrop for us. 
With that, I now have with me Pankaj sir, Anurag and Gulshan to address your questions. 
Moderator: 
Thank you very much. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. First question 
is from the line of Kapil Singh from Nomura. Please go ahead. 
Kapil Singh: 
Good evening, sir. Congratulations on a very strong performance for the quarter. My first 
question is just on the outlook for the second half. Vaaman, you mentioned that of course 
growth will be slower. But when we look at absolute terms, most of the OEMs have actually 
given a fairly strong second half growth guidance. So, in absolute terms, can we expect 
that the second half can be better than where we are in the 2nd Quarter? And are there 
some more new programs starting which could support growth in the second half ahead 
of the industry? 
Laksh Vaaman Sehgal: 
Thanks for that question. Look, third quarter is usually a strong quarter because of the 
period that has already kicked in. But it's also a precursor before that is the Shradh period. 
So, a little bit of a balancing out there. But of course, we are very hopeful. I think, of course, 
the GST cut provided a very strong boost. And we are hoping that the momentum 
continues. And like all the OEMs are saying, I think, at the same time, we were very focused 
to deliver the capacities when the growth had kind of slowed down. So, we kind of kept 
focused and made sure that we were ready for this kind of period. So, we are completely 

 
Motherson Sumi Wiring India Limited 
Oct 30, 2026 
 
 
Page 4 of 11 
ready. I think the ramp-ups, like we said, have gone really well. And we are really hopeful 
that this festive period again continues to deliver very strong revenue growth. Pankaj sir, 
Gulshan, can you add anything to that? 
Pankaj Mital: 
Vaaman sir, as you said, you are right that the momentum continues at the moment. So, 
the momentum continues. And yes, what he mentioned was that the kind of growth, which 
we saw with respect to the last year, because after the GST cut, the momentum has been 
continuing and continues. So, definitely, we do believe that there should be continuous 
growth as we move forward. But the range of growth in terms of percentages may not be 
as wide as what was with respect to last year. 
Kapil Singh: 
And so, there are more programs starting in the second half as well? 
Pankaj Mital: 
The programs have been continuously coming in. So, definitely, power makers keep 
launching new vehicles and this will be a continued process. 
Kapil Singh: 
And so, the second question was on margin. Now, what we have seen is that gross margins 
have been under pressure, and you mentioned about copper as well. Are we also on a 
quarterly basis getting the claims from the customers? And when we look at other 
operating costs, they have been fairly well controlled. So, just some color here, like what 
exactly are we doing here that other operating costs have been continuously coming down 
as a percentage of the sales? How should we look at this? Is there hope for this to keep 
coming down further? Or there are certain expenses you have controlled, and they could 
increase a bit in the second half? Thanks. 
Pankaj Mital: 
Basically, when the Greenfield sites came up, there have been costs and the revenues 
were not there. And as revenues keep coming in, then when we look at the ratios, they're 
improved. And for us as a company, our endeavor has always been to be preserved. We 
have always austerity measures in place. So, we continue to move up on that path. So, I 
am not giving you a forward-looking statement, but that's the endeavor which we have. 
And it all depends on how the markets fluctuate and what happens. But that's the 
endeavor of the company to remain optimized as a fast manufacturer of this and keep 
investing in the future growth and in the new technologies and keep investing in new 
technologies, new processes, and also digitization and automation as we move forward. 
Kapil Singh: 
And, sir, we are getting the claims on a quarterly basis as we had expected, because I am 
just trying to understand the gross margin has come off. So, are there claims pending here 
which will result in a gross margin improvement as well as we go forward, or it will happen 
more through backward integration of programs? 
V.C. Sehgal: 
I think, Kapil, there are two things. One, the corporate impact, and also the wage impact. 
So, these things are under negotiation with the customers, and you will see normally three 

 
Motherson Sumi Wiring India Limited 
Oct 30, 2026 
 
 
Page 5 of 11 
months or six months lag is there. So, within this financial year, we will report better 
numbers. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. Next question is from line of Raghunandhan NL from Nuvama Research. Please 
go ahead. 
Raghunandhan NL: 
Congratulations to the entire team, Pankaj sir, Anurag sir, Gulshan on all-round beat. 
Good to see a bit of margin at a four-quarter high. Sir, you just indicated that discussions 
are constructive with customers, and for both input and minimum wage inflation, price 
hikes are likely to be received over a period of three to six months. Just a clarification here, 
for the minimum wage inflation, would you receive the entire pass-through or a partial 
pass-through? 
V.C. Sehgal: 
It's under negotiation. I don't know what the decision is. Why should it be partial? I didn't 
understand. 
Raghunandhan NL: 
I mean, it is not indexed like copper, where 100% is generally a pass-through. So, because 
this is a negotiation, I was just trying to understand whether the customers will expect 
some part to be absorbed by the company. 
V.C. Sehgal: 
Of course, and we try to do our best to get full recovery from this. 
Raghunandhan NL: 
Okay. Noted, sir. That is good to hear. EBITDA margin is at a four-quarter high. On the raw 
material cost to revenue, it is still high at 70% of revenue, almost at an all-time high. Do 
you expect that as the pass-through happens of cost inflation, the margins will 
sequentially improve? And generally, you also work on backward integration. So, would 
that also help performance going forward? 
Anurag Gahlot: 
Obviously, as the commodity price, which is copper in our case, is on the lag of a quarter 
with a major of the customers. So, in the next quarter, we will see a recovery of that. So, 
there will be definitely an impact of that also. And localization is, yes, always on our cards 
to work towards that. And we are in the right direction to localize for the imported 
components. 
Raghunandhan NL: 
Noted, sir. Thank you for that. And in the press release, you have also highlighted of the 
ramp-up of Greenfields. Kharkhauda plant in Q1 itself had achieved high optimal 
utilization. Is it fair to assume that Gujarat plant and Pune plant have also seen better 
utilization in Q2 versus the previous quarter? If possible, can you indicate whether the 
Greenfield, all three put together, have they reached optimal levels of utilization as per 
your own targets? 

 
Motherson Sumi Wiring India Limited 
Oct 30, 2026 
 
 
Page 6 of 11 
Anurag Gahlot: 
As Vaaman sir has also said in his commentary that these three Greenfield plants have 
progressed, the ramp-up has progressed well. And now, we are operating at a very optimal 
utilization level. So, now, I can just tell you that there are no Greenfield at this moment. 
Now, they are with all the regular plants also. We are considering like that in total when we 
are doing the capacity utilization. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. Next question is from line of Joseph George from IIFL Capital. Please go ahead. 
Joseph George: 
Hi. Thank you for the opportunity. The question that I had was on the deficiency of or the 
lag in terms of the copper price pass-through. So, assuming that copper prices stabilize at 
the levels seen in 2Q, how much under-recovery is left in terms of, say, gross margins or 
the way to pay? 
V.C. Sehgal: 
The recovery, I didn't understand the question. But, see, over a period of time, it all equals 
out, whether the price is going up or going down. But, Pankaj, you can understand this 
better. 
Pankaj Mital: 
Can you clarify the question, please? 
Joseph George: 
What I meant by under-recovery is, assuming copper price has been very volatile over the 
last 4-5 quarters. And if I assume that copper price stabilizes at the levels seen in 2Q, as 
in it done increase or fall from the 2Q levels, how much more price increases are due from 
the customers, which will reflect in the upcoming quarters? 
Pankaj Mital: 
So, basically, as the team has informed that we have a lag of mostly quarter. In some 
cases, smaller cases would have been up to 6 months, but mostly, the majority is 3 
months. So, that's the lag. So, if the copper price is stabilized and on a quarter-on-quarter 
basis, it's there, but it has not stabilized, then we can't predict this now. But, to answer 
your question, and in one quarter, two quarters, three quarters, if they remain exactly the 
same, then you buy and sell at the same price. 
Moderator: 
Thank you very much. Next question is from the line of Kaustav Bubna from Kamana 
Holdings. Please go ahead. 
Kaustav Bubna: 
Thanks for taking the question. So, my question is around this whole content per vehicle 
topic. I wanted to understand, after speaking with EV automobile companies who are 
transitioning to EV in India, like for example, Mahindra and other companies, they all say 
they're shifting fully to zonal architecture. And once you shift fully to zonal architecture, 
that whole argument of content per vehicle actually is not there, because the amount of 
wiring needed is much lesser. And so, I wanted to understand how, you know, your view 
on this, where is this growth that we are showing today coming from? And how much of 
this growth is at risk because of a lot of our customers moving to zonal? If you could give 

 
Motherson Sumi Wiring India Limited 
Oct 30, 2026 
 
 
Page 7 of 11 
some color on, in-depth color on that, it'll be appreciable as it'll help understand how to 
look at growth going ahead. 
V.C. Sehgal: 
You know, you are serving the. We have been hearing this transition to electric vehicles for 
approximately, Pankaj, 20 years? 
Pankaj Mital: 
Yes, sir. And to answer this question, I mean, it's not a straightforward answer, sir, to your 
question, because this transition to zonal architecture has been there for a very long time. 
And maybe the benchmark would be, if you will look at globally also, that where the zonal 
architecture has been implemented, and then how many out of the total platforms that 
any carmaker has across. So, far, we have seen that there has been a content increase 
there have been discussions on the, because the aspirations of the people, and also the 
innovations of the carmakers to not just let it be a car, but it's more than just a mode of 
transportation that has led to content increase. So, it's not about the architecture alone, 
but it's about the innovations that the carmakers have brought in into making that product 
something more than just transportation. So, it provides a huge amount of things to a 
person who is in the car. 
Kaustav Bubna: 
Also the second question is, do you have, does the company have the full gamut of these 
high end specialized wire harnesses and cabling for cars? Because I also observed that 
some customers have to get some components for their interconnected systems from 
third parties, because Motherson doesn't have the full gamut of wiring options yet. Is that 
true? 
V.C. Sehgal: 
Sir, approximately 7 million to 8 million components and terminals, etc. are used in wiring 
harnesses. You mean to say you know of a company which does all that by itself? 
Kaustav Bubna: 
No, I am just trying to understand from you where... 
V.C. Sehgal: 
Wiring harnesses particular thing, that components, every component has a customer 
design components. So, Acura design, Suzuki design, Honda design, like that. So, it's not 
practically feasible that you are making everything yourself. We, of course, have our own 
manufacturing of wires and components. We have collaboration with Sumitomo for that. 
So, it's a very long discussion, if you want to understand that. And it's not so easy to make 
you understand the type of components in a wiring harness are phenomenal. The range is 
out of the world. So, my thing is, you make whatever you are using, the maximum, you 
make it yourself, also import from different customers. According to the sources, they are 
important. But all the components can't be changed individually. It has to be as per 
drawing. The drawing specifies which customer, specifies which component in the wiring 
harness. Because you have your own field, you have a lot of maintenance and all these 
things are required. So, you cannot make anything by yourself and just attach. 

 
Motherson Sumi Wiring India Limited 
Oct 30, 2026 
 
 
Page 8 of 11 
Moderator: 
Thank you. Next question is from the line of Shubham Bhadra from Ambit Asset 
Management. Please go ahead. 
Shubham Bhadra: 
I just wanted to understand, so if I go back to '23, '24, '25, we used to do around 35% kind 
of gross margins, which have come down to 32.5% in FY'26 and have further come down 
to 30%. Now this is likely due to copper impact. But I wanted to understand that 
hypothetically, if copper stabilizes at where it is, then what will be a normalized gross 
margin that we should think about in the coming years? 
V.C. Sehgal: 
Normally, we don't guide on the margins. We always talk about gross. 
Pankaj Mital: 
Yes. So, you see, we always work on return on capital employed. And you will see that the 
company has maintained very healthy return on capital employed despite all these 
uncertainties in the market and also the increase in commodity. You would appreciate 
that we strive to get what we evaluate what we are doing. If the commodity price goes up, 
then the best for us is to get that recovery. So, in the medium term, you would not see that 
there is a sudden sharp increase because when the customers are compensating us for 
these increases, then it's a numerator denominator effect. So, whereas the margins 
remain healthy, it's still as a percentage you may optically see that it has something like 
what you are seeing today. 
V.C. Sehgal: 
He's talking about three years ago, the margins. That time, the international wiring harness 
was also a part of this. So, maybe the answer is there somewhere, if you understand that. 
Shubham Bhadra: 
Basically, I am trying to understand that because of the numerator-denominator impact, 
how much of the… 
V.C. Sehgal: 
But I don't understand numerator and denominator. Can you please tell me how many 
years ago did you quote the figure? 
Shubham Bhadra: 
Sir, I am basically looking at FY'25 and FY'24 gross margins. 
V.C. Sehgal: 
In 24, MSWIL was there? 
Shubham Bhadra: 
'24 and '25. 
V.C. Sehgal: 
'24 MSWIL was not there. 
Pankaj Mital: 
Yes, 24 MSWIL was there. So, he's comparing MSWIL only. 
Pankaj Mital: 
So, for us, we don't provide a guidance on the margins because MSWIL we see as one 
company, it has a huge number of programs. We have hundreds of programs, multitude 

 
Motherson Sumi Wiring India Limited 
Oct 30, 2026 
 
 
Page 9 of 11 
of customers. It's a combination of everything what we see in our results. And therefore, 
directionally, the company has always been focusing on managing its tax, its capital in the 
most optimized manner. And that's where we continue to focus on the general capital. 
Shubham Bhadra: 
Got it, sir. Secondly, I wanted to understand, since now Greenfields have also ramped up 
well, what would be our current capacity utilization across the company? 
Pankaj Mital: 
So, our capacity utilization has been a stated policy in the company. The moment it hits 
around 80%, we are in an expansion mode. And you would see that as the customers keep 
growing and the customers are putting up new facilities, the company will set up and 
expand its facilities. And the company has expanded its facilities in the past two, three 
years to ensure that we are ahead of time and we are in a position to support our 
customers' growth. And we never second-guess their growth. And that's the reason why 
we have been able to support our customers. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. Next question is from the line of Ankur Poddar from Swan Investments. Please 
go ahead. 
Ankur Poddar: 
Hi, sir. Congrats on a very strong set of performance for the quarter. So, most of my 
questions have been answered. Just one clarification is on the Greenfield itself. So, you 
mentioned that they have reached optimum level of utilization and now we should look at 
it at a consolidated level with our base business also. So, is it fair to assume that the 
margins for the Greenfields have also reached our company-level margins? 
Anurag Gahlot: 
See, we don't talk about the margins at the plant-wise level or for the Greenfield 
specifically. What you are seeing, the total margin, is for the overall performance of 
MSWIL. 
Ankur Poddar: 
And just a follow-up on the previous participant's question on the CAPEX that we are 
looking forward for this year and going forward. Can you give us some guidance there? 
Gulshan Pahuja: 
For this year, we have already laid out the guidance that largely in line with what we had in 
the previous year of Rs. 200 crores approximately. 
Ankur Poddar: 
And for FY'28? 
Gulshan Pahuja: 
 FY28, it all depends on because we are supplying to our customers. So, right now, the 
schedules have not finalized where we are setting in. So, in terms of giving you the 
indication in terms of the capitalization at this moment for FY'28 would be very difficult. 
But as we said in the beginning or so far that obviously the growth is there and we are 
looking at the capacities expansion and all. So, that will be there. But in terms of 

 
Motherson Sumi Wiring India Limited 
Oct 30, 2026 
 
 
Page 10 of 11 
quantifying it, how much it would be, that clarity would come in the upcoming time when 
it would be laying down. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. Next question is from the line of Andrey Purushottam from Cogito Advisors. 
Please go ahead. 
Andrey Purushottam: 
I had just one clarification and one question. The clarification was that are we saying that 
EBITDA has lagged revenue growth. It is primarily due to raw materials, copper prices and 
wage growth? 
Gulshan Pahuja: 
Sir, can you clarify the question again in terms of how you are looking at the EBITDA with 
the revenue growth, just for my understanding so that I would be able to answer. 
Andrey Purushottam: 
Well, if you just look at your own figures, your revenue growth has been higher than your 
EBITDA growth. So, in a sense, you have not been able to take advantage of operating 
leverage and there may be two very good reasons for it, which so far in this discussion 
seem to be the lag in the pass-through of copper and other raw materials and the other is 
the wage growth that has been imposed due to regulation. Are these the two major factors 
that have contributed to this or am I missing anything else? 
Gulshan Pahuja: 
So, I understood your question now. So, the point is, if you just look at the revenue growth, 
the revenue growth is 47% in which the copper growth contains 12%. If you just take out 
the copper inflation, as you are aware that we do not charge anything on the copper, it is 
completely a pass-through. So, if you just take out the revenue growth is 35% and our 
EBITDA is around, growth in EBITDA is 34%. So, practically on the similar lines where we 
are and minimum wage impact are still there in this quarter, but due to continuous work 
on our cost optimizations, cost of austerity measures and all, we try to control our cost as 
much as possible so that we would be able to have the better operating leverage in the 
results, that is you are looking at it. 
Andrey Purushottam: 
Right. And just one question, across industry, actually, because of the sharp volatility in 
raw material prices, there have been moves to, you know, cut down the lag from three 
months to one month. Is this happening with you guys also? And is there any chance that 
the OEMs will agree to a shorter lag period in ensuing quarters of months? 
Pankaj Mital: 
These are something, if something happens on that account, we will keep you informed. 
So, far, there has been a lag period. Of course, there have been discussions, as you 
mentioned, and once anything happens, then, you know, it's as Mr. Sehgal mentioned, 
that a lot of topics are macro-operational solutions which happen with the technology. 
And we work as partners along with our customers to find solutions to the issues which 
are facing the industry and to find any given solutions at the end of the day. 

 
Motherson Sumi Wiring India Limited 
Oct 30, 2026 
 
 
Page 11 of 11 
Moderator: 
Thank you very much. As there are no further questions, I now hand the conference over 
to Mr. V. C. Sehgal for closing comments. 
V. C. Sehgal: 
Thank you. Thank you all very much to make sense of what we have achieved. We are all 
very excited. We believe these particular questions have been answered over time and yet 
to come. So, we try our best to make you remember the history. Thank you all very much. 
Have a great weekend. Bye-bye. 
Moderator: 
Thank you very much. On behalf of Motherson Sumi Wiring India Limited, that concludes 
this conference. Thank you all for joining us and you may now disconnect your lines. Thank 
you.
