“Pine Labs Limited 
Q2 FY2027 Earnings Call” 
 
October 29, 2026 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Management: 
Mr. Amrish Rau – Chief Executive Officer – Pine Labs 
Limited 
Mr. Sameer Kamath – Group Chief Financial Officer – Pine 
Labs Limited 

 
 
Moderator: 
Hello everyone. Welcome to the Pine Labs Limited Q2 FY2027 earnings call. Please 
note all participants will be in the listen only mode and this call is being recorded. 
Joining us from the Pine Labs management team are Mr. Amrish Rau, CEO, and Mr. 
Sameer Kamath, Group CFO. We will begin the call with opening remarks from Mr. 
Amrish Rau followed by a Q&A session. Before we begin, please know that some of 
the statements made during this discussion may be forward looking in nature. 
Actual results may vary significantly due to various external factors. The Zoom 
conference call is intended solely for investors and analysts. So, if you are joining 
from a media organization, we request you to please disconnect. Please reach out 
to the company's investor relations team for any questions. With that, I now hand 
over the call to Mr. Rau. Over to you, Sir. 
Amrish Rau: 
Thank you very much. Welcome everyone to our earnings call. I wanted to give a 
very quick overview of what is happening in the market. How are we looking at the 
business? How did we feel we performed in Q2 and then we will go into the Q&A 
section of it? I thought in Q2 there was good execution across Pine Labs. Every one 
of our lines of businesses continued to deliver very well and we were able to drive 
the growth that we were targeting for. So as  you know, we came in at about 24% 
growth on the revenue side and as far as EBITDA is concerned, adjusted EBITDA is 
concerned, we came in at about 27% growth on a year-on-year basis, so across 
the company, good execution. I think what was most interesting for me across the 
company, may that be in the offline side of the business, the issuing side of the 
business, and online. each of these segments, we actually grew faster than the 
market. We gained market share in all the various businesses that we have been 
operating in. I would like to give you a little bit of a breakdown in each of the 
business and what is happening in each of the businesses. On the offline side of 
the business, on the enterprise accounts, we continue to hold on to 100% of our 
businesses out there. Our net revenue retention is extremely strong on the 
enterprise side of the business and every one of our logos and brands are intact. 
What I would say is we have gone ahead and added very strong brands. One of the 

 
 
great examples is Tanishq where we did not have any presence in Tanishq for a 
long period of time and through this Q2 we are now deployed all across all the 
stores of Tanishq. We have also continued to increase market share with another 
large retailer where they are clearly seeing the value of what Pine Labs is delivering, 
so on the enterprise segment we have a moat and we have been able to protect 
our base out there, but what is interesting is on the mid market segment and when 
it comes to mid market these are apparel brands, these are coffee shops, the 
restaurants, duty frees, and airports. In those segments, we have continued to gain 
market share and there we have actually seen that on a trailing 12 month basis, we 
have almost deployed close to about 100,000 terminals in the mid market segment. 
So in the mid market segment, we are picking up new logos. 
 
Why is that happening? It is coming down to a few simple points. Even on the mid 
market side, the merchant requirements are getting complex. They want us to be 
fully integrated either into their ERP or into their invoicing system and billing 
systems. Those complex technology changes required out there, Pine Labs is the 
only one who have been investing into it, and merchants are seeing a 
differentiation and wanting to work with us. So that is the reason why we have been 
able to win there. The second part is we have also started to do a lot of value added 
services, which is bringing in footfall into these mid-market merchants and these 
mid-market merchants are appreciating the fact that we are in partnerships which 
can potentially bring in consumers into their stores So they are partnering with us. 
We, in turn, are making a small take on flow-based income in those mid market 
segments also. So because of our distribution in enterprise and in the mid market 
segment, we have also been able to drive the flow based income in Pine Labs. 
 
Coming to the flow based income, the flow based income in Pine Labs actually 
grew by about 25% on a year-on-year basis. The volumes grew in a little higher, 
came in at about 50% because we have actually again gained market share on 
the UPI side and that is the reason why the volumes are almost at 50%. But the flow 
based income grew by 25% on a year-on-year basis. We have added new revenue 

 
 
streams in our flow based income. I mean, the good news is a lot of people are 
asking us about installment payment services, which is obviously more than what 
people used to ask us about POS, but our flow based income is now coming up with 
more revenue streams associated with data related services, marketing related 
services, distribution of marketing related products. All of those have gone into our 
flow based income and that has been a healthy rise on a year-on-year basis. On 
the issuing side of the business, we have again grown significantly on both on the 
processing side, but also on the distribution of prepaid cards and gift cards. On the 
distribution of prepaid cards and gift cards, again, we have grown faster than the 
market. We have gained market share on the distribution front. On the processing 
side, as you know, we already have about 80% to 85% of the market. This growth 
has come on the backs of new products, which we have taken in the market. Just 
to highlight two products out there. One, we have actually brought in some gaming 
related brands on our distribution when it comes to prepaid cards and gift cards. 
The mass transit program associated with NCMC, which is called Bharat Yatra, for 
example, we now distributed somewhere close to 25,000 to 30,000 cards on a 
monthly basis on the Bharat Yatra prepaid card, which is being used for daily 
transit. Now we are effectively distributing almost 1000 NCMC cards on a daily basis. 
These are cards which are distributed largely through Blinkit and Zepto being the 
channel for that. 
 
What I am most excited about on the issuing side of the business, we are seeing 
more new use cases come up on the issuing side of the business and we will be 
launching them in the month of November. I think I have talked about it before. I 
wanted to share with it again. By the end of November, we will have an employee 
tax benefit card out in the market that effectively will allow us to go back to the 
corporates that we have any which way been working with and give them a 
solution which will be around the employee tax benefit area. That should be coming 
up towards end of November, early December. 

 
 
 
Just talking a little bit more in terms of the online and bill payments business side. 
On the online side of the business, we have now the top four Q-commerce 
companies using our payment gateway for daily transactions. We are also 
providing installment payment services on our online platform for these Q-
commerce businesses, especially when it comes to electronics, mobile phones, 
and any consumer durables, which they could be selling. During Flipkart's Big Billion 
Days, we were one of the payment gateways that they had enabled for. What that 
is showing me is that we are actually making progress with the products where the 
largest and the biggest retailers are continuing to use Pine Labs in the online world 
also. I also wanted to very quickly share with you that one of the largest billers, 
consumer billers in the country has signed up with Pine Labs. It will go live in Q3. So 
we are again winning new deals on the bill payment side also. 
 
Very quickly, touching upon the international markets, some of you have asked us 
what we have been doing with UAE and Dubai, and I have told you that we have 
partnered with Emirates NBD, and with Wio Bank, where we are providing the entire 
technology services, both for offline payments and online payments to both these 
banks. Just to highlight how big those businesses have become, in UAE, we are now 
starting to process 1 lakh transactions a day. That is the size and scale that we are 
operating in the UAE market. I also want to tell you, we are now getting close to 1 
lakh POS deployed in the Malaysian market and in Philippines, now we have 50,000 
POS machines, which is completely running off Pine Labs platform. So unlike what 
people believe that international is a small bit of Pine Labs, we are not just in those 
markets, but we are actually winning in those markets. As I just told you, these are 
numbers of scale where we are operating in. We are now present in about 22 
countries and we are continuing to have very good wins in many of those markets 
out there. 
 
Finally, I just wanted to very quickly touch upon what is my outlook for H2. We have 
had a very good H1. We have been able to prove the fact that there is enough 
opportunity in the market. We are seeing more opportunity come along in the 

 
 
market, especially when it comes to offline, online, bill payment services, and in the 
issuing area. So we want to continue to invest on the sales side. Over H1, we have 
invested heavily when it comes to sales people. We are also deploying more sales 
people in the international markets because of these wins that we have created in 
the international market. So quite happy with what we have delivered in H1, and we 
are going to continue to invest so that we can continue to increase our revenues in 
H2 also. Some of the things to look forward to are in the second half of this year we 
should be able to scale our gaming distribution when it comes to gift cards. The 
employee tax benefit card is something to talk about. The data related services 
marketing and advertising related revenues will continue to increase. Affordability 
market is something that we are absolutely focused on in expansion. You will see a 
lot more of that in Q3 when we are going much more beyond electronic segment 
and then the final piece is the entire emerging opportunity around UPI. We gave a 
little bit of numbers when it comes to our UPI transactions in the earnings report 
that we sent out with. I have nothing more to add in terms of when UPI MDR will go 
live. Ball is completely in NPCI's court. So that is more or less in terms of what is 
happening in the market. Happy to take any questions. Operator, you can take any 
questions. 
Moderator: 
Thank you, Sir. Ladies and gentlemen, we will now begin the question and answer 
session. Anyone who has a question may click on the raise hand button from the 
bottom toolbar. The operator will announce your turn in the queue. Ladies and 
gentlemen, we will wait for a moment for the question queue to assemble. We will 
take the first question from Vijit Jain of Citi. Please go ahead. Mr. Vijit Jain. 
Vijit Jain: 
Great thank you. So my first question is in good to see the growth in India in the 
issuing and acquiring platform business sustaining Q2. India business, even that I 
see is up 40% Y-o-Y. I know this is a quarter with no big billion day sales and most 
of the sales event would have happened in 3Q. So I am just wondering despite that 
base if this- grew 40% would this likely grow even faster in 3Q because all the festive 

 
 
season is kind of sandwiched into 3Q this year? That is my first question and I will 
just come back with it. 
Sameer Kamath: 
Amrish, I will take that that first. 
Amrish Rau: 
Sure go ahead, go ahead. 
Sameer Kamath: 
So thanks, Vijit. I think, look, our prepaid business has multiple use cases, and it is 
not only that cyclical to a festive season or otherwise and if you see our core 
business continues to do well with some of our large players who have kind of 
renewed their contracts with us, etc. So there is a core base which is there and new 
use cases coming in. We found a lot of new use cases, as Amrish was also saying, 
across multiple lines, apart from just the core use case we found with some of the 
e-commerce companies. Like, for example, refund wallet is a very large use case, 
which has significant traction across the existing clients and new clients which 
have come in. Gaming is a new platform which has given us better take rates as 
well. So I think a lot of our use cases that we have been talking about and over the 
period building out have started seeing traction across counters and that is why 
you are seeing some of these growth rates come in. Nothing specific to our season 
per se in these things and I think that is something we are trying to build going 
forward as well. 
Amrish Rau: 
I will just add a little bit more on to that one Vijit is that the October month is almost 
gone. In that period, we have actually gone through Navratri and Dussehra. Navratri 
and Dussehra were extremely strong. So as far as the Navratri and Dussehra period 
was concerned, I have nothing to worry about in terms of what has happened in 
those days. However, when it comes to Diwali, I think we will know in the next two 
weeks. We obviously have deployed our people on the field. They are in various 
stores, but we will have a better picture on that in about two weeks’ time. 
Vijit Jain: 
Correct and Amrish, just following up on that thing within your affordability 
business. Now that you have October behind you and we know that consumer 

 
 
electronics prices have been going up pretty sharply this year. That generally 
brings to mind the question of whether EMI on cards will see higher penetration this 
time around. Are you seeing that in October and how do you think about that 
particular business? Whatever color you can give on affordability business in 
festive season so far would be super helpful? 
Amrish Rau: 
Vijit, I am just going to keep the festive season only up to the Dussehra is what I am 
going to say and I am saying as far as Dussehra is concerned, it has been a good 
start to the quarter. Again, I am not ready to say much about Diwali because I think 
it also depends heavily in terms of what banks are going to be doing and also how 
the mood comes through in the Diwali period. 
Vijit Jain: 
Got it, thank you. Understand that. My next question is on UPI. Thanks for the 
disclosure in the letter on the eligible GTV for 2027 and 2028 as well. I guess my 
question is the 2028 number is a good 60% Y-o-Y again over FY2027 and I am just 
trying to understand what are the key drivers of that. If I look at your devices, net 
device addition number, and I know that you have an aggressive plan of 1 million 
device adds as well. So I mean, are you looking at your device count aspirations 
and then projecting that Rs.32,000 Crores to Rs.33,000 Crores or is it something 
else? Whatever you can tell me would be super helpful. 
Amrish Rau: 
First, let me just tell you what is happening in the market, right? What is happening 
in the market is if you are into organized retail, the retailer wants to have 
reconciliation, which is completely automated now, including when it comes to a 
UPI based transaction. Nobody is turning around and saying that I will keep UPI as 
a separate independent device or a sticker outside. So now, I said that in the last 
quarter also. 75% to 77% of the transactions on our POS machine is now a UPI 
transaction. Only 25% is a card based transaction. Now, those 75% transactions 
have grown at about 68% for compounding for the last two years and all which we 
have done is we have said that we think there is another 70% kind of a year which 
is coming up. In other words, what I am trying to say is that organized retailer is also 

 
 
moving to a device-based UPI. We as a company who have not really tried to do a 
bit more in terms of having some soundboxes or having some screen based boxes 
at the merchant location. If we make in a little effort, I do not think so we should be 
short by 70% growth in the next year and at least for one more year. So I think we 
will be able to capture and that is one of the things, which led me to turn around 
and say that we will be deploying at least 10 lakh more soundboxes in the market. 
Vijit Jain: 
Understood, Amrish. Super helpful that and one last bit within that. Since these are 
merchants, these are large enterprise merchants, right? So for you to pass on the 
40 bps MDR to them, is that going to be an automatic process or do you have to go 
to the merchants one by one with your bank partners to kind of work this way out? 
Amrish Rau: 
So just to clarify, from a technical standpoint, we do not need to do anything more. 
From a commercial standpoint, I absolutely do believe when it comes to the largest 
of large merchants that we have with us, there will be a commercial conversation 
to be had for sure. 
Sameer Kamath: 
But Vijit, let me also add that we are seeing two levels of growth, transacting POS 
going up and also the value for transacting POS going up and a large part of our 
base also now comes from the mid market segment where they are going at 40% 
and we are all on the transaction rails there. So a large part of our volumes also 
now comes from the mid market and not just the large segment. So it is a well 
diversified pool of UPI-generating volumes. 
Vijit Jain: 
Understood. Super helpful. Thank you. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. Our next question is from Pranav Kshatriya of Emkay Global. Please go 
ahead. 
Pranav Kshatriya: 
Thanks for the opportunity. I just want to dwell a little bit on the UPI MDR, what you 
commented. I mean thank you for the numbers what you have given. But of course 
of the 65% odd of the transaction value, which are about 2000, there will be certain 

 
 
categories which will be excluded from the MDR or will have a very low MDR of Rs.5 
cap? So what would be the addressable GMV and what we should look at as a take 
rate on that just to get a sense on how this will pan out financially? 
Amrish Rau: 
Pranav, there is a reason why we put it out in the way we have put it out and that is 
because I do think that it is going to take a little longer to do that calculation, which 
says what will be the net take rate across our entire UPI base. So what we felt was 
everybody has heard the 40 basis points which are going to come out. I think it is 
fairly clear that to the acquirer going to be anywhere about 11 basis points. So we 
wanted to just give you the volumes associated with it, what comes through on 
some commercial negotiations, what comes through in terms of breakup between 
some of the changes which could potentially come-up in terms of MCC based 
pricing. We did not want to hazard a guess on that. 
Pranav Kshatriya: 
No worries. Thank you. I will move on to the next question. I want to understand, it is 
good to see 25% plus kind of a growth on transaction-based revenue. And that I 
am just trying to understand what exactly is driving that growth, because 
affordability, I would assume that is the largest part of that. But this time, the festive 
season falls in Q3. Also, the electronics prices have been higher and that is why 
some of the media reports says that the GMV on the electronics has been down for 
the big billion so which I assume that will sort of impact Pine Labs affordability 
business also to some extent at least. So what exactly are the drivers if you can 
highlight let us say top two, three product or even if affordability is not impacted 
that also would be useful. 
Amrish Rau: 
Pranav, to be honest, we have been very clear in explaining this for a long period of 
time. So under the flow-based income, anything that we earn as far as DCC, which 
is the dynamic currency conversion kind of payment transaction, that goes in there. 
Anything that we earn as an aggregator-based revenues, which is transaction-
based, 10 basis points, 15 basis points, 20 basis points, on our regular payment 
transaction, we put it into the flow-based services. Anywhere where we actually 

 
 
provide access to consumer internet companies, so that they can close a 
transaction at a merchant location. Whatever the fees that we earn associated to 
that transaction, we again go and book it into this line item. So that is third. Fourth, 
we have a lot of data-related, marketing-related, advertisement-related services 
in our portfolio. Now those revenues also go and sit in that same bucket here under 
flow-based. And then finally comes on the affordability side. As far as we are 
concerned, we are actually trying to grow all of these services. And some of these 
other services have continued to now become, I would not say significant, I will say 
become chunkier part of our overall revenues when it comes to flow-based 
income. And effectively, that has driven the 25% growth on a year-on-year basis. 
So I do want you all to think about this business to be much more broader than just 
a one-trick pony around affordability. 
Pranav Kshatriya: 
Thank you for that explanation, but I assume that affordability was not at all 
impacted by seasonality or anything like that, or basically the electronic prices.  
Sameer Kamath: 
Pranav, to be very candid, look, whatever macro factors are there, macro factors 
that we have to stay. But adjusted for two, three things you have to keep in mind. 
You have to keep in mind also that festive season was actually driven, it was started 
early, late September, there was a GST cut, etc. If you were to adjust for those one-
offs which are reasoned because of these movements of the festive period, we 
would have seen more or less reasonable numbers. I think across segments, two, 
three things you have to keep in mind for us, affordability has been predominantly 
in the past CDIT, but you have seen volumes across non-CDIT also grow in. So, I 
think non-CDIT plus some of the other initiatives have helped us build an overall 
portfolio of affordability and any short-term shock that you see in any of these 
segments, we are kind of getting compensated by all of these other segments. 
Pranav Kshatriya: 
Fantastic. My next question is around the capex and some of the indirect costs. So 
capex has gone up quite significantly to 240 odd Crores rupees in H1. How should 

 
 
we see this in the context of higher chip prices driving the higher devices, as well as 
your aspiration to deploy a lot more soundboxes? 
Sameer Kamath: 
Pranav, I will take that question. So if you remember in Q4, we said that there was 
this global crisis which resulted into delayed procurements and some orders 
slipping up. So almost about Rs.35-40 Crores of capex actually slipped from Q4 to 
Q1 because of these chip problems, etc. So what you see in this year is an overflow 
of last year, number one about Rs.35 Crores, plus you also are now having to pay 
almost 80% advance to lock-in prices given that chip shortages are there, the 
vendors earlier worked on 20% advance, they want higher advances. So almost 
about Rs.20-25 Crores of advance for which procurements are still to happen, are 
sitting in the capex which you have seen. So I think adjusted for that, we are pretty 
much in the range, factored for two things. In the mid-market space, we are 
growing at about 39-40%. Some part of it is capex, some part of it is obviously 
device sold, plus we are also seeing a lot of soundboxes that we are going to deploy 
given the UPI opportunity. So there will be some procurement there. I think adjusted 
for these, there will be a normalized increase in the business given the opportunity 
we see. Otherwise, I think you will see more or less steady state numbers across the 
two years. 
Pranav Kshatriya: 
Thank you for that. Last question from my side. On indirect costs, some jump, you 
talked about investment in marketing and hiring more marketing professional, 
especially in the overseas geographies. How should we think about this? Is Rs.425 
odd Crores or Rs.426 Crores indirect cost is a new normal or it can further increase 
because it was very steady till Q4 FY 2026 and then Q1 was a jump then Q2 again is 
a sharp jump so should we expect this run rate to continue going forward. 
Amrish Rau: 
Sameer, you want to take that. 
Sameer Kamath: 
Pranav, two things are there. I think cloud and data cost is a real cost and I think we 
have always guided that when you look at indirect expenses, look at expenses 
which are linked to top line and which are variable. And cloud and data cost which 

 
 
you see has always been trending in that 8.5% to 9% including the cloud 
infrastructure. I think we have put a lot of initiatives in place to optimize this, to 
modernize it because we are now leveraging AI and the resultant of that 
tokenization cost is the real cost. So that cost will remain variable to about 8% or 9% 
of top line. The other cost within which the indirect cost sits is the outsourced 
employees which are required for ground level execution across multiple initiatives, 
including, for example, we have won large OMC contracts, we want to penetrate 
into the non-CDIT segment, some of the initiatives about investing the sales people 
off-roll and on-roll come within the indirect cost as well. So I think those kind of 
expenses are variabilized, but are revenue accretive costs and that is where they 
will be there. Secondly, one item at a callout which is again a quarter by quarter 
callout, we are a large sponsor of GFF. GFF happened in Q3 last year, GFF happened 
in Q2 this year, so that is a cost which is switched between quarters but I think given 
the size of the event and the showcasing that we can do for products, I think that is 
an important spend for us to kind of showcase our capability and based on those 
capabilities we are able to monetize a lot of those opportunities. So I think one has 
to keep that calibrated and look from a long-term perspective. I think we are 
judicious about our costs. All of these costs are going towards either a new 
geography or a new opportunity or ground level presence to kind of build the rails 
for monetizing for the flow-based businesses. 
Pranav Kshatriya: 
Thank you for your answer. Wish you all the very best. 
Amrish Rau: 
Thank you. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. Our next question is from Nitin Aggarwal of Motilal Oswal. Please go 
ahead. 
Nitin Aggarwal: 
Thanks for the opportunity and congrats Amrish and Sameer on the results. I have 
a couple of questions. One is on the international business revenues. The mix was 
gradually inching up slightly every quarter. This quarter there is a slight dip. And if I 
look at Q-on-Q, this implies just 2%-3% Q-on-Q growth. So how do we look at that? 

 
 
Sameer Kamath:

“Pine Labs Limited 
Q2 FY2027 Earnings Call” 
 
October 29, 2026 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Management: 
Mr. Amrish Rau – Chief Executive Officer – Pine Labs 
Limited 
Mr. Sameer Kamath – Group Chief Financial Officer – Pine 
Labs Limited 

 
 
Moderator: 
Hello everyone. Welcome to the Pine Labs Limited Q2 FY2027 earnings call. Please 
note all participants will be in the listen only mode and this call is being recorded. 
Joining us from the Pine Labs management team are Mr. Amrish Rau, CEO, and Mr. 
Sameer Kamath, Group CFO. We will begin the call with opening remarks from Mr. 
Amrish Rau followed by a Q&A session. Before we begin, please know that some of 
the statements made during this discussion may be forward looking in nature. 
Actual results may vary significantly due to various external factors. The Zoom 
conference call is intended solely for investors and analysts. So, if you are joining 
from a media organization, we request you to please disconnect. Please reach out 
to the company's investor relations team for any questions. With that, I now hand 
over the call to Mr. Rau. Over to you, Sir. 
Amrish Rau: 
Thank you very much. Welcome everyone to our earnings call. I wanted to give a 
very quick overview of what is happening in the market. How are we looking at the 
business? How did we feel we performed in Q2 and then we will go into the Q&A 
section of it? I thought in Q2 there was good execution across Pine Labs. Every one 
of our lines of businesses continued to deliver very well and we were able to drive 
the growth that we were targeting for. So as  you know, we came in at about 24% 
growth on the revenue side and as far as EBITDA is concerned, adjusted EBITDA is 
concerned, we came in at about 27% growth on a year-on-year basis, so across 
the company, good execution. I think what was most interesting for me across the 
company, may that be in the offline side of the business, the issuing side of the 
business, and online. each of these segments, we actually grew faster than the 
market. We gained market share in all the various businesses that we have been 
operating in. I would like to give you a little bit of a breakdown in each of the 
business and what is happening in each of the businesses. On the offline side of 
the business, on the enterprise accounts, we continue to hold on to 100% of our 
businesses out there. Our net revenue retention is extremely strong on the 
enterprise side of the business and every one of our logos and brands are intact. 
What I would say is we have gone ahead and added very strong brands. One of the 

 
 
great examples is Tanishq where we did not have any presence in Tanishq for a 
long period of time and through this Q2 we are now deployed all across all the 
stores of Tanishq. We have also continued to increase market share with another 
large retailer where they are clearly seeing the value of what Pine Labs is delivering, 
so on the enterprise segment we have a moat and we have been able to protect 
our base out there, but what is interesting is on the mid market segment and when 
it comes to mid market these are apparel brands, these are coffee shops, the 
restaurants, duty frees, and airports. In those segments, we have continued to gain 
market share and there we have actually seen that on a trailing 12 month basis, we 
have almost deployed close to about 100,000 terminals in the mid market segment. 
So in the mid market segment, we are picking up new logos. 
 
Why is that happening? It is coming down to a few simple points. Even on the mid 
market side, the merchant requirements are getting complex. They want us to be 
fully integrated either into their ERP or into their invoicing system and billing 
systems. Those complex technology changes required out there, Pine Labs is the 
only one who have been investing into it, and merchants are seeing a 
differentiation and wanting to work with us. So that is the reason why we have been 
able to win there. The second part is we have also started to do a lot of value added 
services, which is bringing in footfall into these mid-market merchants and these 
mid-market merchants are appreciating the fact that we are in partnerships which 
can potentially bring in consumers into their stores So they are partnering with us. 
We, in turn, are making a small take on flow-based income in those mid market 
segments also. So because of our distribution in enterprise and in the mid market 
segment, we have also been able to drive the flow based income in Pine Labs. 
 
Coming to the flow based income, the flow based income in Pine Labs actually 
grew by about 25% on a year-on-year basis. The volumes grew in a little higher, 
came in at about 50% because we have actually again gained market share on 
the UPI side and that is the reason why the volumes are almost at 50%. But the flow 
based income grew by 25% on a year-on-year basis. We have added new revenue 

 
 
streams in our flow based income. I mean, the good news is a lot of people are 
asking us about installment payment services, which is obviously more than what 
people used to ask us about POS, but our flow based income is now coming up with 
more revenue streams associated with data related services, marketing related 
services, distribution of marketing related products. All of those have gone into our 
flow based income and that has been a healthy rise on a year-on-year basis. On 
the issuing side of the business, we have again grown significantly on both on the 
processing side, but also on the distribution of prepaid cards and gift cards. On the 
distribution of prepaid cards and gift cards, again, we have grown faster than the 
market. We have gained market share on the distribution front. On the processing 
side, as you know, we already have about 80% to 85% of the market. This growth 
has come on the backs of new products, which we have taken in the market. Just 
to highlight two products out there. One, we have actually brought in some gaming 
related brands on our distribution when it comes to prepaid cards and gift cards. 
The mass transit program associated with NCMC, which is called Bharat Yatra, for 
example, we now distributed somewhere close to 25,000 to 30,000 cards on a 
monthly basis on the Bharat Yatra prepaid card, which is being used for daily 
transit. Now we are effectively distributing almost 1000 NCMC cards on a daily basis. 
These are cards which are distributed largely through Blinkit and Zepto being the 
channel for that. 
 
What I am most excited about on the issuing side of the business, we are seeing 
more new use cases come up on the issuing side of the business and we will be 
launching them in the month of November. I think I have talked about it before. I 
wanted to share with it again. By the end of November, we will have an employee 
tax benefit card out in the market that effectively will allow us to go back to the 
corporates that we have any which way been working with and give them a 
solution which will be around the employee tax benefit area. That should be coming 
up towards end of November, early December. 

 
 
 
Just talking a little bit more in terms of the online and bill payments business side. 
On the online side of the business, we have now the top four Q-commerce 
companies using our payment gateway for daily transactions. We are also 
providing installment payment services on our online platform for these Q-
commerce businesses, especially when it comes to electronics, mobile phones, 
and any consumer durables, which they could be selling. During Flipkart's Big Billion 
Days, we were one of the payment gateways that they had enabled for. What that 
is showing me is that we are actually making progress with the products where the 
largest and the biggest retailers are continuing to use Pine Labs in the online world 
also. I also wanted to very quickly share with you that one of the largest billers, 
consumer billers in the country has signed up with Pine Labs. It will go live in Q3. So 
we are again winning new deals on the bill payment side also. 
 
Very quickly, touching upon the international markets, some of you have asked us 
what we have been doing with UAE and Dubai, and I have told you that we have 
partnered with Emirates NBD, and with Wio Bank, where we are providing the entire 
technology services, both for offline payments and online payments to both these 
banks. Just to highlight how big those businesses have become, in UAE, we are now 
starting to process 1 lakh transactions a day. That is the size and scale that we are 
operating in the UAE market. I also want to tell you, we are now getting close to 1 
lakh POS deployed in the Malaysian market and in Philippines, now we have 50,000 
POS machines, which is completely running off Pine Labs platform. So unlike what 
people believe that international is a small bit of Pine Labs, we are not just in those 
markets, but we are actually winning in those markets. As I just told you, these are 
numbers of scale where we are operating in. We are now present in about 22 
countries and we are continuing to have very good wins in many of those markets 
out there. 
 
Finally, I just wanted to very quickly touch upon what is my outlook for H2. We have 
had a very good H1. We have been able to prove the fact that there is enough 
opportunity in the market. We are seeing more opportunity come along in the 

 
 
market, especially when it comes to offline, online, bill payment services, and in the 
issuing area. So we want to continue to invest on the sales side. Over H1, we have 
invested heavily when it comes to sales people. We are also deploying more sales 
people in the international markets because of these wins that we have created in 
the international market. So quite happy with what we have delivered in H1, and we 
are going to continue to invest so that we can continue to increase our revenues in 
H2 also. Some of the things to look forward to are in the second half of this year we 
should be able to scale our gaming distribution when it comes to gift cards. The 
employee tax benefit card is something to talk about. The data related services 
marketing and advertising related revenues will continue to increase. Affordability 
market is something that we are absolutely focused on in expansion. You will see a 
lot more of that in Q3 when we are going much more beyond electronic segment 
and then the final piece is the entire emerging opportunity around UPI. We gave a 
little bit of numbers when it comes to our UPI transactions in the earnings report 
that we sent out with. I have nothing more to add in terms of when UPI MDR will go 
live. Ball is completely in NPCI's court. So that is more or less in terms of what is 
happening in the market. Happy to take any questions. Operator, you can take any 
questions. 
Moderator: 
Thank you, Sir. Ladies and gentlemen, we will now begin the question and answer 
session. Anyone who has a question may click on the raise hand button from the 
bottom toolbar. The operator will announce your turn in the queue. Ladies and 
gentlemen, we will wait for a moment for the question queue to assemble. We will 
take the first question from Vijit Jain of Citi. Please go ahead. Mr. Vijit Jain. 
Vijit Jain: 
Great thank you. So my first question is in good to see the growth in India in the 
issuing and acquiring platform business sustaining Q2. India business, even that I 
see is up 40% Y-o-Y. I know this is a quarter with no big billion day sales and most 
of the sales event would have happened in 3Q. So I am just wondering despite that 
base if this- grew 40% would this likely grow even faster in 3Q because all the festive 

 
 
season is kind of sandwiched into 3Q this year? That is my first question and I will 
just come back with it. 
Sameer Kamath: 
Amrish, I will take that that first. 
Amrish Rau: 
Sure go ahead, go ahead. 
Sameer Kamath: 
So thanks, Vijit. I think, look, our prepaid business has multiple use cases, and it is 
not only that cyclical to a festive season or otherwise and if you see our core 
business continues to do well with some of our large players who have kind of 
renewed their contracts with us, etc. So there is a core base which is there and new 
use cases coming in. We found a lot of new use cases, as Amrish was also saying, 
across multiple lines, apart from just the core use case we found with some of the 
e-commerce companies. Like, for example, refund wallet is a very large use case, 
which has significant traction across the existing clients and new clients which 
have come in. Gaming is a new platform which has given us better take rates as 
well. So I think a lot of our use cases that we have been talking about and over the 
period building out have started seeing traction across counters and that is why 
you are seeing some of these growth rates come in. Nothing specific to our season 
per se in these things and I think that is something we are trying to build going 
forward as well. 
Amrish Rau: 
I will just add a little bit more on to that one Vijit is that the October month is almost 
gone. In that period, we have actually gone through Navratri and Dussehra. Navratri 
and Dussehra were extremely strong. So as far as the Navratri and Dussehra period 
was concerned, I have nothing to worry about in terms of what has happened in 
those days. However, when it comes to Diwali, I think we will know in the next two 
weeks. We obviously have deployed our people on the field. They are in various 
stores, but we will have a better picture on that in about two weeks’ time. 
Vijit Jain: 
Correct and Amrish, just following up on that thing within your affordability 
business. Now that you have October behind you and we know that consumer 

 
 
electronics prices have been going up pretty sharply this year. That generally 
brings to mind the question of whether EMI on cards will see higher penetration this 
time around. Are you seeing that in October and how do you think about that 
particular business? Whatever color you can give on affordability business in 
festive season so far would be super helpful? 
Amrish Rau: 
Vijit, I am just going to keep the festive season only up to the Dussehra is what I am 
going to say and I am saying as far as Dussehra is concerned, it has been a good 
start to the quarter. Again, I am not ready to say much about Diwali because I think 
it also depends heavily in terms of what banks are going to be doing and also how 
the mood comes through in the Diwali period. 
Vijit Jain: 
Got it, thank you. Understand that. My next question is on UPI. Thanks for the 
disclosure in the letter on the eligible GTV for 2027 and 2028 as well. I guess my 
question is the 2028 number is a good 60% Y-o-Y again over FY2027 and I am just 
trying to understand what are the key drivers of that. If I look at your devices, net 
device addition number, and I know that you have an aggressive plan of 1 million 
device adds as well. So I mean, are you looking at your device count aspirations 
and then projecting that Rs.32,000 Crores to Rs.33,000 Crores or is it something 
else? Whatever you can tell me would be super helpful. 
Amrish Rau: 
First, let me just tell you what is happening in the market, right? What is happening 
in the market is if you are into organized retail, the retailer wants to have 
reconciliation, which is completely automated now, including when it comes to a 
UPI based transaction. Nobody is turning around and saying that I will keep UPI as 
a separate independent device or a sticker outside. So now, I said that in the last 
quarter also. 75% to 77% of the transactions on our POS machine is now a UPI 
transaction. Only 25% is a card based transaction. Now, those 75% transactions 
have grown at about 68% for compounding for the last two years and all which we 
have done is we have said that we think there is another 70% kind of a year which 
is coming up. In other words, what I am trying to say is that organized retailer is also 

 
 
moving to a device-based UPI. We as a company who have not really tried to do a 
bit more in terms of having some soundboxes or having some screen based boxes 
at the merchant location. If we make in a little effort, I do not think so we should be 
short by 70% growth in the next year and at least for one more year. So I think we 
will be able to capture and that is one of the things, which led me to turn around 
and say that we will be deploying at least 10 lakh more soundboxes in the market. 
Vijit Jain: 
Understood, Amrish. Super helpful that and one last bit within that. Since these are 
merchants, these are large enterprise merchants, right? So for you to pass on the 
40 bps MDR to them, is that going to be an automatic process or do you have to go 
to the merchants one by one with your bank partners to kind of work this way out? 
Amrish Rau: 
So just to clarify, from a technical standpoint, we do not need to do anything more. 
From a commercial standpoint, I absolutely do believe when it comes to the largest 
of large merchants that we have with us, there will be a commercial conversation 
to be had for sure. 
Sameer Kamath: 
But Vijit, let me also add that we are seeing two levels of growth, transacting POS 
going up and also the value for transacting POS going up and a large part of our 
base also now comes from the mid market segment where they are going at 40% 
and we are all on the transaction rails there. So a large part of our volumes also 
now comes from the mid market and not just the large segment. So it is a well 
diversified pool of UPI-generating volumes. 
Vijit Jain: 
Understood. Super helpful. Thank you. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. Our next question is from Pranav Kshatriya of Emkay Global. Please go 
ahead. 
Pranav Kshatriya: 
Thanks for the opportunity. I just want to dwell a little bit on the UPI MDR, what you 
commented. I mean thank you for the numbers what you have given. But of course 
of the 65% odd of the transaction value, which are about 2000, there will be certain 

 
 
categories which will be excluded from the MDR or will have a very low MDR of Rs.5 
cap? So what would be the addressable GMV and what we should look at as a take 
rate on that just to get a sense on how this will pan out financially? 
Amrish Rau: 
Pranav, there is a reason why we put it out in the way we have put it out and that is 
because I do think that it is going to take a little longer to do that calculation, which 
says what will be the net take rate across our entire UPI base. So what we felt was 
everybody has heard the 40 basis points which are going to come out. I think it is 
fairly clear that to the acquirer going to be anywhere about 11 basis points. So we 
wanted to just give you the volumes associated with it, what comes through on 
some commercial negotiations, what comes through in terms of breakup between 
some of the changes which could potentially come-up in terms of MCC based 
pricing. We did not want to hazard a guess on that. 
Pranav Kshatriya: 
No worries. Thank you. I will move on to the next question. I want to understand, it is 
good to see 25% plus kind of a growth on transaction-based revenue. And that I 
am just trying to understand what exactly is driving that growth, because 
affordability, I would assume that is the largest part of that. But this time, the festive 
season falls in Q3. Also, the electronics prices have been higher and that is why 
some of the media reports says that the GMV on the electronics has been down for 
the big billion so which I assume that will sort of impact Pine Labs affordability 
business also to some extent at least. So what exactly are the drivers if you can 
highlight let us say top two, three product or even if affordability is not impacted 
that also would be useful. 
Amrish Rau: 
Pranav, to be honest, we have been very clear in explaining this for a long period of 
time. So under the flow-based income, anything that we earn as far as DCC, which 
is the dynamic currency conversion kind of payment transaction, that goes in there. 
Anything that we earn as an aggregator-based revenues, which is transaction-
based, 10 basis points, 15 basis points, 20 basis points, on our regular payment 
transaction, we put it into the flow-based services. Anywhere where we actually 

 
 
provide access to consumer internet companies, so that they can close a 
transaction at a merchant location. Whatever the fees that we earn associated to 
that transaction, we again go and book it into this line item. So that is third. Fourth, 
we have a lot of data-related, marketing-related, advertisement-related services 
in our portfolio. Now those revenues also go and sit in that same bucket here under 
flow-based. And then finally comes on the affordability side. As far as we are 
concerned, we are actually trying to grow all of these services. And some of these 
other services have continued to now become, I would not say significant, I will say 
become chunkier part of our overall revenues when it comes to flow-based 
income. And effectively, that has driven the 25% growth on a year-on-year basis. 
So I do want you all to think about this business to be much more broader than just 
a one-trick pony around affordability. 
Pranav Kshatriya: 
Thank you for that explanation, but I assume that affordability was not at all 
impacted by seasonality or anything like that, or basically the electronic prices.  
Sameer Kamath: 
Pranav, to be very candid, look, whatever macro factors are there, macro factors 
that we have to stay. But adjusted for two, three things you have to keep in mind. 
You have to keep in mind also that festive season was actually driven, it was started 
early, late September, there was a GST cut, etc. If you were to adjust for those one-
offs which are reasoned because of these movements of the festive period, we 
would have seen more or less reasonable numbers. I think across segments, two, 
three things you have to keep in mind for us, affordability has been predominantly 
in the past CDIT, but you have seen volumes across non-CDIT also grow in. So, I 
think non-CDIT plus some of the other initiatives have helped us build an overall 
portfolio of affordability and any short-term shock that you see in any of these 
segments, we are kind of getting compensated by all of these other segments. 
Pranav Kshatriya: 
Fantastic. My next question is around the capex and some of the indirect costs. So 
capex has gone up quite significantly to 240 odd Crores rupees in H1. How should 

 
 
we see this in the context of higher chip prices driving the higher devices, as well as 
your aspiration to deploy a lot more soundboxes? 
Sameer Kamath: 
Pranav, I will take that question. So if you remember in Q4, we said that there was 
this global crisis which resulted into delayed procurements and some orders 
slipping up. So almost about Rs.35-40 Crores of capex actually slipped from Q4 to

about Rs.20-25 Crores of advance for which procurements are still to happen, are 
sitting in the capex which you have seen. So I think adjusted for that, we are pretty 
much in the range, factored for two things. In the mid-market space, we are 
growing at about 39-40%. Some part of it is capex, some part of it is obviously 
device sold, plus we are also seeing a lot of soundboxes that we are going to deploy

for these, there will be a normalized increase in the business given the opportunity 
we see. Otherwise, I think you will see more or less steady state numbers across the 
two years. 
Pranav Kshatriya: 
Thank you for that. Last question from my side. On indirect costs, some jump, you 
talked about investment in marketing and hiring more marketing professional, 
especially in the overseas geographies. How should we think about this? Is Rs.425 
odd Crores or Rs.426 Crores indirect cost is a new normal or it can further increase 
because it was very steady till Q4 FY 2026 and then Q1 was a jump then Q2 again is 
a sharp jump so should we expect this run rate to continue going forward. 
Amrish Rau: 
Sameer, you want to take that. 
Sameer Kamath: 
Pranav, two things are there. I think cloud and data cost is a real cost and I think we 
have always guided that when you look at indirect expenses, look at expenses 
which are linked to top line and which are variable. And cloud and data cost which 

 
 
you see has always been trending in that 8.5% to 9% including the cloud 
infrastructure. I think we have put a lot of initiatives in place to optimize this, to 
modernize it because we are now leveraging AI and the resultant of that 
tokenization cost is the real cost. So that cost will remain variable to about 8% or 9% 
of top line. The other cost within which the indirect cost sits is the outsourced 
employees which are required for ground level execution across multiple initiatives, 
including, for example, we have won large OMC contracts, we want to penetrate 
into the non-CDIT segment, some of the initiatives about investing the sales people

callout, we are a large sponsor of GFF. GFF happened in Q3 last year, GFF happened 
in Q2 this year, so that is a cost which is switched between quarters but I think given 
the size of the event and the showcasing that we can do for products, I think that is 
an important spend for us to kind of showcase our capability and based on those 
capabilities we are able to monetize a lot of those opportunities. So I think one has 
to keep that calibrated and look from a long-term perspective. I think we are 
judicious about our costs. All of these costs are going towards either a new 
geography or a new opportunity or ground level presence to kind of build the rails 
for monetizing for the flow-based businesses. 
Pranav Kshatriya: 
Thank you for your answer. Wish you all the very best. 
Amrish Rau: 
Thank you. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. Our next question is from Nitin Aggarwal of Motilal Oswal. Please go 
ahead. 
Nitin Aggarwal: 
Thanks for the opportunity and congrats Amrish and Sameer on the results. I have 
a couple of questions. One is on the international business revenues. The mix was 
gradually inching up slightly every quarter. This quarter there is a slight dip. And if I 
look at Q-on-Q, this implies just 2%-3% Q-on-Q growth. So how do we look at that? 

 
 
Sameer Kamath: 
I think look, I think overall if you see international businesses are growing in cohorts

the overall business. Some new businesses are building up. I think while the

If you see, there are a lot of vectors within our India business, as Amrish said, which 
are also becoming large and chunky. So mix is a long-term guidance. It is not 
something that can be trapped on a quarter-on-quarter basis. The good part is 
across each of the geographies, and I think Amrish gave some color on it, whether 
we are working in Philippines where it is becoming large, whether we are doing one 
lakh transactions a day in UAE, these are proof points of the fact that these 
geographies have accepted Pine Labs as a preferred partner for their payment and 
e-commerce solution business. 
Amrish Rau: 
Sameer, I want to give one very specific reason associated with it. See, one of the 
things what we do in the international market, especially in Singapore, is we 
distribute gift cards, prepaid cards for some of the large brands. And without being 
specific, one of the largest retailers in the world has actually decided to move out 
of the Singapore market. So the distribution of those cards in the Singapore market 
is a business which has actually been reduced in Q2 for us very specifically. So if 
we actually start to keep Q2 as the base for the change which has happened from

the business. 
Nitin Aggarwal: 
Right. Because the reason I asked also is because our profitability in the overseas 
market, the tax rate will be a function of the revenue line, revenue growth number 
or business size that we reach up to. And it may take longer if it does not grow fast

Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to PG Electroplast Q2 FY27 Earnings Conference 
Call, hosted by JM Financial Institutional Securities Limited. 
As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode, and there will be an 
opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need assistance 
during the conference call, please signal an operator by pressing “*”, then “0” on your touch-
tone phone. Please note that this conference is being recorded. 
I now hand the conference over to Mr. Shalin Choksy from JM Financial Institutional Securities 
Limited. Thank you and over to you, sir. 
Shalin Choksy: 
Thank you. Good morning, everyone. On behalf of JM Financial Institutional Securities, I 
welcome you all to the Q2 FY27 Earnings Call of PG Electroplast Limited. We have with us the 
management of the company, represented by Mr. Vishal Gupta - Managing Director and Mr. 
Pramod Gupta - Chief Financial Officer. 
Before we start off, a brief disclaimer. This presentation has been prepared for informational 
purposes only and does not constitute a prospectus, offering circular, or offering memorandum, 
and is not an offer or initiation to buy or sell any securities, nor shall part or all of this 
presentation from the basis of or to be relied on in any connection with a contract or investment 
decision. 
This presentation contains forward-looking statements based on the currently held beliefs of the 
management of the company which are expressed in good faith and in management's opinion 
are reasonable. The forward-looking statements may involve known and unknown risks, 
uncertainty, and other factors which may cause the actual results, financial condition, 
performance, or achievements of the company or industry to differ materially from those in 
forward-looking statements. These forward-looking statements represent only the company's 
current intentions, beliefs, or expectations, and any such statement speaks only as of the date on 
which it was made. The company assumes no obligation to revise or update any forward-looking 
statements. 
With this, I will hand over the call to the management for their opening remarks, post which we 
can open the floor for questions and answers. Thank you and over to you, Mr. Gupta. 
Vishal Gupta: 
Thank you, Shalin and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining PG Electroplast Q2 FY27 
Earnings Call. I am Vishal Gupta – the Managing Director. And I am joined today by                   
Mr. Pramod Gupta, our CFO, and Mr. Vikas Gupta, our Managing Director, Operations is also 
joining this call. 
Second quarter has panned out on expected lines and we have seen good secondary sales in the 
Room AC business for the industry, resulting in a strong order book for us also. Our teams are 

 
PG Electroplast Limited 
October 28, 2026 
 
 
Page 3 of 19 
gearing up for strong execution in the second half of FY27. For the first half of FY27, 
consolidated revenues crossed Rs. 2,950 crore for the first time in the company's history and the 
room AC and washing machine verticals posted their highest ever first half sales. Growth in first 
half came from combination of volume and price. We saw double digit volume growth and a 
similar quantum of ASP increase as commodity costs and rupee depreciation got passed through 
to our customers. Our order book remains healthy across all product lines. 
I will let Pramodji take you through the numbers in detail and then I will come back to cover our 
capacity roadmap and few other operating priorities for the current financial year. Pramodji! 
Pramod Gupta: 
Thank you, Vishalji. Good morning, everyone. 
Consolidated revenues for the quarter was Rs. 934 crores up 42.5% year-on-year. EBITDA came 
in at Rs. 69.14 crores versus Rs. 44.68 crores last year, growth of 54.8% with EBITDA margin 
of 7.4%. Net income was Rs. 13.67 crores versus Rs. 2.76 crores last financial year in the same 
quarter. 
For first half, product business has contributed 70.3% of sales revenue, growing 41.1% year-on-
year. Within that, AC business saw growth of 36.2% to Rs. 1,561 crores. Washing machines 
crossed Rs. 500 crores of sales and grew 60.7% for the first half. Cooler was muted at about 
4.8% growth and contributed Rs. 19.3 crores. Electronic business has seen a very sharp growth 
of 90.3% and contributed 12% of revenues for the first half. Plastic molding and components 
contributed Rs. 521.6 crores and was up 7.5% year-on-year. Our JV Goodworth Electronics 
posted revenues of Rs. 623.8 crores in the first half versus Rs. 483.4 crores last year. EBITDA 
stood at Rs. 22.7 crores versus Rs. 10.3 crores last year. Our subsidiary PG Technoplast, which 
is obviously a part of consolidated sales which I told above, reported Rs. 2,130 crores in sales 
this year in the first half. 
On margin, I want to clarify once again that gross contribution as a percentage has softened on 
a year-on-year basis, largely because of the pass-through of the commodity prices, particularly 
copper, aluminum, plastic, etc., along with the rupee depreciation. And as you all know, on a 
per-unit basis, margin remains stable and we get a fixed amount on a per-unit basis and not the 
percentage margin for doing the contract manufacturing. 
On balance sheet, things remain quite healthy. Cash and bank balance stood at Rs. 422.5 crores 
and most of the CAPEX for this year is already paid for. Basically, CAPEX payments that are 
not in gross fixed are either in CWIP or advances to suppliers. 
With this, I will now hand it over back to Vishalji. 
Vishal Gupta: 
Thanks, Pramodji. Let me cover some business outlook and our strategy along with a couple of 
other developments for this quarter. 

 
PG Electroplast Limited 
October 28, 2026 
 
 
Page 4 of 19 
Post our flagship washing machine manufacturing facility that came online in new campus in 
DMIC, Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh last quarter. Our new campus at Salarpur, Bhiwadi is now 
operational and we are consolidating operations by relocating some of our Greater Noida 
operations to this new facility. This facility will have coolers, sanitaryware, plastic components 
and mold making facilities. 
Second, our refrigerator facility at Sri City in South India is progressing well. We are targeting 
commercial production as earlier committed in the last quarter of current financial year with this 
becoming a meaningful revenue contributor for FY '28. We have already tied up with our anchor 
customers and we are in active discussions with other customers as well with some soft 
commitments already in place. The facility will have a capacity of 1.2 million units and will start 
in Phase-1 with direct cool and side-by-side refrigerators and add frost-free and multi-door in 
Phase-2. 
On compressors, also the project at Supa is on track for mass production in this financial year. 
Things are progressing well. We expect our first 2 million capacity to come online as planned in 
this financial year only. Alongside that, our strategic priorities for this year are R&D, new 
product development, backward integration and capability enhancement. This all is aimed at 
building longer-term resilience and improving capital efficiencies. 
With that, we will now open the floor for questions. Thank you. 
Moderator: 
Thank you very much. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. The first question 
is from the line of Tanay Shah from DAM Capital. Please go ahead. 
Tanay Shah: 
Yes. Hi, sir. Good morning. Thank you so much for your opportunity. Sir, I have a few questions. 
First one being, we spoke about a double-digit volume growth in AC. Maybe, if you can help us 
understand how the industry sort of grew this quarter on a very unfavorable base versus how we 
have sort of done against that? 
Vishal Gupta: 
In this quarter, the primary sales have been muted. We don't see much larger, very strong growth. 
But secondary sales as per the feedback what we are getting from the industry people has been 
very strong. But again, if you see, if you try to compare this with the Y-o-Y basis, July you can 
compare. August, there was an aberration because of the GST announcement was done. And 
then in September also, the sales started after 22nd September only. But all said and done, still 
the secondary sales have been very strong in the channel. And channel inventory is on a much 
lower side as compared to last year. Yes, second quarter, we didn't see much action. But I believe 
that December quarter and March quarter, we will see much better numbers for our company as 
per the feedback that we are getting from our clients and the kind of order book which we have 
been able to build up to maybe March-April for ourselves. 

 
PG Electroplast Limited 
October 28, 2026 
 
 
Page 5 of 19 
Tanay Shah: 
And so you spoke about, most of the prices being passed on to the customer. So if you could 
quantify the percentage of price hikes taken, and is it completely absorbed now by our 
customers? Or is there another round of price hikes which are due from our side? 
Vishal Gupta: 
See, price hike has been an ongoing activity for us. The first price increase had happened in 
January of this calendar year. Then, it again happened in the month of April, because it is 
normally done on a quarterly basis. And it has been done again in the quarter starting from this 
October quarter. And January quarter also, we are going to take a further price increase from our 
clients, which has been already aligned with most of the clients. So with this second price 
increase, which will happen first January onwards, most likely most of the price hikes, which 
should be factored in till now, will be taken into account for. 
Tanay Shah: 
Sir, I was asking from our second quarter perspective, because I think we mentioned in a press 
release that most of the price increase has been passed through. So I just want to see that if the 
gross margin compression was also due to some bit of under absorption, or it is just as a function 
of, obviously, the ASP hike, which is optically making our gross margins look lower? 
Pramod Gupta: 
First of all, gross margins as a percentage will always be lower in a high commodity price 
environment, because we as a contract manufacturer typically get our margins or contribution 
on a per unit basis. That is point number one. Point number two, this quarter, which you have to 
keep in mind is that we had a very high growth in the electronics business. Electronics business 
has a much lower margin. That is one. And secondly, this quarter, the high growth was due to 
the rising prices of electronic components, semiconductors specifically, rather than very huge 
volume growth. The reason this has happened is because we do a lot of contract manufacturing 
and also we supply motherboards of TVs, etc., where the memory prices have shot up very 
significantly. So because of those reasons, because the mix change and high commodity prices, 
the gross contribution percentage is lower for the quarter. But on an absolute price per piece 
basis, we are in our usual range now. And whatever price increases was required in the AC 
business, till September that we have been able to pass on in October. And again, whatever will 
be required for the quarter starting January, which will be based on the average cost of October, 
November, December, we intend to pass it from 1st of January. 
Tanay Shah: 
Sure, sir. And the other thing what I wanted to understand was if you could help us with the 
incentives booked this quarter and a corresponding incentive number for the last year, same 
quarter? 
Pramod Gupta: 
So this quarter, we don't have any PLI. PLI, we book, as you know, on the basis of the sanctions 
received and we are yet to file for the last financial year's numbers. PLI, this thing, because there 
are GST audit, etc., just is getting completed. So that number is likely to come probably in the 
Q3 and Q4 for us and we will be reporting that number to you. For the full year, this year, the 
PLI is likely to be close to Rs. 70 crores plus for us.

October 28, 2026

Tanay Shah: 
Sure. And anything specifically booked apart from the PLI in this quarter? Obviously, there is 
no PLI booking this quarter, but any other incentives from a state perspective, which we booked? 
Pramod Gupta: 
For the PGEL, we continue to book about Rs. 1.55 crores of incentive, which we get for the 
Maharashtra government that has been booked. 
Tanay Shah: 
Got that. I will fall back in the queue. Thank you so much for answering my question. All the 
best. Thanks. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. The next question is from the line of Achal Lohade from Nuvama Institutional 
Equities. Please go ahead. 
Achal Lohade: 
Good morning, sir. Thank you for the opportunity. Sir, if you could talk a little bit about how 
was the sales volume for RAC in 2Q? And if you could also help us with the corresponding 
number of last year 2Q? And what is the expectation for FY27, basis the current order book

Pramod Gupta:

Pramod Gupta: 
It will be surely close to about 15%-20% range. 
Vishal Gupta: 
The average price increase across 3-4 quarters and what we expect in January quarter, all 
cumulative will be something around 15%. 
Achal Lohade: 
Got it. The other question I have, this is more medium-term question. We have called out with 
respect to the ref, washing machines, etc. But any thought on the additional growth avenues in 
terms of the segments, products, etc., if you could give us some sense, or let us say, next                  
3-5 years beyond the current products what we are currently looking at? 
Pramod Gupta: 
The immediate priorities for the management and top leadership team remain operationalizing 
these new projects which have seen sizable CAPEX in the last 3 years for us and trying to restore 
the profitability in the business to the next level. And we will be looking for growth 
opportunities, but right now, we do not want to focus on anything substantial till the time we

have been able to scale up these new initiatives which we are taking. And I think for 27 and 28, 
the key priorities just remain to get these new projects on stream and the requisite profitability 
on them. These are sizable CAPEX projects which we have done and we think that we can 
continue to see good volume momentum across the product lines which we are there, which is 
AC, washing machine, refrigerator, TVs. And we do not intend to right now defocus on them 
and try to look for some other new opportunities. We are right now very focused on getting these 
new projects up and running and in a profitable manner. 
Achal Lohade: 
Fair point. Thank you. I have this last question, if I may, with respect to the compressor scenario, 
if you could give us some sense, any further update from the previous call in terms of how it is 
shaping up for the industry? And also another related question was in terms of the exports

Vishal Gupta: 
The compressor project, as I said in the call earlier, is on track. The machine installation is going

we are hoping that we hope to start trial production by end of November. And I think by January-

April-May, we will take a decision on that also. 
Achal Lohade: 
And on exports, if you could help us understand? 
Vishal Gupta: 
Exports, we are doing a small number of exports right now to SARC nations, very small number. 
When you try to compare with China in Europe and America markets, the products are a little 
different. They are quite different. And on the top of that, the pricing, what they are offering in 
those markets, in spite of whatever duty benefits, what we have, because of FT and all that, still 
that price disability is very large as of now. So it looks as of now, it is a little challenging for our 
exports to these countries. But yes, SARC nations, we are doing small exports, but those markets 
itself are very small. And nothing to talk about much right now. Products are there, products are 
being developed. But whenever we do some kind of benchmarking, then the pricing becomes a 
major issue when we are talking about exports. 
Achal Lohade: 
All right. Thank you, sir. I will fall back in the queue. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. The next question is from the line of Santosh Seshadri from Avendus Spark. Please 
go ahead. 
Santosh Seshadri: 
Hi, good morning. Thanks for taking up the questions. So my first question is on the cost savings 
that you have achieved. There has been some considerable savings in employee cost and other 

 
PG Electroplast Limited 
October 28, 2026 
 
 
Page 8 of 19 
operating expense line items. Sir, my question is, how should we think about it going forward? 
Should we expect it at the similar levels or maybe a step up in the cost base, given that many of 
the new projects, especially the compressor facilities are ramping up in the second half? 
Pramod Gupta: 
So I will take this question in two parts. Looking at the employee cost, obviously we are running 
a tight ship and we are trying to control that. But there is a growth there. But in the other 
operational expenses, manufacturing expense, there is a reduction Y-o-Y because of two reasons. 
One is that last year we had a FOREX loss of about Rs. 8 crores. And this year, we had a smaller 
FOREX loss of about Rs. 3 crores only. So there was Rs. 5 crores benefit on that account. And 
also last year, we had some one-off related to some GST, etc., which we took in the second 
quarter. And because of all those things, there was about Rs. 3 crores of additional cost, which 
we have not incurred in this quarter. That is why the other expenses are looking the way they 
are. Going forward, as we ramp up the new facilities and the production in the existing facilities, 
obviously, the manpower cost and other expenses are likely to go up. But obviously, they will 
not be going in line with the sales growth because this year, there is a significant portion of sales 
growth which is happening because of the commodity pass-through. So the costs will be 
increasing more in line with the volume increases, which will be about 20%-25% on an overall 
company basis and that is what is our internal target. 
Santosh Seshadri: 
Got it, sir. And as a follow-up on that, how should we think about the margins in the second half 
and going forward vis-a-vis the price increases that you are planning to achieve further? 
Pramod Gupta: 
Second half, typically is slightly better for us seasonally because there are obviously slightly 
higher sales and also operating leverage kicks in. Also the way we book the PLI, the 4th quarter 
typically sees better margins. So we hope to have slightly better margin in the second half than 
what we have reported in the first half this year. 
Santosh Seshadri: 
And just lastly, on the finance cost, can you provide some color? How should we expect this 
going forward? Is there any room for optimizing working capital and bringing the finance cost 
down? Any color on that will be helpful. 
Pramod Gupta: 
We are trying to work on optimizing the working capital, but actually what is happening is 
because of the high commodity prices, even with the optimization, the amount of inventory that 
you are requiring to keep is actually high. And that is leading to high investment in the working 
capital, leading to higher interest costs. We are trying our best to optimize wherever possible. 
Hopefully, because all the CAPEX has been paid off, only the working capital requirements will 
go up and we have some inventory. We are hoping that the second half interest cost should not 
significantly increase from the first half interest cost. And that is going to be the focus area in 
the company in the second half. 
Santosh Seshadri: 
Thank you very much, sir.

Vishal Gupta: 
Thank you.

Advisors. Please go ahead. 
Bala Murali Krishna: 
Hi, sir. Good morning. 
Pramod Gupta: 
Good morning.

Regarding this new subsidiary you have created, do you have any plans for any other new 
products? What are the thoughts behind this? 
Pramod Gupta: 
We have not created any new subsidiary. We have a subsidiary which is actually already there, 
which is PG Technoplast and PG Technoplast has a subsidiary called Next Generation 
Manufacturing. So that structure remains. We have not created any new company right now.

Dear Sirs, 
 
Please note that a meeting of the Board of Directors of the Company was held on Friday, October 30, 
2026, at 03.25 PM and was concluded at 05:45 PM. 
 
In terms of SEBI Listing Regulations, we would like to inform you that in the said meeting the Board of

1. 
The standalone and consolidated unaudited financial results along with the statement of assets 
and liabilities and cash flow statement for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026.

2026, pursuant to Regulations 52(7) & 52(7A) of the Listing Regulations; 
2. 
An Interim Dividend of Rs. 2.15 per share having face value of Re. 1 each. 
3. 
The record date for the payment of interim dividend to be Friday, November 06, 2026. Dividend 
shall be paid to the shareholders on or before Saturday, November 28, 2026. 
 
The disclosure of Related Party Transactions pursuant to the provisions of Regulations 23 (9) of the 
Listing Regulations is being filed as a part of Integrated Filing (Financial) with BSE and NSE through 
XBRL Mode.

On July 21, 2026, the Board of Directors of the Company approved acquisition of 28.99% equity stake on HL Mando Anand India Private Limited equivalent to 48,134,427 equity shares from Asia Investments Private Limited
(Promoter and holding company of the Company), for a composite consideration of Rs.22,310 millions which was approved by the shareholder on August 19, 2026. The Consideration was discharged by issue of 1,44,04,204 equity
shares at aggregating to Rs. 18,810 million to the Promoter on preferential basis and balance Rs. 3,500 millions was paid in cash. The preferential allotment of securities was done on September 11, 2026 which was considered as the
date of acquisition by the management. The Company has accounted the acquisition at fair value in accordance with IND AS 28 "Investments in Associates and Joint Ventures".
On July 21, 2026, the Board of Directors of the Company had accorded its approval for execution of Share Purchase Agreement and Joint Venture Agreements ('Agreements') with HL Klemove Corporation and HL Klemove India
Private Limited ('the "Target Company'), purchasing 37,844,999 equity shares of the Target Company at a consideration of USD 98.44 million. The Company has acquired the shares on August 25, 2026 and has been considered as
date of acquisition. The Company has accounted the acquisition at fair value in accordance with IND AS 28 "Investments in Associates and Joint Ventures".
Particulars
These standalone financial results have been prepared in accordance with the Indian Accounting Standard (Ind AS) as prescribed under Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013, read with Rule 3 of the Companies (Indian Accounting
Standards) Rule, 2015 and relevant amendment thereunder.
The above standalone results have been reviewed by the Audit Committee and approved by the Board of Directors in their meeting held on October 30, 2026.
 - After accounting for Scheme 
As the Company's business activity falls within a single operating segment viz. "auto components and parts", no segment information is required to be disclosed. 
Exceptional item relates to the obligations for the employees past service created pursuant to the implementation of the four labour codes with effect from November 21, 2025.
