The Board of Directors, at its meeting held on June 30, 2025, approved a Composite Scheme of Arrangement (the "Scheme") involving the merger of Anchemco India Private Limited (a fellow subsidiary) with Asia Investments Private
Limited (the Immediate Holding Company) on a going concern basis with effect from the Appointed Date of April 1, 2025, and the subsequent demerger and transfer of the Automotive Undertaking (as defined in the Scheme) of Asia
Investments Private Limited to the Company with effect from the Appointed Date of April 1, 2026. 
The Scheme was approved by the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) vide its order dated May 11, 2026. Accordingly, during the half year ended September 30, 2026, the Company has given effect to the Scheme using the
pooling of interest method, applied retrospectively for all periods and year ended March 31, 2026, presented in the standalone financial results, as prescribed under Ind AS 103 – "Business Combinations", and the figures for the
previous periods have been restated accordingly. The restated results for the quarter ended September 30, 2025, half year ended September 30, 2025 and the quarter ended March 31, 2026, have, to the extent of the Automotive
Undertaking included therein, neither been subjected to limited review and such figures have been furnished by the management of the Company, which has exercised necessary due diligence to ensure that these financial results

Pursuant to Regulation 30, 33, 42, 43, 51 & 52 of SEBI (Listing Obligations and 
Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, we write to inform that Board of Directors 
of the Company at their meeting held on Wednesday, 04th November, 2026, have, inter 
– alia considered and approved the following:
1.
The Standalone & Consolidated Un-Audited Financial Results of the Company for the
Quarter and Half year ended 30th September, 2026. The copy of the Un-Audited
Financial Results along with the Limited Review Report given by the Joint Statutory
Auditors of the Company on the Un-Audited Financial Results and other required
disclosures are enclosed herewith as Annexure-I.
The Un-Audited Financial Results have been reviewed and recommended by the
Audit Committee and approved by the Board of Directors of the Company, at their
respective meetings held on 04th November, 2026.
2.
Declaration of Interim Dividend of 15% (i.e. Rs. 1.5/- per equity share) on the face
value of paid-up equity shares of Rs. 10/- each for the Financial Year 2026-27.
3.
Fixation of 12th November, 2026 as the Record Date for the purpose of ascertaining
the members entitled for Interim Dividend for the FY 2026-27. It is further informed
that the said interim dividend will be paid to eligible shareholders as per the
statutory timelines in one or more tranches.
4.
Fund raising through Issuance of Bonds in the nature of Debentures of upto Rs. 2,500
Crore in phased manner based on requirement.
5.
Setting up of an additional 660 MW unit as an expansion project of NUPPL within
the existing 1,886-acre premises of Ghatampur Thermal Power Station (3 × 660 MW).
6.
Offer for Sale (OFS) of up to 10,00,00,000 (Ten Crore) equity shares of face value of
Rs.10 each held by the Company in NLC India Renewables Limited (NIRL), Wholly

Notes to Standalone Unaudited Financial Results for the Quarter and Half Year ended 
30th Sep tern her 2026 
1. The above Standalone Unaudited Financial Results for the quarter and half year ended 30th 
September 2026 have been reviewed by the Audit Committee in its meeting held on 4th 
November 2026 and approved by the Board of Directors in their meeting held on the same 
date. 
2. The Joint Statutory Auditors have carried out a limited review of these Standalone 
Unaudited Financial Results as required under Regulations 33 and 52 of the Securities a~d 
Exchange Board oflndia (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 
2015, as amended from time to time. 
3. The Standalone Unaudited Financial Results for the quarter and half year ended 30th 
September 2026, are in compliance with IND AS and other accounting principles 
generally accepted in India. 
4. In line with the National Monetization Pipeline and in consultation with the Ministry of 
Coal, NLCIL executed a Business Transfer Agreement (BT A) with NLC India 
Renewables Limited on 31 st October 2025 for transferring 1,430 MW of renewable energy 
assets. Phase I was completed on 1st January 2026, followed by Phase JI involving 708.96 
MW of assets for ~853.97 crore, based on the assets and liabilities as of 1st September 
2026, pursuant to the second addendum to the BTA signed on 3rd September 2026. 
5. The company invested 200,00,00,000 equity shares in NLC India Renewables Limited 
(NIRL ), wholly owned subsidiary of the company at Rs. IO per share aggregating to Rs. 
2,000 crore on 12th October 2026. Pursuant to this investment, the Company's total 
investment in NIRL increased to ~5,119.75 crore as on 12th October 2026. 
6. The Company remeasured its Deferred Tax Assets and Deferred Tax Liabilities during the 
half year ended 30th September 2026 by applying the provisions ofnew tax regime against 
the hitherto applied old tax regime. The change is in accordance with the option exercised 
for the financial year 2025-26 the impact of which is ~714.17 crores.

1. The above Standalone Unaudited Financial Results for the quarter and half year ended 30th 
September 2026 have been reviewed by the Audit Committee in its meeting held on 4th 
November 2026 and approved by the Board of Directors in their meeting held on the same 
date. 
2. The Joint Statutory Auditors have carried out a limited review of these Standalone 
Unaudited Financial Results as required under Regulations 33 and 52 of the Securities a~d 
Exchange Board oflndia (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 
2015, as amended from time to time. 
3. The Standalone Unaudited Financial Results for the quarter and half year ended 30th 
September 2026, are in compliance with IND AS and other accounting principles 
generally accepted in India. 
4. In line with the National Monetization Pipeline and in consultation with the Ministry of 
Coal, NLCIL executed a Business Transfer Agreement (BT A) with NLC India 
Renewables Limited on 31 st October 2025 for transferring 1,430 MW of renewable energy 
assets. Phase I was completed on 1st January 2026, followed by Phase JI involving 708.96 
MW of assets for ~853.97 crore, based on the assets and liabilities as of 1st September 
2026, pursuant to the second addendum to the BTA signed on 3rd September 2026. 
5. The company invested 200,00,00,000 equity shares in NLC India Renewables Limited 
(NIRL ), wholly owned subsidiary of the company at Rs. IO per share aggregating to Rs. 
2,000 crore on 12th October 2026. Pursuant to this investment, the Company's total 
investment in NIRL increased to ~5,119.75 crore as on 12th October 2026. 
6. The Company remeasured its Deferred Tax Assets and Deferred Tax Liabilities during the 
half year ended 30th September 2026 by applying the provisions ofnew tax regime against 
the hitherto applied old tax regime. The change is in accordance with the option exercised 
for the financial year 2025-26 the impact of which is ~714.17 crores. 
7. CERC and Regulatory related matters: 
1. 
CERC notified the Tariff Regulations, 2024 for the 2024-29 period vide order 
dated 15th March 2024. Pending the receipt of the tariff orders, thermal billing/ 
accounting is being carried out as per the 2019-24 CERC orders. Income of N4.64 
crore for Q2 FY 2026-27 and ~283 crore cumulatively has been recognized under 
the regulatory deferral account based on account of operating norms applicable for 
2024-29 tariff period. 
11. 
For Neyveli Mines, billing is provisionally based on CERC's interim lignite price 
order, since final tariff order for 2019-24 is yet to be received. For Barsingsar 
Mines, billing is provisionally based on the input price filed with CERC for 2024-
29. 
iii. 
During FY 2022-23, the Company billed ~386.51 crore to DlSCOMs towards 
income tax recoverable under CERC Tariff Regulation · :_ .. ::

where the matter is still sub-judice. Accordingly, the Company has retained

the members entitled for Interim Dividend for the FY 2026-27. It is further informed
that the said interim dividend will be paid to eligible shareholders as per the
statutory timelines in one or more tranches.

Crore in phased manner based on requirement.

the existing 1,886-acre premises of Ghatampur Thermal Power Station (3 × 660 MW).

Notes to Standalone Unaudited Financial Results for the Quarter and Half Year ended 
30th Sep tern her 2026 
1. The above Standalone Unaudited Financial Results for the quarter and half year ended 30th 
September 2026 have been reviewed by the Audit Committee in its meeting held on 4th 
November 2026 and approved by the Board of Directors in their meeting held on the same 
date. 
2. The Joint Statutory Auditors have carried out a limited review of these Standalone 
Unaudited Financial Results as required under Regulations 33 and 52 of the Securities a~d 
Exchange Board oflndia (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 
2015, as amended from time to time. 
3. The Standalone Unaudited Financial Results for the quarter and half year ended 30th 
September 2026, are in compliance with IND AS and other accounting principles 
generally accepted in India. 
4. In line with the National Monetization Pipeline and in consultation with the Ministry of 
Coal, NLCIL executed a Business Transfer Agreement (BT A) with NLC India 
Renewables Limited on 31 st October 2025 for transferring 1,430 MW of renewable energy 
assets. Phase I was completed on 1st January 2026, followed by Phase JI involving 708.96 
MW of assets for ~853.97 crore, based on the assets and liabilities as of 1st September 
2026, pursuant to the second addendum to the BTA signed on 3rd September 2026. 
5. The company invested 200,00,00,000 equity shares in NLC India Renewables Limited 
(NIRL ), wholly owned subsidiary of the company at Rs. IO per share aggregating to Rs. 
2,000 crore on 12th October 2026. Pursuant to this investment, the Company's total 
investment in NIRL increased to ~5,119.75 crore as on 12th October 2026. 
6. The Company remeasured its Deferred Tax Assets and Deferred Tax Liabilities during the 
half year ended 30th September 2026 by applying the provisions ofnew tax regime against 
the hitherto applied old tax regime. The change is in accordance with the option exercised 
for the financial year 2025-26 the impact of which is ~714.17 crores. 
7. CERC and Regulatory related matters: 
1. 
CERC notified the Tariff Regulations, 2024 for the 2024-29 period vide order 
dated 15th March 2024. Pending the receipt of the tariff orders, thermal billing/ 
accounting is being carried out as per the 2019-24 CERC orders. Income of N4.64 
crore for Q2 FY 2026-27 and ~283 crore cumulatively has been recognized under 
the regulatory deferral account based on account of operating norms applicable for 
2024-29 tariff period. 
11.

order, since final tariff order for 2019-24 is yet to be received. For Barsingsar 
Mines, billing is provisionally based on the input price filed with CERC for 2024-
29.

1. The above Standalone Unaudited Financial Results for the quarter and half year ended 30th 
September 2026 have been reviewed by the Audit Committee in its meeting held on 4th 
November 2026 and approved by the Board of Directors in their meeting held on the same 
date. 
2. The Joint Statutory Auditors have carried out a limited review of these Standalone 
Unaudited Financial Results as required under Regulations 33 and 52 of the Securities a~d 
Exchange Board oflndia (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 
2015, as amended from time to time. 
3. The Standalone Unaudited Financial Results for the quarter and half year ended 30th 
September 2026, are in compliance with IND AS and other accounting principles 
generally accepted in India. 
4. In line with the National Monetization Pipeline and in consultation with the Ministry of 
Coal, NLCIL executed a Business Transfer Agreement (BT A) with NLC India 
Renewables Limited on 31 st October 2025 for transferring 1,430 MW of renewable energy 
assets. Phase I was completed on 1st January 2026, followed by Phase JI involving 708.96 
MW of assets for ~853.97 crore, based on the assets and liabilities as of 1st September 
2026, pursuant to the second addendum to the BTA signed on 3rd September 2026. 
5. The company invested 200,00,00,000 equity shares in NLC India Renewables Limited 
(NIRL ), wholly owned subsidiary of the company at Rs. IO per share aggregating to Rs. 
2,000 crore on 12th October 2026. Pursuant to this investment, the Company's total 
investment in NIRL increased to ~5,119.75 crore as on 12th October 2026. 
6. The Company remeasured its Deferred Tax Assets and Deferred Tax Liabilities during the 
half year ended 30th September 2026 by applying the provisions ofnew tax regime against 
the hitherto applied old tax regime. The change is in accordance with the option exercised 
for the financial year 2025-26 the impact of which is ~714.17 crores. 
7. CERC and Regulatory related matters: 
1. 
CERC notified the Tariff Regulations, 2024 for the 2024-29 period vide order 
dated 15th March 2024. Pending the receipt of the tariff orders, thermal billing/ 
accounting is being carried out as per the 2019-24 CERC orders. Income of N4.64 
crore for Q2 FY 2026-27 and ~283 crore cumulatively has been recognized under 
the regulatory deferral account based on account of operating norms applicable for 
2024-29 tariff period. 
11. 
For Neyveli Mines, billing is provisionally based on CERC's interim lignite price 
order, since final tariff order for 2019-24 is yet to be received. For Barsingsar 
Mines, billing is provisionally based on the input price filed with CERC for 2024-
29. 
iii. 
During FY 2022-23, the Company billed ~386.51 crore to DlSCOMs towards 
income tax recoverable under CERC Tariff Regulation · :_ .. ::

However, the same was litigated in various High Courts, who in turn has remanded 
the matter to CERC for adjudication except for the High Court of Andhra Pradesh, 
where the matter is still sub-judice. Accordingly, the Company has retained 
regulatory deferral liability of ~415.77 crore, including cumulative interest of 
~29.26 crore, as at 30th September 2026. 
1v. 
As per CERC Tariff Regulations, regulatory income of n6.69 crore for Q2 FY 
2026-27 and ~382.43 crore cumulatively has been recognized towards expenses 
which are subject to check by CERC e.g. security expenses, water charges and 
capital spares.

Tariff Regulations. Further, regulatory liability of ~10.23 crore was reversed. 
vi. 
During the quarter, the company received truing up o.rder dated 29.09.2026 in 
respect of BTPS for FY 2019-24. Accordingly unbilled income of n6.02 crore 
(~59.64 crore towards principal and n6.38 crore towards interest) was recognized

ended September 30, 2025). Furthermore, during the half year ended September 30, 2026, the Company has aquired loan exposure of an amount off 5230.99 Crore with an outstanding off 5216.59 Crore as on 
30.09.2026. 
There was Nil Investor complaint pending with HUDCO as on 30th September, 2026. 
During the half year ended 30th September,2026, there were no transactions in the nature of exceptional or extraordinary items. 
The Company has sufficient liquidity as well as adequate undrawn lines of credits from various banks to take care of its operational requirements. Considering high credit worthiness and well-established relationship of the 
Company with lenders, it can continue to mobilize sufficient funds from domestic & international markets to meet contingencies, if any. Further, there has been no default in repayment of debt securities, borrowings and 
other liabilities and the Company has met all its debt servicing obligations, both towards principal and interest, during the period in a timely manner. 
Pursuant to the Board Resolutions vide item no. 688.2.16 in the board meeting held on 12.12.2025, it has been decided that Company has no intention to make a withdrawal from the Special Reserve created and maintained 
under section 36(l )(viii) of the Income Tax Act 1961. Accordingly, the Company is not creating any deferred tax liability on the outstanding amount of Special Reserve created and maintained as on 30.09.2026. 
Pursuant to the press release issued by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) dated August 6, 2026, bearing reference number 2026-2027/ 823, titled " RBI releases list of NBFCs in the Upper Layer ( NBFC-UL) under Scale Based 
Regulation for NBFCs", Housing and Urban Development Corporation Limited (HUDCO) has been included in the list of Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) classified under the Upper Layer (NBFC-UL) for the financial 
year 2026-27. The said classification has been made under the RBI's Scale Based Regulation framework, pursuant to the revised criteria prescribed under the Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies-, 
Registration, Exemptions and Framework for Scale Based Regulation) Directions, 2025.Further, RBI vide letter dated August 07, 2026 has also communicated the decision to place HUDCO is Upper Layer. 
As per the communication dated 22nd September, 2026 received from Department of Investment and Public Asset Management {DIPAM), Ministry of Finance, Government of India, shares held under the demat account of 
Ministry of Rural Development (20.73%) have been transferred to the demat account of Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA). Consequent upon this transfer, entire promoter shareholding (75%) of the Company is 
held by MoHUA i.e. the Administrative Ministry. 
The additional information as required under Regulation 52(4) of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 is attached as Annexure A. 
The company has maintained 100% security cover by way of charge on the receivables of the company for all the secured bonds/ debentures issued by the company and outstanding as on September 30, 2026. In

Dear Sir/Madam, 
 
Subject: Outcome of Board Meeting 
 
We wish to inform you that the Board of Directors of the Company at its meeting held today, i.e. 4th 
November, 2026 has inter-alia 
 
i. 
Considered and approved Un-Audited Financial Results (Standalone and Consolidated) of 
the Company for the Quarter and Half year ended 30th September, 2026, as reviewed and 
recommended by the Audit Committee. 
 
In this regard, we are enclosing herewith Un-Audited Financial Results (Standalone and 
Consolidated) of the Company for the Quarter and Half year ended 30th September, 2026 
along with the Limited Review Reports issued by the Statutory Auditors of the Company 
(Annexure-A). 
 
ii. 
Declared an Interim Dividend of 400% i.e. ₹4.00/- per equity share of ₹1/- each fully paid up 
for the Financial Year 2026-27 and the same shall be paid to the Equity Shareholders of the 
Company whose names appear in the Register of Members of the Company or in the records 
of the Depositories as beneficial owners as on Wednesday, 11th November, 2026 which is 
the Record Date fixed for the said purpose. 
 
We would like to further inform you that the said Interim Dividend will be paid to the 
Equity Shareholders of the Company on and from Thursday, 26th November, 2026. 
 
iii. 
Considered and approved the reconstitution of the Board Committees w.e.f. 4th November, 
2026. The composition of re-constituted committees approved by the Board is annexed as 
Annexure-B. 
 
Further, the said meeting commenced at 01.00 P.M and concluded at 02.30 P.M. 
 
Thanking You. 
Yours faithfully 
For Balrampur Chini Mills Limited

Dear Sir/Madam, 
 
Subject: Outcome of Board Meeting 
 
We wish to inform you that the Board of Directors of the Company at its meeting held today, i.e. 4th 
November, 2026 has inter-alia 
 
i. 
Considered and approved Un-Audited Financial Results (Standalone and Consolidated) of 
the Company for the Quarter and Half year ended 30th September, 2026, as reviewed and 
recommended by the Audit Committee. 
 
In this regard, we are enclosing herewith Un-Audited Financial Results (Standalone and 
Consolidated) of the Company for the Quarter and Half year ended 30th September, 2026 
along with the Limited Review Reports issued by the Statutory Auditors of the Company 
(Annexure-A). 
 
ii. 
Declared an Interim Dividend of 400% i.e. ₹4.00/- per equity share of ₹1/- each fully paid up 
for the Financial Year 2026-27 and the same shall be paid to the Equity Shareholders of the 
Company whose names appear in the Register of Members of the Company or in the records 
of the Depositories as beneficial owners as on Wednesday, 11th November, 2026 which is 
the Record Date fixed for the said purpose. 
 
We would like to further inform you that the said Interim Dividend will be paid to the 
Equity Shareholders of the Company on and from Thursday, 26th November, 2026. 
 
iii. 
Considered and approved the reconstitution of the Board Committees w.e.f. 4th November, 
2026. The composition of re-constituted committees approved by the Board is annexed as 
Annexure-B. 
 
Further, the said meeting commenced at 01.00 P.M and concluded at 02.30 P.M. 
 
Thanking You. 
Yours faithfully 
For Balrampur Chini Mills Limited

The above Statement of Unaudited Standalone Financial Results of Balrampur Chini Mills Limited ("the
Company") for the quarter and six months ended 30th September 2026, along with notes thereupon,
including the Statement of Unaudited Standalone Assets and Liabilities, and the Statement of Unaudited
Standalone Cash Flows, as given in Note 1 and 2 respectively, were reviewed by the Audit Committee
and thereafter, approved by the Board of Directors. The results were taken on record at their respective
meetings held on 4th November, 2026. The Statutory Auditors have carried out limited review of the
above financial results for the quarter and six months ended 30th September, 2026.
4.
The Board of Directors have declared an interim dividend of z 4/- (400.00%) per Equity Share of z 1/­
each.
S(a) 
Pursuant to the "BCML Employees Stock Appreciation Rights Plan 2023" ("ESAR 2023" / "Plan"), and
the "BCML Restricted Stock Unit Scheme 2025" ("RSU 2025" / "Scheme"), rights/ units have been
granted to eligible employees entitling them to subscribe to the Company's equity shares, on or after the
respective vesting dates, in accordance with the terms and conditions of the Plan/ Scheme.
During the quarter and six months ended 30th September, 2026, the Company has allotted 330289 equity
shares of par value of z 1/- each pursuant to the exercise of ESARs.
As at 30th September, 2026, 5065 equity shares were pending allotment pursuant to the exercise of
ESARs.
5(b) 
Subsequent to 30th September 2026, further 87132 ESARs were exercised up to 23rd October 2026. During
October 2026, the Company has allotted an aggregate of 44287 equity shares of par value of z 1/- each
pursuant to the exercise of ESARs. The above allotment includes 5065 equity shares of par value of z 1/­
each, which were pending allotment as at 30th September 2026.
6(a) 
During the six months ended 30th September 2026, the Company has issued and allotted 9316771 equity
shares of par value of z 1/- each on a preferential basis for cash at an issue price of z 483/- per equity
share (including a securities premium of z 482/- per equity share), aggregating to z 45000.00 lakhs,
pursuant to the requisite approvals of the Board of Directors and the Shareholders.
6(b) 
During the quarter and six months ended 30th September 2026, the Company has utilised z 15062.00
lakhs and z 32136.00 lakhs, respectively, towards the objects of the issue. The unutilised balance of the
issue proceeds amounting to z 12864.00 lakhs as at 30th September, 2026 were temporarily invested in
bank deposits and money market mutual funds pending utilisation towards the objects of the issue.
7.
Consequent to the above allotments, as mentioned in Notes 5(a) and 6(a) above, the paid-up equity share
capital of the Company has increased to 211597496 equity shares of par value of t 1/- each as at 30th
September 2026.

Dear Sir/Madam, 
 
Subject: Outcome of Board Meeting 
 
We wish to inform you that the Board of Directors of the Company at its meeting held today, i.e. 4th 
November, 2026 has inter-alia 
 
i. 
Considered and approved Un-Audited Financial Results (Standalone and Consolidated) of 
the Company for the Quarter and Half year ended 30th September, 2026, as reviewed and 
recommended by the Audit Committee. 
 
In this regard, we are enclosing herewith Un-Audited Financial Results (Standalone and 
Consolidated) of the Company for the Quarter and Half year ended 30th September, 2026 
along with the Limited Review Reports issued by the Statutory Auditors of the Company 
(Annexure-A). 
 
ii. 
Declared an Interim Dividend of 400% i.e. ₹4.00/- per equity share of ₹1/- each fully paid up 
for the Financial Year 2026-27 and the same shall be paid to the Equity Shareholders of the 
Company whose names appear in the Register of Members of the Company or in the records 
of the Depositories as beneficial owners as on Wednesday, 11th November, 2026 which is 
the Record Date fixed for the said purpose. 
 
We would like to further inform you that the said Interim Dividend will be paid to the 
Equity Shareholders of the Company on and from Thursday, 26th November, 2026. 
 
iii. 
Considered and approved the reconstitution of the Board Committees w.e.f. 4th November, 
2026. The composition of re-constituted committees approved by the Board is annexed as 
Annexure-B. 
 
Further, the said meeting commenced at 01.00 P.M and concluded at 02.30 P.M. 
 
Thanking You. 
Yours faithfully 
For Balrampur Chini Mills Limited

Companies Act, 2013, as amended, read with relevant rules issued thereunder and other accounting principles
generally accepted in India, and in compliance with Regulation 33 of the Listing Regulations. Our responsibility is to
issue a report on the Statement based on our review.

'Review of Interim Financial Information performed by the Independent Auditor of the Entity', issued by the
Institute of Chartered Accountants of India. This Standard requires that we plan and perform the review to obtain

Q2 & H1 FY27 Financial Results 
Marksans Pharma crosses Rs. 900 crore quarterly revenue for the first time; Q2FY27 
EBITDA up 48% to a record Rs. 214 crore, H1FY27 PAT nearly doubles to Rs. 303 crore 
 
Mumbai, November 4th, 2026 – Marksans Pharma Ltd. (NSE: MARKSANS; BSE Code: 524404) reported the financial 
results for the quarter and half year ended on September 30, 2026. 
Mark Saldanha, Founder, Chairman & Managing Director, said, “Q2FY27 marks a landmark quarter for Marksans 
Pharma, with the Company delivering its strongest-ever performance. Revenue reached ₹940 crore, up 30.5% YoY. 
Adjusted for acquisition (QliniQ) impact, revenue growth remained healthy at 25%.  
EBITDA grew 48.3% to a record ₹214 crore, with margins expanding 274 bps to 22.8%. For H1FY27, revenue grew 32.9% 
to ₹1,781 crore, EBITDA rose 74.7% with margins up 574 bps to 24.0%, and PAT nearly doubled to ₹303 crore, already 
over 70% of our full-year FY26 profit. 
Growth was broad-based. UK & Europe grew 64.9% to a record ₹405 crore in Q2, with the base business growing 48.6% 
organically and QliniQ, our new European front-end, contributing around ₹84 crore in H1. Australia & New Zealand 
grew 64.0%, and US & North America delivered its highest-ever quarter at ₹421 crore. Equally encouraging was the 
strength of cash generation, with H1 operating cash flow reaching ₹322 crore, 4.3 times the previous year, and cash 
balances closing at ₹1,124 crore. Our trailing twelve-month ROCE also improved to 24.7%. 
We enter the next phase of our growth journey from a position of considerable strength, supported by an expanding 
global footprint, a robust product pipeline and a strong net-cash position. Our focus remains on sustaining profitable 
organic growth while selectively pursuing strategic acquisitions that strengthen our capabilities and market presence. 
We remain confident in our growth trajectory and committed to creating sustainable long-term shareholder value. 
Q2FY27 Financial Highlights 
▪ 
Operating Revenue stood at Rs. 940 cr, up by 30.5% YoY 
▪ 
Gross profit came in at Rs. 550 cr, up by 33.6% YoY, with a gross margin of 58.5% 
▪ 
EBITDA stood at Rs. 214 cr, up by 48.3% YoY, with an EBITDA margin of 22.8% 
▪ 
PAT stood at Rs. 144 cr, up by 44.8% YoY, with a net margin of 15.0% 
▪ 
Diluted EPS was at Rs. 3.11 
H1FY27 Financial Highlights 
▪ 
Operating Revenue stood at Rs. 1,781 cr, up by 32.9% YoY 
▪ 
Gross profit came in at Rs. 1,047 cr, up by 36.0% YoY, with a gross margin of 58.8% 
▪ 
EBITDA stood at Rs. 427 cr, up by 74.7% YoY, with an EBITDA margin of 24.0% 
▪ 
PAT stood at Rs. 303 cr, up by 92.5% YoY, with a net margin of 16.6% 
▪ 
Diluted EPS was at Rs. 6.58 
Business Highlights  
US Market 
▪ 
US & North America Formulation business reported revenues of Rs. 421 cr in Q2FY27, up 8.7% YoY and 11.6% QoQ 
— the highest-ever quarterly revenue for the region  

 
 
 
 
▪ 
Largest market, contributing ~45% of consolidated revenue. H1FY27 revenue of Rs. 798 cr, up 11.7% YoY 
▪ 
Order book remains strong despite a softer US consumer environment, supporting the outlook for H2FY27; price 
erosion in the Rx portfolio remained in single digits 
UK and Europe Market 
▪ 
Revenues from the UK & Europe Formulation business stood at Rs. 405 cr in Q2FY27, up 64.9% YoY and 13.7% 
QoQ — the highest-ever quarterly revenue for the region 
▪ 
H1FY27 revenue of Rs. 761 cr, up 69.4% YoY 
▪ 
Excluding QliniQ, UK & Europe revenue grew 48.6% YoY to Rs. 365 cr in Q2FY27; QliniQ B.V. (Netherlands) 
contributed ~Rs. 40 cr in the quarter 
▪ 
After a flat FY26, the UK market has stabilised; new launches are driving both topline growth and margin 
improvement 
Australia and New Zealand Market 
▪ 
Australia and New Zealand businesses reported revenues of Rs. 101 cr in Q2FY27, up 64.0% YoY and 14.8% QoQ, 
driven by strong traction in the branded prescription (Rx) portfolio under Nova Pharmaceuticals 
▪ 
H1FY27 revenue of Rs. 188 cr, up 59.0% YoY; ANZ now contributes 10.7% of consolidated revenue 
RoW Market 
▪ 
RoW business reported revenues of Rs. 14 cr in Q2FY27, down 47.0% YoY and 29.6% QoQ, amidst the West Asia 
crisis 
▪ 
Middle East shipments impacted; stabilization in geopolitical conditions could support recovery in the quarters to 
come. 
Other Highlights 
▪ 
Net cash from operating activities of Rs. 322 cr in H1FY27, 4.3x H1FY26; EBITDA-to-cash conversion of 75% 
(H1FY26: 31%) 
▪ 
Capex of Rs. 46 cr incurred during H1FY27; free cash flow of Rs. 275 cr 
▪ 
Working capital cycle of ~122 days in Q2FY27, improved from ~132 days in Q1FY27 (H1FY27: ~128 days vs ~138 
days in FY26) 
▪ 
Cash balance of Rs. 1,124 cr as on 30th September 2026; net cash of Rs. 1,095 cr, up Rs. 135 cr in H1FY27 after Rs. 
95 cr of acquisitions and Rs. 41 cr of dividend 
▪ 
Trailing twelve-month ROCE of 24.7% (Sep-25: 18.7%) and ROE of 18.6% (Sep-25: 13.6%) 
▪ 
R&D spends at Rs. 23.9 cr in Q2FY27, 2.5% of consolidated revenue

Mark Saldanha
FOUNDER, CHAIRMAN & MANAGING DIRECTOR
“Q2FY27 marks a landmark quarter for Marksans Pharma, with the Company delivering its strongest-ever performance. 
Revenue reached ₹940 crore, up 30.5% YoY. Adjusted for acquisition (QliniQ) impact, revenue growth remained healthy 
at 25%. 
EBITDA grew 48.3% to a record ₹214 crore, with margins expanding 274 bps to 22.8%. For H1FY27, revenue grew 32.9% 
to ₹1,781 crore, EBITDA rose 74.7% with margins up 574 bps to 24.0%, and PAT nearly doubled to ₹303 crore, already 
over 70% of our full-year FY26 profit.
Growth was broad-based. UK & Europe grew 64.9% to a record ₹405 crore in Q2, with the base business growing 48.6% 
organically and QliniQ, our new European front-end, contributing around ₹84 crore in H1. Australia & New Zealand 
grew 64.0%, and US & North America delivered its highest-ever quarter at ₹421 crore. Equally encouraging was the 
strength of cash generation, with H1 operating cash flow reaching ₹322 crore, 4.3 times the previous year, and cash 
balances closing at ₹1,124 crore. Our trailing twelve-month ROCE also improved to 24.7%.
We enter the next phase of our growth journey from a position of considerable strength, supported by an expanding 
global footprint, a robust product pipeline and a strong net-cash position. Our focus remains on sustaining profitable 
organic growth while selectively pursuing strategic acquisitions that strengthen our capabilities and market presence. 
We remain confident in our growth trajectory and committed to creating sustainable long-term shareholder value.”

Mark Saldanha

“Q2FY27 marks a landmark quarter for Marksans Pharma, with the Company delivering its strongest-ever performance. 
Revenue reached ₹940 crore, up 30.5% YoY. Adjusted for acquisition (QliniQ) impact, revenue growth remained healthy 
at 25%. 
EBITDA grew 48.3% to a record ₹214 crore, with margins expanding 274 bps to 22.8%. For H1FY27, revenue grew 32.9% 
to ₹1,781 crore, EBITDA rose 74.7% with margins up 574 bps to 24.0%, and PAT nearly doubled to ₹303 crore, already 
over 70% of our full-year FY26 profit.
Growth was broad-based. UK & Europe grew 64.9% to a record ₹405 crore in Q2, with the base business growing 48.6% 
organically and QliniQ, our new European front-end, contributing around ₹84 crore in H1. Australia & New Zealand 
grew 64.0%, and US & North America delivered its highest-ever quarter at ₹421 crore. Equally encouraging was the 
strength of cash generation, with H1 operating cash flow reaching ₹322 crore, 4.3 times the previous year, and cash 
balances closing at ₹1,124 crore. Our trailing twelve-month ROCE also improved to 24.7%.

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE 
 
Equitas Small Finance Bank Limited announces Mr. Balaji Nuthalapadi as Interim CEO, subject to 
RBI Approval 
 
Board initiates the process to identify a successor to Mr. P. N. Vasudevan 
 
India, November 4, 2026: Equitas Small Finance Bank Limited announced on 3 November 2026 that 
its Board of Directors, based on the recommendation of the Nomination and Remuneration 
Committee, has approved the appointment of Mr. Balaji Nuthalapadi, currently serving as a Whole-
Time Director (Executive Director) of the Bank, as its Interim Chief Executive Officer (CEO), subject 
to the approval of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).  
 
As Executive Director at Equitas Small Finance Bank Limited, Mr. Balaji Nuthalapadi has played a 
pivotal role in enhancing digital capabilities, upgrading technology and improving operational 
efficiency. Prior to joining Equitas Small Finance Bank Limited, he was with Citi for 28 years and 
served as Managing Director and Head of India Citi Solutions Centers and Head of India Operations 
and Technology. He worked in multiple geographies across Asia & EMEA in roles spanning asset 
sales, wealth management, re-engineering, consumer operations and technology and Global 
Capability Center leadership where he led the scale-up of Citi’s global hubs in India. 
 
The appointment follows the resignation of Mr. P. N. Vasudevan as Managing Director and CEO of 
the Bank. Mr. Balaji Nuthalapadi's appointment will take effect from the date of RBI approval or such 
other date as may be stipulated by the RBI. Equitas Small Finance Bank Limited shall ensure to its 
stakeholders and investors that smooth and seamless transition which connote stability. 
 
The Board has placed on record its deep appreciation and sincere gratitude to Mr. P. N. Vasudevan 
for his invaluable contributions, exemplary leadership and dedicated service to the Bank during his 
tenure. The Bank will determine his relieving date following the receipt of RBI approval for the interim 
CEO appointment and in consultation with Mr. P. N. Vasudevan. 
 
The Board has also initiated the process of identifying a successor to Mr. P. N. Vasudevan and will 
submit its recommendation to the RBI in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements. 
 
Equitas Small Finance Bank Limited remains committed to its strategic priorities, business objectives 
and its mission of delivering inclusive, responsible and customer-centric banking services. The Bank 
will continue to focus on strengthening its customer relationships, expanding its reach and creating 
sustainable value for all its stakeholders. 
 
About Equitas Small Finance Bank Limited (ESFB) 
Equitas Small Finance Bank Limited is one of the largest small finance banks in India. As a new-age 
bank, we offer a bouquet of products and services tailored to meet the needs of our customers – 
individuals with limited access to formal financing channels, as well as affluent and mass affluent, 
Small & Medium Enterprises (SMEs) and corporates. Our firmly entrenched strategy focuses on 
providing credit to the unbanked and underbanked micro and small entrepreneurs, developing 
products to address the growing aspirations at the ‘bottom of the pyramid’, fuelled by granular 
deposits and ‘value for money’ banking relationships.

Subject: Intimation for allotment of Equity Shares under ‘Aether Industries Limited 
Employee Stock Option Scheme 2021’ 
 
In accordance with Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligation and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015, we herewith inform that the Nomination and Remuneration 
Committee of the Company on November 4, 2026, has approved the issue and allotment of 
7,979 Equity Shares of Face Value of Rs. 10 each at exercise price of Rs. 885/- each pursuant 
to ‘Aether Industries Limited Employee Stock Option Scheme 2021’ (herein referred as AIL 
ESOS 2021) to eligible employees upon exercise of Options, as annexed. 
 
For the above AIL ESOS 2021, the Company has obtained in-principle approval of M/s. BSE 
India Limited and M/s. National Stock Exchange of India Limited for a pool of 11,00,000 Equity 
Shares, each shall be ranking pari-passu with existing Equity Shares. 
 
Necessary communication of this corporate action will be made to Depositories for credit of 
Equity Shares in account of beneficiaries, followed by listing and trading approvals from Stock 
Exchanges. 
 
Upon allotment of above issued Equity Shares, Company’s Share Capital stands to 
Rs.1,32,73,58,240 (Rupees One Hundred Thirty-two Crore Seventy-three Lakh Fifty-eight 
Thousand Two Hundred Forty only), comprising 13,27,35,824 Equity Shares of Rs. 10 each.

Brief Profile 
Mr. B.Rajesh Kanna oversees the financial stewardship of the organization, ensuring 
robust internal controls, sustainable growth, and adherence to statutory and regulatory 
requirements. He works closely with the Board of Directors and senior management in 
driving operational efficiency, capital allocation, business expansion, and long-term 
value creation for shareholders. His contributions have supported Thangamayil 
Jewellery’s continued growth and strong market presence across Tamil Nadu. 
 
Mr.B.  Rajesh Kanna is recognized for his expertise in financial management, corporate 
governance, and strategic planning, contributing significantly to the company’s 
reputation as a trusted and professionally managed jewellery retailer. 
Mr. B. Rajesh Kanna  handles financial management, capital allocation, and risk 
management with strategic executive oversight. 
 
Dual Role Handling: Pursuant to Sections 196, 197, 203, and applicable provisions of the 
Companies Act, 2013 read with SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015, Mr. Rajesh Kanna will 
handle both positions as Whole-time Director and Chief Financial Officer, ensuring 
continuity and seamless execution. 
 
Operational Synergy & Leadership Continuity: His established relationship with the 
Board, executive management, and external financial stakeholders provides leadership 
stability as the company expands its retail presence..

Graduated from the University of Warwick, UK with a degree in Engineering

Managing Director of Thiagarajar Mills (P) Ltd., Madurai.

Date of Appointment: November 04, 2026.  
Term: Appointed for a term of 5 years from 04.11.2026 to 03.11.2031. 
3 
Brief Profile 
Mr. B.Rajesh Kanna oversees the financial stewardship of the organization, ensuring 
robust internal controls, sustainable growth, and adherence to statutory and regulatory 
requirements. He works closely with the Board of Directors and senior management in 
driving operational efficiency, capital allocation, business expansion, and long-term 
value creation for shareholders. His contributions have supported Thangamayil 
Jewellery’s continued growth and strong market presence across Tamil Nadu. 
 
Mr.B.  Rajesh Kanna is recognized for his expertise in financial management, corporate 
governance, and strategic planning, contributing significantly to the company’s 
reputation as a trusted and professionally managed jewellery retailer. 
Mr. B. Rajesh Kanna  handles financial management, capital allocation, and risk 
management with strategic executive oversight. 
 
Dual Role Handling: Pursuant to Sections 196, 197, 203, and applicable provisions of the 
Companies Act, 2013 read with SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015, Mr. Rajesh Kanna will 
handle both positions as Whole-time Director and Chief Financial Officer, ensuring 
continuity and seamless execution. 
 
Operational Synergy & Leadership Continuity: His established relationship with the 
Board, executive management, and external financial stakeholders provides leadership 
stability as the company expands its retail presence..

K. Hari Thiagarajan was born on 2nd August, 1988, and is the son of Sri. & Smt. 
Karumuttu T. Kannan and grandson of Sri & Smt. Karumuttu Thiagarajan Chettiar. 
 
Graduated from the University of Warwick, UK with a degree in Engineering 
Management.   
 
Managing Director of Thiagarajar Mills (P) Ltd., Madurai. 
 
Chairman & Managing Director of VTM Limited, Virudhunagar. 
 
Correspondent of Thiagarajar College [Arts & Science], Madurai and Chairman &

Coimbatore.

Date of Appointment: November 04, 2026.  
Term: Appointed for a term of 5 years from 04.11.2026 to 03.11.2031. 
3 
Brief Profile 
Mr. B.Rajesh Kanna oversees the financial stewardship of the organization, ensuring 
robust internal controls, sustainable growth, and adherence to statutory and regulatory 
requirements. He works closely with the Board of Directors and senior management in 
driving operational efficiency, capital allocation, business expansion, and long-term 
value creation for shareholders. His contributions have supported Thangamayil 
Jewellery’s continued growth and strong market presence across Tamil Nadu. 
 
Mr.B.  Rajesh Kanna is recognized for his expertise in financial management, corporate 
governance, and strategic planning, contributing significantly to the company’s 
reputation as a trusted and professionally managed jewellery retailer. 
Mr. B. Rajesh Kanna  handles financial management, capital allocation, and risk 
management with strategic executive oversight. 
 
Dual Role Handling: Pursuant to Sections 196, 197, 203, and applicable provisions of the 
Companies Act, 2013 read with SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015, Mr. Rajesh Kanna will 
handle both positions as Whole-time Director and Chief Financial Officer, ensuring 
continuity and seamless execution. 
 
Operational Synergy & Leadership Continuity: His established relationship with the 
Board, executive management, and external financial stakeholders provides leadership 
stability as the company expands its retail presence..

Brief Profile 
K. Hari Thiagarajan was born on 2nd August, 1988, and is the son of Sri. & Smt. 
Karumuttu T. Kannan and grandson of Sri & Smt. Karumuttu Thiagarajan Chettiar. 
 
Graduated from the University of Warwick, UK with a degree in Engineering 
Management.   
 
Managing Director of Thiagarajar Mills (P) Ltd., Madurai. 
 
Chairman & Managing Director of VTM Limited, Virudhunagar. 
 
Correspondent of Thiagarajar College [Arts & Science], Madurai and Chairman & 
Correspondent of Thiagarajar College of Engineering, Madurai.  
 
Past Chairman of CII (Confederation of Indian Industry), Tamil Nadu State Council. 
 
Elected Member- Tamil Nadu State Representative of CII Southern Regional Council 
for the year 2025-26 
 
Chairman -Education and Industry Institute Linkages of CII SR Taskforce on People 
Skills for the year 2025-26 
 
Member of Entrepreneurs’ Organization, Chennai Chapter.  
 
 
Executive Committee Member of SIMA (The Southern India Mills’ Association), 
Coimbatore. 
 
 
He is passionate about classical Tamil literature & Sanskrit.  His other interests 
include photography, reading, cycling & mentoring potential entrepreneurs.

SJS’s monthly revenue crosses Rs 1,000 mn for the first time in September 2026 
SJS delivers highest ever Quarterly Revenue at Rs. 2,827.3 Mn, a growth of 16.9% YoY 
EBITDA up 23.1% YoY and PAT rises 34.8% YoY in Q2FY27 
 
Bengaluru, November 4th 2026: The Board of Directors at SJS Enterprises Limited (“SJS” or the “Company”) 
(BSE: 543387; NSE: SJS), one of India’s leading companies in the decorative aesthetics industry, today 
approved the financial results for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026. The Company 
delivered a strong financial performance. 
Financial Performance Summary (Consolidated) 
Note: Q1FY27 and H1FY27 PAT includes Rs 241.7 Mn exceptional gain - one time gain (post tax) on sale of Bangalore old facility in Q1FY27, which 
was not in use since 2019. 
Q2 FY2027 Key Performance Highlights (Consolidated):  
 
SJS’s monthly revenue crosses Rs 1,000 mn for the first time in September 2026 
 
Revenue growth of 16.9% YoY to Rs. 2,827.3 Mn, driven by 33.4% YoY growth in the Passenger 
Vehicle segment and 23.1% YoY growth in exports 
 
Steady growth momentum with 21.7% YoY growth in automotive business compared to 17.8% 
YoY growth in automotive industry (2W+PV) production volumes 
 
EBITDA grew 23.1% YoY to Rs. 896.4 Mn, with EBITDA margins at 31.0%  
 
PAT increased 34.8% YoY to Rs. 583.3 Mn, with a PAT margin of 20.6% - highest quarterly margin 
since listing 
 
Capital expenditure was funded entirely through robust internal cash generation, enabling us 
to maintain a net cash position of Rs 3,318.7 Mn.

In furtherance of our letter dated 28th October, 2026, informing about the Board Meeting

Pursuant to Regulation 33 of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements)

Company under IND-AS for the quarter and half year ended 30th September, 2026,

the Company (enclosed herewith). 
 
2. Approval of investment in SJS Display Electronics Private Limited (‘SDEPL’), a 
Wholly Owned Subsidiary of the Company: 
 
The Board of Directors has approved increasing the investment limit in SJS Display 
Electronics Private Limited (‘SDEPL’), a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company, from 
₹10,00,00,000 (Rupees Ten Crore only), as approved on August 06, 2026, to 
₹50,00,00,000 (Rupees Fifty Crore only). The investment shall be made by way of 
subscription to share capital of SDEPL, in one or more tranches, subject to applicable laws. 
 
3. Granting of Inter-Corporate Loan to SJS Display Electronics Private Limited, a 
Wholly-owned Subsidiary of the Company: 
 
Pursuant to Regulation 30 read with Part B of Schedule III to the SEBI (Listing Obligations 
and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, the Board of Directors has approved 
the grant of an inter-corporate loan up to of ₹50,00,00,000/- (Rupees Fifty Crore only) to 

 
SJS Display Electronics Private Limited, a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company, which 
may be disbursed in one or more tranches. 
 
The loan agreement in this regard will be executed between the Company and SJS Display 
Electronics Private Limited in due course. 
 
4. Allotment of 6,750 Equity shares pursuant to exercise of vested Employee Stock 
options under ‘SJS Enterprises – Employee Stock Option Plan 2021’: 
 
Pursuant to Regulation 30 read with Schedule III to the Securities and Exchange Board of 
India (Listing Obligation and Disclosure Requirements) Regulation, 2015 (“Listing 
Regulations”), read with Regulation 10(c) of Securities and Exchange Board of India 
(Share Based Employee Benefits and Sweat Equity) Regulations, 2021, ["SEBI (SBEBSE 
Regulations")], we wish to inform you that the Board of Directors has approved and allotted 
6,750 Equity Shares of face value Rs. 10/- each towards the exercise of vested Employee 
Stock Options under ‘SJS Enterprises – Employee Stock Option Plan 2021’.

Q2 & H1 FY27 Earnings Conference Call”

LT Foods Limited 
October 28, 2026 
 
Page 2 of 22 
 
Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to Q2 and H1 FY27 LT Foods 
Earnings Call. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode 
and there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation 
concludes. Should you need assistance during the conference call, please signal 
an operator by pressing star then zero on your touchtone phone. Please note 
that this conference is being recorded. I now hand the conference over to Mr. 
Sumant Kumar from Motilal Oswal. Thank you and over to you, sir. 
Sumant Kumar: 
Thank you. Good evening, everyone and a very warm welcome to LT Foods to 
Q2FY27 Post Result Earnings Call hosted by Motilal Oswal Financial Services. On 
the call today, we have management team being represented by Mr. Ashwani 
Kumar Arora, MD and CEO, Mr. Sachin Gupta, CFO and Ms. Monika Chawla 
Jaggia, Chief Corporate Development Officer. We will begin the call with the key 
thoughts from the management team. Thereafter, we will open the floor for 
the Q&A session. I would now like to request the management to share their 
perspective on the performance of the company. Thank you and over to you. 
Monika Chawla: 
Thank you, Sumant, for the introduction. Along with us, we have Mr. Ritesh 
Arora as well. He is the CEO of India and Far East business. So, good evening, 
everyone and thank you for joining us today on the post Q2 and H1FY27 
earnings conference call of LT Foods Limited.  
Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made 
during this call may constitute forward-looking statements. These statements 
are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and 
uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those 
expressed or implied.  
The result documents are available on our company's website as well as the 
stock exchanges. So, I'll start with a brief strategic update across our key 
geographies and businesses. Across markets, our priorities remain consistent, 
strengthen our brands, expand consumer reach, build differentiated portfolio, 
deepen distribution and invest in capabilities that support sustainable and 
profitable growth.  
I'll start with India. India continues to be a strong growth engine for LT Foods. 

LT Foods Limited 
October 28, 2026 
 
Page 3 of 22 
 
Our strategy is centered on premiumization, portfolio expansion, deeper 
distribution and digitally enabled execution. During the quarter, we 
strengthened our portfolio with Daawat Delight, Rozana Platinum, and new 
formats such as biryani gravy and biryani masala.  
We are also seeing encouraging traction in health-focused offerings, including 
brown, red and black rice, while our biryani kits have grown by 38% during the 
first half. Our brand investments are translating into measurable outcomes. 
Against category growth of approximately 1.3%, our branded portfolio grew by 
nearly around nearly 8%, supporting 140 basis point increase in market share 
on year-to-date basis.  
Household reach increased from 56.2 lakhs to 67.5 lakhs over the last year. 
Through our project Vistaar, we are increasing direct distribution, feet-on-
street capabilities and assortment productivity. Alongside this, investments in 
supply chain and sales digitalization are improving forecasting, frontline 
execution and on-shelf availability.  
With branded basmati still significantly underpenetrated in India, we see a long 
runway to acquire consumers, premiumize the category and expand into 
adjacent consumption occasions. Now, I'll cover the United States. That United 
States remains our largest international market and an important growth 
engine supported by strong brands, category leadership and established 
omnichannel presence and strong distribution.  
We continue to strengthen our core rice portfolio while expanding into 
convenience-led and value-added consumption occasions. During the period, 
we advanced our ready-to-heat portfolio, expanding microwaveable formats 
and continued premiumization across Royal and Golden Star and rice.  
We are also investing in digital commerce and consumer discovery capabilities 
to keep our brands visible and relevant as the path to purchase increasingly 
moves across digital and AI-enabled platforms. Our ambition is to leverage our 
leadership into rice to build a broader branded foods platform in North 
America.  

LT Foods Limited 
October 28, 2026 
 
Page 4 of 22 
 
If I talk about Europe, Europe continues to be an important strategic market 
for us. While the operating environment remains challenging. We have made 
meaningful progress in strengthening the underlying business and creating a 
more scalable platform for the future growth. During the quarter, we further 
expanded our customer base and secured new mainstream private label 
business across Germany and the Nordic markets.  
We have strengthened our presence in France and are expanding our 
commercial coverage across Europe. Together, these initiatives are increasing 
our participation across both mainstream and ethnic channels and 
substantially broadening the opportunity available to us. 
 
At the same time, we remain sharply focused on improving the quality of the 
business through better product and channel mix, procurement efficiencies, 
automation, productivity improvement, and disciplined cost management. Our 
strategy from here is very clear. Scale the mainstream business, deepen our 
presence 
across 
key 
European 
markets, 
strengthen 
higher 
margin 
opportunities, and continue improving the efficiency of our operating model and 
keep growing and further strengthening the Daawat brand in ethnic market. 
 
Overall, Europe remains in a investment and scale-building phase, but the 
business today is on a stronger footing than it was few quarters ago. We have 
expanded our customer base, strengthened our commercial organization, and 
improved organized operating performance. Our focus now is on translating 
these gains into sustainable growth and progressively stronger profitability over 
the medium term. 
 
Middle East continues to be an attractive long-term growth opportunity for LT 
Foods despite being a highly competitive and fragmented market. During the 
period, the region delivered strong volume growth, outperforming both last 
year and growth was supported by deeper market penetration, expansion of 
private label partnerships, and continued strengthening of our core branded 
portfolio. 
 
We also continue investing behind brand building, consumer awareness, 
helping strengthen brand equity and expand our consumer franchise across the 

LT Foods Limited 
October 28, 2026 
 
Page 5 of 22 
 
region. While the overall demand in the region remains strong, the quarter was 
significantly impacted by the supply disruptions, which constrained inventory 
flow into the region and a sharp escalation in the freight cost further raised the 
landed cost and weighed heavily on the profitability during this period. 
 
While we have taken active steps to mitigate these pressures through alternate 
routing, optimizing spends, and increased pricing, the full impact of these will 
show up in the subsequent quarters. Though still, we continued the momentum 
in our e-commerce business, where we maintain category leadership position 
and delivered strong growth despite the intermittent supply chain disruptions. 
 
Looking ahead, our strategy remains focused on expanding distribution, 
improving product availability, strengthening local partnership, and increasing 
penetration across both branded and private label opportunities. We believe 
these initiatives will further strengthen our position in the region over time. 
 
In rest of the world markets, we continue to enjoy leadership position across 
several markets. Through focused brand investments, strong execution, and 
continued distribution expansion, we are further strengthening our market 
share and consolidating our leadership position across these geographies. 
 
If I talk about Nature Bio Foods, which is undergoing an important strategic 
transformation from an India-centric sourcing and export business into a 
globally integrated consumer-focused organic food platform. The first pillar is 
moving closer to our customers through deeper direct relationships with 
retailers and consumer brands.  
This transition has created near-term revenue pressure as parts of the 
traditional intermediary-led business are replaced, but it should improve 
customer ownership and value chain participation over time. The second pillar 
is portfolio and sourcing diversification. We are expanding beyond rice and 
developing sourcing capabilities across different geographies like Turkey and 
other regions.  
Together with our European processing capability, this strengthens supply chain 
flexibility and enables a broader organic portfolio. In India, we are consolidating 

LT Foods Limited 
October 28, 2026 
 
Page 6 of 22 
 
manufacturing through a new Madhya Pradesh facility with the first phase 
expected to commence operations in this financial year. This transition involves 
near-term cost but should structurally improve efficiency, resource utilization, 
and cost competitiveness. 
 
Our further investment in Leev also provides an entry into Benelux organic retail 
market, particularly in breakfast and between-meal snacking and creates an 
additional platform for downstream growth. Overall, Nature Bio Foods, the 
organic arm of LT Foods, is moving from an origin-led organic ingredient model 
towards a globally sourced destination-focused organic food platform with 
deeper customer relationship and greater participation in the downstream value 
chain. 
 
To summarize, across geographies and segments, our strategic direction 
remains clear. Defend and deepen leadership in the core, broaden participation 
in convenience and value-added foods, strengthen consumer brands, improve 
the quality and profitability of international operations, and invest in digital and 
operational capabilities that support long-term scale. 
 
India continues to deliver strong profitable growth, North America provides the 
platform to extend beyond rice, Europe and UK are progressing through 
disciplined operational improvement, and Middle East is building consumer 
scale and Nature Bio Foods is being repositioned for high-quality growth. 
Together, these priorities support our evolution into a larger, more diversified, 
globally relevant branded food company. 
 
Now with this, I'll hand over to Sachin, CFO of the company, for the detailed 
financial update. Over to you, Sachin, please. 
Sachin Gupta: 
Thank you, Monika. Good evening, everyone and thank you for joining us today. 
I am pleased to share our financial performance for the second quarter and first 
half of FY27. The first half delivered healthy, broad-based growth across all key 
geographies, led by different segments, even as we stepped up our investments 
behind our brand and maintained our focus on operational efficiency and 
disciplined capital allocation. 

LT Foods Limited 
October 28, 2026 
 
Page 7 of 22 
 
 
Now, let me begin with our consolidated financial performance.  
 
During Q2 FY27, the consolidated revenue grew by 17% on year-on-year 
basis to INR3,253 crores from INR2,772 crores in Q2 FY26, a growth of 3% 
over  Q1 FY27. The gross profit increased by 12% to INR1,058 crores from 
INR948 crores. 
 
The gross margin for the quarter was 32.5% compared with 34.2% in  
Q2FY26. The change in the gross margin was primarily due to two factors. 
Firstly, the change in the shipment terms with the related party from CIF 
to FOB basis, under which the freight cost now forms part of the cost of 
goods sold instead of other expenditure. This classification is EBITDA 
neutral. 
                                                Secondly, the higher shipment cost across the major markets. Shipping cost as 
a percentage to revenue rose by almost 40 basis point, which also has an impact 
on the EBITDA.  
 
EBITDA grew by 13% to INR358 crores from INR316 crores in Q2FY26,and 
was marginally lower than INR363 crores in Q1FY27. EBITDA margin stood 
at 11% compared with 11.4% in Q2FY26 and 11.5% in Q1FY27. 
                                               This moderation reflects the gross margin factor which I just explained and a 
planned step-up investment in the advertisement to support our brands under 
new launches. Advertisement investment increased by INR25 crores over 
quarter 1 or 2.5% of the revenue as against 1.8% in quarter 1, a jump of almost 
70 basis point. 
 
We also continue to invest in building our health and convenience portfolio 
ahead of the commissioning of RTH facility in the U.S., which weighed on our 
quarterly margins. Meanwhile, the organic food segment improved sequentially 
with EBITDA of INR22 crores against INR10 crores in Q1FY27. 
 
Depreciation increased with the capitalization of new assets, while the finance 
cost was higher on the year-on-year basis on higher supplier funding 
arrangements undertaken to optimize the working capital cycle. PAT increased 

LT Foods Limited 
October 28, 2026 
 
Page 8 of 22 
 
by 10% on year-on-year basis to INR180 crores from INR164 crores.  
 
For H1FY27, the consolidated revenue grew by 22% to INR6,414 crores from 
INR5,273 crores in H1FY26. On normalized basis, after adjusting to Golden 
Star, which was not fully consolidated in quarter 1 FY26, the revenue grew 
by 18%. The gross profit increased by 15% to INR2,087 crores. EBITDA grew 
by 17% to INR721 crores. And the PAT grew by 9% to INR364 crores from 
INR332 crores in H1FY26. 
 
EBITDA margin in H1FY27 stood at 11.2% compared to 11.7% in last year, 
primarily reflecting higher shipment cost and increased brand investments. 
Brand investments in this half rose by almost 29% to INR139 crores. As we 
continue to invest in our brands and future growth platforms, we remain 
focused on driving operating leverage and efficiencies across the value 
chain. 
 
Now, turning on our segment performance.  
 
Our basmati and the specialty rice business continued to lead our growth. In 
H1FY27, the revenue increased by 27% to INR5,764 crores from INR4,552 
crores with volume increase of 11% on year-on-year basis. The segment 
contributed 90% of the consolidated revenue. 
 
The gross margin in this segment was at 33%, while the EBITDA margin 
was at 12%. The EBITDA margin in the matured market like India, U.S., 
and the rest of the world stood at 15%. On the geographical front, India 
grew by 24% on a year-on-year basis with volumes increasing by 10%, 
and India accounted for 29% of the revenue. 
 
On the international business, continues to provide significant scale and 
diversification. North America, which contributed 50% of our revenue, grew by 
21% on a year-on-year basis or 13% on normalized basis after adjusting Golden 
Star. Middle East and the rest of the world grew by 25% and contributed 9% of 
the revenue. Europe contributed 12% of the consolidated revenue during the 
period. 

LT Foods Limited 
October 28, 2026 
 
Page 9 of 22 
 
 
The operating environment in Europe remained challenging, particularly due to 
the raw material and the freight cost pressure. Even so, the European business 
reduced the debt by EUR1.8 million and improved working capital during the 
first half. In the UK, performance was impacted by the lower than planned 
mainstream and industrial volume and elevated operating cost.  
Price recovery initiatives are expected to help offset freight and logistic inflation 
and the business remains focused on improving volumes, inventory 
management, and operating efficiencies. Now, coming to the organic and the 
ingredient business. The revenue in this segment was INR520 crores in H1FY27 
compared to INR583 crores in H1FY26, reflecting the ongoing remodeling of the 
business.  
The gross margin held at 34%, and EBITDA margin was at 6%. Encouragingly, the 
segment improved sequentially in quarter 2 and we continue to work on 
improving the business mix and operating performance. On health and 
convenience portfolio, comprising of ready-to-heat, ready-to-eat, and ready-to-
cook products. 
This segment contributed INR102 crores in H1FY27, up by 8% from INR95 crores 
last year, even before the enhanced RTH capacity has become operational. 
Ready-to-eat grew by 17% on a year-on-year basis, ready-to-cook grew by 28%, 
and the ready-to-heat grew by 7% in the rupee terms. We continue to invest in 
the category with the long-term perspective. 
 
Now, coming to the balance sheet and capital efficiencies, where we have made 
a meaningful progress. Inventory days reduced to 159 days from 187 days in the 
last half year, with the trade payable days reduced to 26 days from 29 days. As a 
result of the working capital days improvement significantly to 143 days from 
174 days in the last year. 
 
We ended this half year with a net cash position of INR247 crores in our balance 
sheet. Our return on capital employed improved to 22.4% from 22% in the last 
year. Return on equity was at 15.7% and the interest coverage stood at a 
comfortable 13.8 times. Improving working capital and capital efficiency remains 
priority as we continue to invest in brand, capacity distribution, and new growth 

LT Foods Limited 
October 28, 2026 
 
Page 10 of 22 
 
opportunities. 
 
Now, coming to the standalone performance. For this half year, the revenue in 
the standalone basis grew by 14% to INR2,417 crores from INR2,119 crores. 
EBITDA increased by 34% to INR223 crores with EBITDA margin improving to 
9.2% from 7.9% and the PBT also grew by 28% to INR173 crores. PAT grew by 
INR24 crores to INR134 crores from INR108 crores. 
 
The Q2 standalone revenue grew by 17% on a year-on-year basis to INR1,241 
crores, and the EBITDA rose to INR103 crores from INR101 crores in Q2, with 
the margin moderating to 8.3% due to higher expenditures including the brand 
investments. The standalone balance sheet remains net cash positive as on 
September 26th. 
 
Now to summarize, the first half of FY27 reflected the continued scale-up of our 
businesses. More importantly, we have delivered this growth alongside a 
meaningful improvement in working capital and higher return on capital 
employed. Going forward, our financial priorities remain clear  
 
sustaining profitable growth in our core basmati and the specialty rice 
business 
 
 
improving profitability in the organic food business,  
 
scaling up our convenience food portfolio,  
 
driving efficiencies across the value chain,   
 
maintaining discipline across the working capital and capital allocation.  
These priorities are anchored in our strategies of strengthening the core, 
expanding distribution and our product portfolio, driving premiumization, and 
building efficiencies across the value chain. With this, I request the operator to 
open the floor for questions. 
Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, we will wait for a moment while the question queue 
assembles. The first question is from Bhavi Chauhan from Care PMS. Please go 
ahead. 
Bhavi Chauhan: 
So my first question is related to the inventory. What is the current inventory 

LT Foods Limited 
October 28, 2026 
 
Page 11 of 22 
 
level of basmati rice that company's holding? And what is the average cost of 
that inventory? And in Q2, our inventory is quite low. So what is our strategy 
for  upcoming season where the prices are expected to be higher? 
Sachin Gupta: 
So, I will take the first part. So, our inventory level as on September 26th, the 
paddy inventory was 82,000 tons at an average rate of INR43. Whereas rice 
inventory was at 260,000 tons at an average rate of INR60. 
Ashwani Kumar Arora: And second question, you said about low inventory. So, whatever the inventory 
we are carrying is to our business plan and is sufficient for whatever the

Bhavi Chauhan: 
So, it is expected that the current paddy arrival is around 20% to 25% on a 
higher side. 
So , what is the trend you are expecting and how will the procurement be done? 
Ashwani Kumar Arora: No, you heard it right. This year, crop '26, the prices are higher by 22% to 25% 
average, depending on variety to variety. But as far as our business model for 
crop '25, we are sufficiently covered to deliver our plan. 
Bhavi Chauhan: 
And the second question is related to basmati. So, if I look at our basmati rice 
segment So our volume growth is around 11% in H1 FY27, while the revenue

Sachin Gupta: 
So, coming to your question regarding the growth in Q2, on a year-on-year 
basis, the quantitative growth in Q2 is 11%, with the value growing by 21% from

Bhavi Chauhan: 
Okay, okay. And the last question is related to our RTC segment.  If I look at our 
gross profit margins and the EBITDA margins of our RTC segment have 
declined sharply in this quarter. So like, any reason for it? Like, is it raw material

inflation that companies stating that we are not able to pass on to our

 Certain promotions  were running in the RTH and RTC segment in this half

Sub: Outcome of Board Meeting held on 4th November 2026 – Financial Results 
 
Pursuant to Regulation 30 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations 
and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, we would like to inform you that the Board of 
Directors of the Company at their meeting held today, 4th November, 2026 (Started at 2.00 p.m. 
and ended at 03.15 p.m.) has approved the unaudited Financial Results (Standalone and 
Consolidated) for the quarter and half year ended 30th September 2026.  
 
In this regard, we are enclosing herewith the following: 
 
a) 
Unaudited Financial Results for the quarter and half year ended 30th September 2026 
(Annexure A) 
 
b) Limited Review Report on the aforesaid financial results issued by our Statutory 
Auditors, M/s. Sundaram & Srinivasan, Chartered Accountants. (Annexure B) 
 
As informed vide our letter dated 22nd October 2026 (Annexure C), an Investor Conference call is 
scheduled on Thursday, 5th November 2026 at 04:00 PM (IST). 
 
 
This is for your information and records. 
 
 
Thanking you 
 
Yours faithfully, 
For Pricol Limited

3. The above unaudited financial results have been reviewed by the Audit Committee and approved by the Board at its meeting held on 4th November, 2026. 
The Statutory Auditors have carried out a "Limited Review" of the above financial results. 
4. The Company's Operations relate to primarily one segment, Automotive Components. Hence, the results are reported under one segment as per the Ind AS 108 -
"Operating Segments". 
5. A Scheme of Amalgamation between erstwhile Pricol Limited ("Transferor Company") with erstwhile Pricol Pune Limited ("Transferee Company") was sanctioned by 
Hon'ble High Court of Judicature at Madras and was accounted for during the financial year 2016-17. The Amalgamation was accounted under Purchase Method as per 
the then prevailing Accounting Standard 14 - "Accounting for Amalgamation", which is different from treatment prescribed under Ind AS 103 - "Business Combination". 
The intangible assets, including Goodwill represented by Customer relationship and assembled work force, are being amortised over its estimated useful life of 15 years 
from the appointed date. 
6. The Board of Directors in the meeting held on 27th June 2026 have approved (subject to the requisite approvals) a Scheme of Arrangement involving the demerger of 
its Driver Information & Connected Vehicle Solutions (DICVS) business undertaking into Pricol Autotech Limited (newly incorporated Company). 
7. The figures for the previous periods have been reclassified/ regrouped wh.erever necessary to conform to current period's classification.
