Regulation 8(1) read with Schedule A of the Securities and Exchange Board of India 
(Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations 2015 (“SEBI PIT Regulations”) requires the 
Company to formulate a Code of practices and procedures for fair disclosure of unpublished 
price sensitive information (“Code”), forms as Part A of this document.  
 
This Code sets out the principles and practices the Company shall follow to ensure uniform, 
transparent, and timely disclosure of Unpublished Price Sensitive Information (“UPSI”) to 
prevent selective disclosure. The Code incorporates the principles laid down in Schedule A 
of the SEBI PIT Regulations and reinforces the Company’s commitment to transparent and 
fair disclosure practices. 
 
The Company shall maintain adequate and effective internal controls and institutional 
mechanisms to ensure compliance with SEBI PIT Regulations, including identification of 
UPSI, restriction of access on a need-to-know basis, and periodic review of compliance 
controls by the Compliance Officer. 
The internal controls shall include the controls specified under Regulation 9A(2), including 
identification of employees having access to UPSI as Designated Persons, identification and 
protection of UPSI, restrictions on its communication or procurement, maintenance of lists 
of persons with whom UPSI is shared, service of confidentiality notices or execution of 
confidentiality agreements, and periodic review of the effectiveness of such controls. 
 
Part -B 
 
Regulation 9A (5) of the SEBI PIT Regulations requires Board of Directors of a listed company 
to formulate written Policy and procedures (“Policy”), for inquiry in case of leak or 
suspected leak of unpublished price sensitive information and to initiate appropriate 
inquiries upon becoming aware of such leak or suspected leak  
 
Part B of this document has been formulated in accordance with the said requirement. 
 
The purpose of Part B is to lay down a structured mechanism for investigating, inquiring 
into, and taking appropriate disciplinary action against any actual or suspected leak of UPSI, 
thereby safeguarding confidentiality and ensuring regulatory compliance. 
 
Definitions and Interpretations 
 
Words and expressions used but not defined in this Code and Policy shall have the same 
meaning assigned to them in the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015, the 
Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992, the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 
1956, the Depositories Act, 1996 or the Companies Act, 2013 and the rules and regulations 
made thereunder, as the case may be or in any amendment thereto. 
 
Inquiry Committee  
 
There shall be a Committee called the Inquiry Committee ("Committee") comprising of: 
- 
Chief Financial Officer; 
- 
Chief Compliance Officer  

3 
 
- 
Chief Risk Officer;  
- 
Chief Human Resource Officer; or 
- 
Any other person nominated by Managing Director & CEO. 
A member who is the subject of the inquiry, is connected with the matter, has reported the 
matter, or may reasonably be perceived to have a conflict of interest shall recuse from the 
inquiry. The Inquiry Committee may co-opt an alternate member or direct that the inquiry 
be conducted by an independent external professional. 
 
The quorum shall be three members. Decisions shall be taken by majority and the reasons 
for material decisions shall be recorded. 
 
The Company Secretary & Compliance Officer of the Company shall act as Secretary to the 
Committee.  
 
The Committee shall also decide the suitable actions under Clause 12 of Code of Conduct 
to regulate, monitor and report trading by its Designated Persons and immediate relatives 
of designated persons. This Committee shall report the matter of breach or violation under 
this Code to the Audit Committee/ Board, in accordance with this Policy. Further, such 
Committee will also concern itself with any leak / suspected leak of unpublished price 
sensitive information and inquiries as laid out in the Policy on procedures to be conducted 
while conducting an inquiry in the event of leak or suspected leak of unpublished price 
sensitive information. 
 
 

4 
 
 
 
Part A - Code of Practices and Procedures for Fair Disclosure of Unpublished Price 
Sensitive Information (“Code”) 
 
Designation and Role of Chief Investor Relations Officer (“CIRO”) 
 
The Company Secretary & Compliance Officer of the Company shall act as the Chief Investor 
Relations Officer (“CIRO”) for the purpose of this Code or in absence of CIRO, such other 
Official as may be nominated by the Board. The CIRO may be contacted by e-mail at 
investor@nivabupa.com.   
 
The CIRO shall be responsible for ensuring dissemination of information and disclosure of 
UPSI at appropriate times, so as to avoid selective disclosure.  
 
Disclosures under the Code 
 
1. The CIRO shall ensure:  
 
prompt public disclosure of UPSI that would impact price discovery no sooner than 
credible and concrete information comes into being in order to make such 
information generally available. 
 
uniform and universal dissemination of UPSI to avoid selective disclosure; and  
 
prompt dissemination of UPSI that gets disclosed inadvertently or selectively or 
otherwise to ensure that the information is made generally available. 
2. It is clarified that information to be termed UPSI should be specific and intended to be 
generally made available at a point of time to ensure it does not lead to creation of a 
false market in securities. For the purpose of disclosure, the CIRO may consult such 
officials within the Company to ensure the correctness and credibility of UPSI. 
3. The CIRO shall disclose or disseminate UPSI (i) by way of intimation to the stock 
exchanges; (ii) on the official website to ensure official confirmation and documentation; 
and (iii) in any other manner as may be decided by the Chief Investor Relations Officer 
to facilitate uniform and universal dissemination of UPSI.  
4. All communications of UPSI with the stock exchange shall be approved by the Chief 
Investor Relations Officer and communicated through appropriate personnel under 
his/her direction. 
5. The Chief Investor Relations Officer shall also be responsible for overseeing the contents 
of UPSI to be posted on the website of the Company for the purposes of this Code and 
shall give appropriate directions for the publication of the same. No other person shall 
be authorised to post any UPSI in the absence of any directions from the Chief Investor 
Relations Officer. 
6. To facilitate timely disclosure of UPSI, designated persons as identified by the Company 
will be required to communicate any UPSI to the Chief Investor Relations Officer as soon 
as credible and concrete information comes into being. 
 
Information to be Shared on a Need-to-Know Basis 
 
All employees, directors, Insiders, and other persons who is bestowed with the information 
or UPSI shall be required to ensure that all information or UPSI is handled within the 
Company on a need-to-know basis and no Unpublished Price Sensitive Information shall be 
communicated to any person except in furtherance of Legitimate Purpose, performance of 
duties or discharge of legal obligations. 
 

5 
 
Information Shared with Specific Persons 
 
1. CIRO shall ensure that any information shared with analysts, investors, research 
personnel and other industry professionals is not UPSI and is generally available.  
2. The only persons authorized to speak on behalf of the Company with analysts, research 
personnel and other industry professionals are the Managing Director & Chief Executive 
Officer, Executive Directors, Chief Financial Officer, CIRO, employees forming part of 
Investor Relations team and any other employees specifically authorised by the 
Managing Director & Chief Executive Officer / CIRO. 
3. Any disclosures made to analysts, research personnel and other industry professionals 
must be complete and specific. Selective disclosures are strictly prohibited. 
4. Inquiries from analysts, research personnel and other industry professionals must be 
handled only by any of the above specified officials. Under no circumstances an attempt 
shall be made by any person other than specified employee to handle these queries 
without prior authorization from the Managing Director & Chief Executive Officer / CIRO. 
All press releases to be issued must be reviewed by the CIRO before being shared with 
the media. In case the CIRO determines that the press release requires disclosure on the 
Stock Exchanges, such press release must be shared with media only after disclosure on 
the Stock Exchanges. For follow-up inquiries on press releases, the CIRO may designate 
any person within the Corporate Communications team to respond to such inquiries. 
5. The CIRO shall ensure that transcripts or recordings of proceedings of post earning or 
quarterly call(s)s with analysts and other investors are made publicly available in 
accordance with applicable law, including the SEBI LODR Regulations. 
 
Sharing of UPSI  
 
1. UPSI may be shared with any person only in furtherance of a ‘legitimate purpose’, 
‘performance of duties’ or ‘discharge of legal obligations’ in accordance with the SEBI 
PIT Regulations and execution of confidentiality agreement with the person to whom 
such information is being shared.  
2. UPSI shall be shared only after satisfaction that (i) sharing is necessary, (ii) recipient is 
subject to confidentiality obligations, and (iii) corresponding entries have been made 
in the Structured Digital Database. 
3. UPSI may be shared only after the recipient is made subject to appropriate 
confidentiality obligations through a confidentiality agreement or service of a 
confidentiality notice, as applicable. 
4. UPSI in relation to the Company and its Securities may be communicated, provided, 
allowed access to or procured, in connection with a transaction in compliance with 
Regulation 3(3) of the Regulations.  
5. The Compliance Officer shall ensure that a structured digital database is maintained 
containing the nature of UPSI and the names of such persons who have shared the 
information and also the names of such persons with whom information is shared along 
with the Permanent Account Number or any other identifier authorized by law where 
Permanent Account Number is not available. Irrespective of whether UPSI is shared 
internally or externally, necessary recording should be made in SDD. The SDD shall not 
be outsourced and shall be maintained internally with adequate internal controls and 
checks such as time stamping and audit trails to ensure non-tampering of the database. 
UPSI which are not emanating from within the Company may be entered in Structured 
Digital Database, not later than two (2) calendar days from the receipt of such 
information.  
6. Any person who receives information as a ‘legitimate purpose’ will be considered an 
insider for the purpose of the SEBI PIT Regulations and due notice shall be given to such 

6 
 
persons, who shall be responsible for maintaining confidentiality of such UPSI. Any 
person who receives UPSI for legitimate purpose shall also be served a notice prior to 
sharing of UPSI making them aware of nature of the information, the obligation to 
maintain confidentiality in compliance with the SEBI PIT Regulations and liabilities 
attached thereto in case of misuse or unauthorized disclosure / leakage of that 
information.  
 
Policy for Determination of “Legitimate Purpose” in relation to communication of 
UPSI  
 
“Legitimate purpose” shall include the following: 
a. 
sharing of UPSI in the ordinary course of business by an insider with  partners, 
collaborators, lenders, customers, suppliers, merchant bankers, legal advisors, 
auditors, insolvency professionals or other advisors or consultants, investigators, 
media or advertising agencies, professional(s) or professional entities, researchers 
and/or analysts and its employees. 
b. Sharing of UPSI for any other purpose may be prescribed under any applicable law for 
the time being in force, in this behalf, as may be amended from time to time.  
 
Provided that such sharing has not been carried out to evade or circumvent the prohibitions 
of the Regulations.  
 
Market Rumours  
 
The Company shall confirm, deny or clarify market rumours where required under 
Regulation 30(11) of the SEBI LODR Regulations and in accordance with the applicable 
timelines, materiality requirements, industry standards and directions issued by SEBI or the 
Stock Exchanges. 
 
The appropriate and fair responses shall be provided to queries on media/news reports and 
requests for verification of market rumours by regulatory authorities after due approval by 
Executive Director(s) /Chief Financial Officer/ CIRO, subject to compliance with Regulation 
30(11) of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 . 
 
Record Retention  
 
The Structured Digital Database shall be preserved for a period of not less than 8 (eight) 
years after completion of the relevant transaction. In the event of receipt of information 
from SEBI regarding any investigation or enforcement proceeding, relevant information in 
the database shall be preserved until completion of such proceeding 
 
Amendments and Review  
 
Oversight: The Audit Committee shall, at least once in every financial year, review 
compliance with the SEBI PIT Regulations and verify that the systems for internal control 
are adequate and operating effectively. The Compliance Officer shall present an annual 
report to the Audit Committee regarding effectiveness of controls established under the 
PIT framework and material instances of non-compliance, if any. 
 
Periodic Review: This Code shall be reviewed by the Audit Committee and the Board of 
Directors as and when deemed necessary, or at least once every two (2) years, to ensure its 
continued relevance and regulatory alignment. 

7 
 
 
Statutory Amendments: Any subsequent amendment, notification, or modification in the 
SEBI PIT Regulations, or applicable law affecting the provisions of this Policy, shall apply.

amended to that extent, notwithstanding whether such changes have been explicitly 
incorporated into this Policy.

Company and promptly intimated to the Stock Exchanges on which the securities of the 
Company are listed, in accordance with Regulation 8 of the SEBI PIT Regulations.

Part B - Policy for Inquiry in case of leak or suspected leak of Unpublished Price Sensitive 
Information 
 
The Policy sets out the broad principles that the Board will follow for the purpose of 
examining any case of leak or suspected leak of Unpublished Price Sensitive Information. 
Any employee, director, consultant or intermediary may confidentially report actual or 
suspected leakage of UPSI through the whistleblower mechanism or directly to the 
Compliance Officer. 
 
No person who makes a report in good faith shall be subjected to retaliation. The identity 
of the complainant shall be protected to the extent reasonably practicable and permitted 
by law. Malicious or knowingly false complaints may attract disciplinary action 
 
The Company shall periodically communicate the whistle-blower reporting mechanism to 
employees and make them aware that the mechanism may be used to report actual or 
suspected leakage of UPSI. 
 
Procedure for Inquiry 
 
It is clarified that while an inquiry in case of a leak, or suspected leak of Unpublished Price 
Sensitive Information may be undertaken through various modes, it shall adhere to the key 
standards set out below. 
 
Step 1: Receipt of Information & Intimation 
 On becoming aware suo-motu or otherwise of any case of leak or suspected leak of UPSI 
by any insider or any person, the Company Secretary & Compliance Officer shall refer 
the matter to the Inquiry Committee in order to investigate the matter.  
 The Compliance Officer shall promptly intimate the Chairperson of Audit Committee, 
regarding the actual or suspected leak of UPSI.  
 
Step 2: Preliminary Inquiry 
 The Inquiry Committee shall conduct a preliminary fact-finding inquiry to determine if 
the complaint holds substance.  
 Preliminary findings shall be submitted to the Audit Committee within 15 working days 
from the date of receipt of the complaint.  
Step 3: Detailed Investigation 
 
Where the preliminary inquiry indicates a prima facie case of leak or suspected leak of 
UPSI, the Inquiry Committee shall undertake or cause to be undertaken a detailed 
investigation and submit its report, findings and recommendations to the Audit 
Committee within 60 days. 
 The Suspect shall be given a reasonable opportunity to present their defence (adhering 
to principles of natural justice). 
 Any extension beyond 60 days shall require approval of the Managing Director & CEO 
together with reasons recorded in writing. Where the matter involves the Managing 
Director & CEO, the extension shall be approved by Chairperson of the Audit Committee. 
 Where a violation is established, the Inquiry Committee shall recommend appropriate 
corrective or disciplinary action in accordance with the Code of Conduct for Designated 
Persons, the employee disciplinary framework and applicable law. Material violations 
shall be reported to the Audit Committee / Board of Directors wherever required. 
 

9 
 
Powers of the Inquiry Committee 
 
The Inquiry Committee shall have the authority to: 
 Access all Company records, communications, emails, hardware logs, and documents, to 
the extent relevant and reasonably necessary for the inquiry, subject to applicable law 
 Summon any employee, insider, or third-party service provider for examination or 
written statements. 
 Engage external forensic investigators, legal counsel, or auditors, if necessary. 
 
Oversight, Reporting & Documentation 
 
 
Obligation : All relevant employees, directors, intermediaries, fiduciaries, advisers, 
consultants and service providers shall cooperate with the Company in connection with 
any inquiry into an actual or suspected leak of UPSI, including by preserving and 
providing relevant records, documents and information, subject to applicable law. 
 
Oversight: The Audit Committee may seek further information, direct additional 
investigation, consider the findings and recommend or approve corrective and 
disciplinary action in accordance with applicable Company policies. 
 
Reporting to SEBI & Exchanges: The Stock Exchanges and SEBI shall be informed where 
required under the SEBI PIT Regulations, the SEBI LODR Regulations, or any applicable 
regulatory direction. 
 Record Retention: All records, complaints, proceedings, and investigation reports shall 
be maintained by the Compliance Officer for a minimum period of 8 years.  
 
Amendments and Review  
 
Periodic Review: This Policy shall be reviewed by the Audit Committee and the Board of 
Directors as and when deemed necessary, or at least once every two (2) years, to ensure its 
continued relevance and regulatory alignment. 
 
Statutory Amendments: Any subsequent amendment, notification, or modification in the 
SEBI PIT Regulations, or applicable law affecting the provisions of this Policy, shall apply. 
The relevant provisions of this Policy shall be deemed to be mutatis mutandis modified or 
amended to that extent, notwithstanding whether such changes have been explicitly 
incorporated into this Policy. 
 
Website 
 
This policy shall be hosted on website of the Company.

Company on a need-to-know basis and no Unpublished Price Sensitive Information shall be 
communicated to any person except in furtherance of Legitimate Purpose, performance of 
duties or discharge of legal obligations. 
 

5 
 
Information Shared with Specific Persons 
 
1. CIRO shall ensure that any information shared with analysts, investors, research 
personnel and other industry professionals is not UPSI and is generally available.  
2. The only persons authorized to speak on behalf of the Company with analysts, research 
personnel and other industry professionals are the Managing Director & Chief Executive 
Officer, Executive Directors, Chief Financial Officer, CIRO, employees forming part of 
Investor Relations team and any other employees specifically authorised by the 
Managing Director & Chief Executive Officer / CIRO. 
3. Any disclosures made to analysts, research personnel and other industry professionals 
must be complete and specific. Selective disclosures are strictly prohibited. 
4. Inquiries from analysts, research personnel and other industry professionals must be 
handled only by any of the above specified officials. Under no circumstances an attempt 
shall be made by any person other than specified employee to handle these queries 
without prior authorization from the Managing Director & Chief Executive Officer / CIRO. 
All press releases to be issued must be reviewed by the CIRO before being shared with 
the media. In case the CIRO determines that the press release requires disclosure on the 
Stock Exchanges, such press release must be shared with media only after disclosure on 
the Stock Exchanges. For follow-up inquiries on press releases, the CIRO may designate 
any person within the Corporate Communications team to respond to such inquiries. 
5. The CIRO shall ensure that transcripts or recordings of proceedings of post earning or 
quarterly call(s)s with analysts and other investors are made publicly available in 
accordance with applicable law, including the SEBI LODR Regulations. 
 
Sharing of UPSI  
 
1. UPSI may be shared with any person only in furtherance of a ‘legitimate purpose’, 
‘performance of duties’ or ‘discharge of legal obligations’ in accordance with the SEBI 
PIT Regulations and execution of confidentiality agreement with the person to whom 
such information is being shared.  
2. UPSI shall be shared only after satisfaction that (i) sharing is necessary, (ii) recipient is 
subject to confidentiality obligations, and (iii) corresponding entries have been made 
in the Structured Digital Database. 
3. UPSI may be shared only after the recipient is made subject to appropriate 
confidentiality obligations through a confidentiality agreement or service of a 
confidentiality notice, as applicable. 
4. UPSI in relation to the Company and its Securities may be communicated, provided, 
allowed access to or procured, in connection with a transaction in compliance with 
Regulation 3(3) of the Regulations.  
5. The Compliance Officer shall ensure that a structured digital database is maintained 
containing the nature of UPSI and the names of such persons who have shared the 
information and also the names of such persons with whom information is shared along 
with the Permanent Account Number or any other identifier authorized by law where 
Permanent Account Number is not available. Irrespective of whether UPSI is shared 
internally or externally, necessary recording should be made in SDD. The SDD shall not 
be outsourced and shall be maintained internally with adequate internal controls and 
checks such as time stamping and audit trails to ensure non-tampering of the database. 
UPSI which are not emanating from within the Company may be entered in Structured 
Digital Database, not later than two (2) calendar days from the receipt of such 
information.  
6. Any person who receives information as a ‘legitimate purpose’ will be considered an 
insider for the purpose of the SEBI PIT Regulations and due notice shall be given to such 

6 
 
persons, who shall be responsible for maintaining confidentiality of such UPSI. Any 
person who receives UPSI for legitimate purpose shall also be served a notice prior to 
sharing of UPSI making them aware of nature of the information, the obligation to 
maintain confidentiality in compliance with the SEBI PIT Regulations and liabilities 
attached thereto in case of misuse or unauthorized disclosure / leakage of that 
information.  
 
Policy for Determination of “Legitimate Purpose” in relation to communication of 
UPSI  
 
“Legitimate purpose” shall include the following: 
a. 
sharing of UPSI in the ordinary course of business by an insider with  partners, 
collaborators, lenders, customers, suppliers, merchant bankers, legal advisors, 
auditors, insolvency professionals or other advisors or consultants, investigators, 
media or advertising agencies, professional(s) or professional entities, researchers 
and/or analysts and its employees. 
b. Sharing of UPSI for any other purpose may be prescribed under any applicable law for 
the time being in force, in this behalf, as may be amended from time to time.  
 
Provided that such sharing has not been carried out to evade or circumvent the prohibitions 
of the Regulations.  
 
Market Rumours  
 
The Company shall confirm, deny or clarify market rumours where required under 
Regulation 30(11) of the SEBI LODR Regulations and in accordance with the applicable 
timelines, materiality requirements, industry standards and directions issued by SEBI or the 
Stock Exchanges. 
 
The appropriate and fair responses shall be provided to queries on media/news reports and 
requests for verification of market rumours by regulatory authorities after due approval by 
Executive Director(s) /Chief Financial Officer/ CIRO, subject to compliance with Regulation 
30(11) of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 . 
 
Record Retention  
 
The Structured Digital Database shall be preserved for a period of not less than 8 (eight) 
years after completion of the relevant transaction. In the event of receipt of information 
from SEBI regarding any investigation or enforcement proceeding, relevant information in 
the database shall be preserved until completion of such proceeding 
 
Amendments and Review  
 
Oversight: The Audit Committee shall, at least once in every financial year, review 
compliance with the SEBI PIT Regulations and verify that the systems for internal control 
are adequate and operating effectively. The Compliance Officer shall present an annual 
report to the Audit Committee regarding effectiveness of controls established under the 
PIT framework and material instances of non-compliance, if any. 
 
Periodic Review: This Code shall be reviewed by the Audit Committee and the Board of 
Directors as and when deemed necessary, or at least once every two (2) years, to ensure its 
continued relevance and regulatory alignment. 

7 
 
 
Statutory Amendments: Any subsequent amendment, notification, or modification in the 
SEBI PIT Regulations, or applicable law affecting the provisions of this Policy, shall apply. 
The relevant provisions of this Policy shall be deemed to be mutatis mutandis modified or 
amended to that extent, notwithstanding whether such changes have been explicitly 
incorporated into this Policy. 
 
Disclosure: Every amendment thereto shall be published on the official website of the 
Company and promptly intimated to the Stock Exchanges on which the securities of the 
Company are listed, in accordance with Regulation 8 of the SEBI PIT Regulations. 
 
 
 

8 
 
 
Part B - Policy for Inquiry in case of leak or suspected leak of Unpublished Price Sensitive 
Information 
 
The Policy sets out the broad principles that the Board will follow for the purpose of 
examining any case of leak or suspected leak of Unpublished Price Sensitive Information. 
Any employee, director, consultant or intermediary may confidentially report actual or 
suspected leakage of UPSI through the whistleblower mechanism or directly to the 
Compliance Officer. 
 
No person who makes a report in good faith shall be subjected to retaliation. The identity 
of the complainant shall be protected to the extent reasonably practicable and permitted 
by law. Malicious or knowingly false complaints may attract disciplinary action 
 
The Company shall periodically communicate the whistle-blower reporting mechanism to 
employees and make them aware that the mechanism may be used to report actual or 
suspected leakage of UPSI. 
 
Procedure for Inquiry 
 
It is clarified that while an inquiry in case of a leak, or suspected leak of Unpublished Price 
Sensitive Information may be undertaken through various modes, it shall adhere to the key 
standards set out below. 
 
Step 1: Receipt of Information & Intimation 
 On becoming aware suo-motu or otherwise of any case of leak or suspected leak of UPSI 
by any insider or any person, the Company Secretary & Compliance Officer shall refer 
the matter to the Inquiry Committee in order to investigate the matter.  
 The Compliance Officer shall promptly intimate the Chairperson of Audit Committee, 
regarding the actual or suspected leak of UPSI.  
 
Step 2: Preliminary Inquiry 
 The Inquiry Committee shall conduct a preliminary fact-finding inquiry to determine if 
the complaint holds substance.  
 Preliminary findings shall be submitted to the Audit Committee within 15 working days 
from the date of receipt of the complaint.  
Step 3: Detailed Investigation 
 
Where the preliminary inquiry indicates a prima facie case of leak or suspected leak of 
UPSI, the Inquiry Committee shall undertake or cause to be undertaken a detailed 
investigation and submit its report, findings and recommendations to the Audit 
Committee within 60 days. 
 The Suspect shall be given a reasonable opportunity to present their defence (adhering 
to principles of natural justice). 
 Any extension beyond 60 days shall require approval of the Managing Director & CEO 
together with reasons recorded in writing. Where the matter involves the Managing 
Director & CEO, the extension shall be approved by Chairperson of the Audit Committee. 
 Where a violation is established, the Inquiry Committee shall recommend appropriate 
corrective or disciplinary action in accordance with the Code of Conduct for Designated 
Persons, the employee disciplinary framework and applicable law. Material violations 
shall be reported to the Audit Committee / Board of Directors wherever required. 
 

9 
 
Powers of the Inquiry Committee 
 
The Inquiry Committee shall have the authority to: 
 Access all Company records, communications, emails, hardware logs, and documents, to 
the extent relevant and reasonably necessary for the inquiry, subject to applicable law 
 Summon any employee, insider, or third-party service provider for examination or 
written statements. 
 Engage external forensic investigators, legal counsel, or auditors, if necessary. 
 
Oversight, Reporting & Documentation 
 
 
Obligation : All relevant employees, directors, intermediaries, fiduciaries, advisers, 
consultants and service providers shall cooperate with the Company in connection with 
any inquiry into an actual or suspected leak of UPSI, including by preserving and 
providing relevant records, documents and information, subject to applicable law. 
 
Oversight: The Audit Committee may seek further information, direct additional 
investigation, consider the findings and recommend or approve corrective and 
disciplinary action in accordance with applicable Company policies. 
 
Reporting to SEBI & Exchanges: The Stock Exchanges and SEBI shall be informed where 
required under the SEBI PIT Regulations, the SEBI LODR Regulations, or any applicable 
regulatory direction. 
 Record Retention: All records, complaints, proceedings, and investigation reports shall 
be maintained by the Compliance Officer for a minimum period of 8 years.  
 
Amendments and Review  
 
Periodic Review: This Policy shall be reviewed by the Audit Committee and the Board of 
Directors as and when deemed necessary, or at least once every two (2) years, to ensure its 
continued relevance and regulatory alignment. 
 
Statutory Amendments: Any subsequent amendment, notification, or modification in the 
SEBI PIT Regulations, or applicable law affecting the provisions of this Policy, shall apply. 
The relevant provisions of this Policy shall be deemed to be mutatis mutandis modified or 
amended to that extent, notwithstanding whether such changes have been explicitly 
incorporated into this Policy. 
 
Website 
 
This policy shall be hosted on website of the Company.

MD & CEO Commentary on H1'FY2027 Performance 
As H1’FY2027 draws to a close, the Indian economy continues to build on its robust performance, with a strong growth forecast of 7.1%1 
for FY2027. The General Insurance sector grew by 8.9% in Gross Direct Premium, accelerating from 7.3% in H1’FY2026. The Health segment 
(including PA) demonstrated a stellar 20.7% growth, up from 9.5% in H1’FY2026.
Niva Bupa grew 33.4% y-o-y on 1/n basis, to achieve GWP ₹ 4,634 crore in H1’FY2027. PAT for H1'FY2027 was ₹ 273.4 crore, more than 
doubling from ₹ 132.0 crore in H1’FY2026 as per Ind AS reporting. Combined insurance service ratio (CISR) for H1'FY2027 was 99.5% 
compared to 103.1% in H1’FY2026. Our H1'FY2027 Retail Health market share is at 11.0%, improving from 9.9% in H1’FY2026.
Niva Bupa served as the Official Health Insurance Principal Partner for Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games. At Shark Awards’26, Niva
Bupa won awards for New Product Launch & Occasion Marketing. We also won 3 awards at FiNOVATE BFSI Awards for “Most Effective 
Launch”, ”Most Effective 360 degree Marketing Campaign” & “Most Effective Holiday, Seasonal & Festival Marketing”. 
Our culture of continuous learning was celebrated at EduSkills Summit 2026, where we received the INFINIA Outstanding Learning 
Organization 2026 honor.
Our Weighted Episodal NPS for H1'FY2027 was 63, an improvement of 6 points over H1’FY2026, reflecting our continued pursuit of service 
excellence.

Mumbai, November 3, 2026: Burger King India brings the excitement of ‘Avengers: Doomsday'

opening remarks. Over to you, sir. 
Rashesh Gogri: 
Good evening and thank you for joining us today to discuss Aarti Pharmalabs second 
quarter and half-year results for financial year 2027. The investor presentation relating 
to today's results has been filed with the exchanges and is available on our website for 
your reference. We continue to make healthy progress in all our business segments and 
are executing well on our growth strategy.  
With a clear focus on near-term opportunities, we aim to further solidify our standing 
as a preferred partner in the global pharmaceutical supply chain. Moving on to our 
standalone financial for Q2 FY27, Aarti Pharmalabs maintained strong momentum 
delivering its highest ever quarterly revenue of INR613 crores as compared to INR417 
crores, which is 47% increase Y-o-Y basis.  
The EBITDA was INR136 crores as compared to INR74 crores in the corresponding 
previous period of the previous year and that is an increase of 84% Y-o-Y. The profit 
after tax for the Q2 financial year 27 was INR66 crores as compared to INR24 crores 
a year back, which is which was 2.75x the increase on last year's low base.  
The EBITDA margins have remained healthy at 22.2% as compared to 17.7% in the 
same quarter last year. Now, I would like to tell you about the specific of the businesses 
in Q2 FY27. The xanthine derivatives and allied product segment contributed to 50% 
of the turnover. The volume split between the beverages and others was 62% and 38% 
respectively.

41% with local sales. Due to geopolitical turmoil, the raw material costs have stayed

elevated and we are passing on the raw material increase to our customers. The API 
and intermediate business clocked 30% of the turnover.

market and 10% for the non-regulated market. Benefiting from the recent capacity 
expansion undertaken in the steroidal API, we have recorded healthy sales in this 
quarter. The third segment CDMO/CMO has contributed to 13% of the revenue in this 
quarter and we are presently working with 23 customers.  
The number of active projects now is 59, out of which 39 projects are in commercial 
stages and 20 are under different stages of development, both at customers end. We 
remain on track to achieve our target of 40% to 50% revenue growth over last year on 
this business segment. The balance 6% turnover was other sales, which includes 
trading sales, export incentives and solvent and other scrap sales.

Atali dedicated block, that is block number two has been done and we target to 
commercialize this block in the H2 FY28. The ramp-up of xanthine expanded capacity 
is progressing and we plan to achieve the full capacity by the end of FY27 and we will 
achieve the utilization sequentially in the next year.  
The capacity expansion of the steroid block of API plant was completed and it has 
started contributing to the production and the revenue. I would like to share a few 
words about the strategic outlook. Building over 25 years technical expertise and heavy 
investments over last 3 years, 4 years, Aarti Pharmalabs has established a solid 
foundation to transition into robust multipillar global pharmaceutical partner. The 
mature xanthine derivative segment, where we hold a dominant market position, 
continues to serve as a cash cow. The company is also geared up to accelerate growth 
led by its high growth CDMO/CMO pillar, followed by API and intermediate segment.

addition still underway in the medium term, Aarti Pharmalabs is well positioned to 
deepen its global partnerships and drive substantial long-term value creation.

Kirloskar Brothers Limited 
 
 
October 28, 2026

Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to the Kirloskar Brothers Limited Q2 and 
H1FY27 Earnings Conference Call. This conference call may contain forward-looking 
statements about the company, which are based on beliefs, opinions and expectations of the 
company as on date of this call. These statements are not the guarantee of future performance 
and involve risks and uncertainties that are difficult to predict. 
 
As a reminder, all participants will be in listen-only mode, and there will be an opportunity for 
you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need assistance during the 
conference call, please signal an operator by pressing star then zero on your touch-tone phone. 
 
I now hand the conference over to Mr. Sanjay Kirloskar, Chairman and Managing Director from 
Kirloskar Brothers Limited. Thank you, and over to you, sir. 
Sanjay Kirloskar: 
Thank you. Good afternoon, everyone. On behalf of Kirloskar Brothers Limited, I extend a very 
warm welcome to all of you joining us on our call today. I hope everyone had an opportunity to 
go through the financial results and the investor presentation, which have been uploaded on the 
stock exchanges and the company's website. 
 
On this call with me, I have Mr. Alok Kirloskar, Managing Director, Kirloskar Brothers 
International B.V.; Rama Kirloskar, Joint Managing Director, KBL and MD KEPL; Mr. 
Bhavesh Chheda, Chief Financial Officer; Mr. Devang Trivedi, our Company Secretary; and 
Strategic Growth Advisors, our Investor Relations Advisors. 
 
Let me begin with my remarks by giving some business highlights. I'm pleased to report that 
during the quarter, consolidated revenues grew by 24% on a year-on-year basis, reaching 
Rs.12,767 million. And for H1, our consolidated revenues grew by 19% on a year-on-year basis, 
reaching Rs.23,816 million. This increase underscores the strong demand for our products and 
services across various segments, both domestically and internationally. 
 
EBITDA for the quarter grew by 16% on a year-on-year basis, reaching Rs.1,432 million with 
EBITDA margin standing at 11.2%. EBITDA for H1 '27 grew by 9%, reaching Rs.2,738 million 
with an EBITDA margin of 11.5%. 
 
During the quarter, we also recorded healthy order inflows across both domestic and 
international markets. Our consolidated order intake grew by 68% year-on-year to Rs.20,472 
million, providing continued visibility for future growth. 
 
Turning to our standalone domestic business. For Q2 FY27, revenue increased by 23% year-on-
year to Rs.7,991 million, while EBITDA grew by 37% to Rs.937 million. Profit after tax stood 
at Rs.544 million, reflecting a 45% year-on-year growth. 
 
Our healthy order book, coupled with our focused approach towards high potential business 
opportunities, provides us with confidence in our growth outlook. We remain confident of 
delivering double-digit revenue growth in FY27 over FY26 for our standalone businesses. 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Kirloskar Brothers Limited 
 
 
October 28, 2026 
 
Page 3 of 16 
 
 
As of September 2026, order book on the domestic front grew by 29% on a year-on-year basis, 
reaching Rs.29,264 million, which, as you know, excludes the small pumps order book reflecting 
a strong pipeline. Furthermore, we are seeing good order inflows across segments. 
 
On the international front, we reported 24% year-on-year growth in revenue during Q2FY27. 
This performance was primarily driven by strong execution across SPP U.K., SPP USA and the 
Dutch Group, supported by the robust order book execution. SPP USA continues to witness 
encouraging traction in data centers, fire and HVAC projects. 
 
EBITDA stood at Rs.233 million with an EBITDA margin of 5.3%. This moderation was 
primarily attributable to a lower contribution from the services business, which traditionally 
carries higher margins. We are actively focused on expanding the services portfolio, which we 
believe will support improvement going forward. Our overseas pending order book stood at 
Rs.17,013 million, reflecting a growth of 32%, providing strong visibility for the coming 
quarters. 
 
Looking ahead, we are very optimistic about the company's growth trajectory backed by a 
healthy mix of domestic and international business, a robust order pipeline and continued focus 
on operational excellence. Our company is well positioned to deliver sustainable growth in the 
periods ahead. This is all. 
 
We can now begin the question-and-answer session. Thank you. 
Moderator: 
Thank you so much, sir. Ladies and gentlemen, we will now begin the question-and-answer 
session. Our first question comes from the line of Mahesh Bendre with LIC Mutual Fund. 
Mahesh Bendre: 
Very strong performance on sales side and the order intake given the current environment. Sir, 
I have two questions. First is on margin side. In this quarter, I think domestically, we have done 
really well. But it's international pieces, which is actually lagging in terms of margin. So do you 
anticipate recovery to happen in the second half? 
Sanjay Kirloskar: 
Margins to go up in the second half. 
Mahesh Bendre: 
Sorry, sir, I didn't... 
Sanjay Kirloskar: 
I said, yes, we do expect margins to go up in the second half as usual. But for the international 
business, and I'll ask Alok to explain it a little more, we are now in our third quarter and the 
current quarter will be the fourth quarter for them because they follow the calendar year as their 
financial year. 
Alok Kirloskar: 
Just to add to that, I think one point which was mentioned at the start was that the mix this year 
has been slower in the U.K. for services. I have mentioned in previous analyst calls that we have, 
from an order point of view, bagged many more service contracts. But as I also said, it takes 
some time for us to finish the site evaluation and kick off the contract. 
 
So we do expect more of those contracts to be kicked off in the current quarter, but definitely in 
KBL's fourth quarter, which is, of course, the first quarter of the international companies from 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Kirloskar Brothers Limited 
 
 
October 28, 2026 
 
Page 4 of 16 
 
Jan to March. So I think that's the reason why it was mentioned earlier that the second half should 
have stronger margins. 
Mahesh Bendre: 
Sure. And sir, the order intake has been very strong for the domestic as well as international 
operations. So is there anything -- I mean, we have observed in terms of such a -- I mean, given 
the current business environment, these numbers are very strong. So anything you would like to 
share on this? 
Sanjay Kirloskar: 
I've always said that we shouldn't look at this company from quarter-to-quarter. And I have 
mentioned many times that sometimes large orders get delayed and I think I mentioned that last 
time. So yes, the orders come in when the customers are ready to place them. So the outlook is 
quite good. 
 
I've always mentioned that this company will grow with India's economic growth. And I think 
customers recognize the fact that our products are superior to whoever else offers the products 
that we make. And I believe there's a growing recognition that not only are they the most efficient 
and reliable, but the quality is also good and they last for a long time. So I think we're seeing 
that from customers recognizing the premium products that we supply. 
Mahesh Bendre: 
Sir, last question from my end. We have seen there is a huge shortage of water in Maharashtra 
and even at India level. So at some point of time, do you anticipate growth in the standard pumps 
to go up given the shortages in the water? 
Sanjay Kirloskar: 
Yes, it should. It should go up. 
Moderator: 
Our next question comes from the line of Raj Shah with ENAM Asset Management. 
Raj Shah: 
My first question was on the margin front. Especially gross margins, if we see, it has seen a 
decline of almost 400 bps in both standalone as well as consolidated business. As you said, in 
the overseas business, especially U.K., there was a fall in service revenues. But when we talk 
about the raw material cost increase, can you please elaborate what was the quantum of RM 
price increase? And were we able to pass on if yes, and by what percentage? 
Sanjay Kirloskar: 
Specially the price of copper, gun metal, steel, which are used in our products. And we have 
been able to pass them on to a large extent. But this also depends on product mix, how different 
products with different material costs go through during different parts of the year. So while we 
are able to pass on and we are the price leaders and always the first ones to increase prices, we 
expect this to get moderated in the next few quarters. 
Raj Shah: 
Okay. Got it. Sir, relating to the U.K. business margins, just following on the previous 
participant's question, if you see the margins, especially in H1, there is 0% profit that we have 
made in specific to U.K. business. In FY'25, it used to be 12% EBITDA margins. In financial 
year '26, it came down to 7%. Do you think this year we can go back to, say, 5% to 7% range? 
I'm not asking for a specific number, but some direction because in H1, we have not made any 
profits in the U.K. business, which is close to 17%, 18% of the total revenues. 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Kirloskar Brothers Limited 
 
 
October 28, 2026 
 
Page 5 of 16 
 
Alok Kirloskar: 
Yes. I think that this year, we will have a recovery in the margins if you look at KBL's financial 
year and even if you look at the U.K. year. It will not be like the financial year 2024-'25. But I 
think that the next year would be similar in terms of margins. 
 
And the reason I say that is 2 issues the U.K. business has this year and one issue may continue. 
One, of course, as you highlighted earlier, is material cost. The material cost has increased in the 
U.K. by 7% to 8% -- actually 8% to be exact. And that's one aspect of it. 
 
The second is that with the oil and gas business picking up again, the oil and gas business has a 
lower margin, but also requires a lot more specialized skill set to be executed. And so with the 
enhanced order book coming in of oil and gas in the U.K., we see that there's a drag in margins 
on the products. And there's an additional drag in margin because of rising employee-related 
expenses. 
 
The benefits only come when the spare parts come of these businesses and that of oil and gas 
products, and that's really why we sell these products. But I would say there are 2 additional 
factors, these 2, which I mentioned, in addition to the fact that our service business has been 
down the first 3 quarters or in KBL's case, the first 2 quarters. And we only expect that partially 
to recover in this quarter and next quarter. 
Raj Shah: 
Okay. Got it. So you expect H2 to be much better in terms of margins in U.K. business? Hello? 
Sanjay Kirloskar: 
Yes, go ahead. 
Raj Shah: 
Yes. Am I audible, sir? Hello? 
Sanjay Kirloskar: 
Yes, you are audible. There's some other noise in the background. 
Raj Shah: 
Yes. So next question, sir, was on -- relating to order inflow. You mentioned that the orders are 
lumpy and it would have been from the customers end the orders came together in Q2. But this 
Rs.2,000 crores order, sir, if you can give some breakup from which sectors you have received 
large orders? And what would be the execution period of this Rs.2,000 crores order inflow for 
this quarter?

We normally don't give order inflow sector-wise. But we do give pending order book position .

Alok Kirloskar: 
Page 12 of investor presentation. 
Sanjay Kirloskar: 
Page 12. 
Raj Shah: 
Yes, yes. I'm aware about the order book, right, sir. 
Sanjay Kirloskar: 
Yes.

Okay, fine. And last question, sir, was relating to the drought situation in the country. There are 
multiple states like Gujarat, Maharashtra, even Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Rajasthan. They 
have announced drought in various of its districts. So as a business, from a broader perspective, 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Kirloskar Brothers Limited 
 
 
October 28, 2026 
 
Page 6 of 16 
 
how do you see this impacting our business? Or if you can also elaborate what quantum of our 
business is directly proportional to the rainfall? 
Sanjay Kirloskar: 
Number one, if the states are going to do something, it's going to take some time. And water has 
to be there in order to be pumped. I'll leave you with these 2 thoughts. So number one, it will be 
state managed. And historically, we do not take orders from state governments. The state 
governments will have to place orders on EPC contractors. And by the time they are ready, we 
will be ready to quote to them.

forward. Historically, third quarter for the company is a good quarter. And maybe with drought-
like conditions, the requirement for retail pumps would be good. 
Moderator:

Manish Goyal: 
I have a few questions. One on the  if we probably look at standalone growth of 23% and in the 
press release, we have mentioned that small pumps have grown 12%. So a couple of questions 
around this. One is on this 12% growth in small pumps, how much would it be driven by the

Dear Sir/ Madam, 
Pursuant to Regulations 30, 33 and any other applicable Regulations of the Securities and Exchange 
Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (‘SEBI Listing 
Regulations’) as amended, we hereby inform you of the outcome of the meeting of the Board of 
Directors of the Company (‘the Board’), at its Meeting held today, i.e., Wednesday, 4th November, 
2026, inter-alia: 
1.
Approval of Unaudited Financial Results:
Considered, approved and took on record the Unaudited Financial Results (Standalone and
Consolidated) of the Company, for the quarter and half year ended on 30th September, 2026.
A copy of the said Results, along with Limited Review Report issued by the Statutory Auditors of
the Company are enclosed as Annexure-A herewith for your record.
2.
Closure of Saregama FZE, Dubai, wholly owned subsidiary of the Company:
Approved the closure/liquidation/dissolution or deregistration of Saregama FZE, Dubai, a wholly
owned subsidiary of the Company, in accordance with the applicable requirements of Jebel Ali
Free Zone Authority (JAFZA), United Arab Emirates and other relevant authorities in the United
Arab Emirates, subject to compliance with applicable Indian laws, including the Foreign Exchange
Management Act, 1999, the applicable Overseas Investment framework, and completion of all
requisite regulatory, tax and statutory formalities.
The details w.r.t. the above event/disclosure as required under Regulation 30 of SEBI (Listing
Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 read with SEBI Master Circular No.
HO/49/14/14(7)2025-CFD-POD2/I/3762/2026 dated 30th January, 2026 is enclosed as Annexure-
B.

Tel: +91 33 2551 2984, Fax: +91 33 2550 0817, Web: www.saregama.com

3.
Approval for voluntary liquidation of Kolkata Metro Networks Limited, a wholly owned
subsidiary of the company:
Considered and approved the proposal to initiate the voluntary liquidation of Kolkata Metro
Networks Limited (“KMNL”), a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company, pursuant to Section 59
and other applicable provisions of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, read with the rules
and regulations made thereunder, subject to approval of the shareholders of KMNL and completion

Dear Sir/ Madam, 
Pursuant to Regulations 30, 33 and any other applicable Regulations of the Securities and Exchange 
Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (‘SEBI Listing 
Regulations’) as amended, we hereby inform you of the outcome of the meeting of the Board of 
Directors of the Company (‘the Board’), at its Meeting held today, i.e., Wednesday, 4th November, 
2026, inter-alia: 
1.
Approval of Unaudited Financial Results:
Considered, approved and took on record the Unaudited Financial Results (Standalone and
Consolidated) of the Company, for the quarter and half year ended on 30th September, 2026.
A copy of the said Results, along with Limited Review Report issued by the Statutory Auditors of
the Company are enclosed as Annexure-A herewith for your record.
2.
Closure of Saregama FZE, Dubai, wholly owned subsidiary of the Company:
Approved the closure/liquidation/dissolution or deregistration of Saregama FZE, Dubai, a wholly
owned subsidiary of the Company, in accordance with the applicable requirements of Jebel Ali
Free Zone Authority (JAFZA), United Arab Emirates and other relevant authorities in the United
Arab Emirates, subject to compliance with applicable Indian laws, including the Foreign Exchange
Management Act, 1999, the applicable Overseas Investment framework, and completion of all
requisite regulatory, tax and statutory formalities.
The details w.r.t. the above event/disclosure as required under Regulation 30 of SEBI (Listing
Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 read with SEBI Master Circular No.
HO/49/14/14(7)2025-CFD-POD2/I/3762/2026 dated 30th January, 2026 is enclosed as Annexure-
B.

3.
Approval for voluntary liquidation of Kolkata Metro Networks Limited, a wholly owned
subsidiary of the company:
Considered and approved the proposal to initiate the voluntary liquidation of Kolkata Metro
Networks Limited (“KMNL”), a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company, pursuant to Section 59
and other applicable provisions of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, read with the rules
and regulations made thereunder, subject to approval of the shareholders of KMNL and completion
of other applicable statutory and regulatory requirements.
The requisite disclosure pursuant to Regulation 30 of the SEBI Listing Regulations read with the 
applicable SEBI Master Circular is enclosed herewith as Annexure C.  
The Meeting of the Board of Directors of the Company commenced at 11:00 A.M. and concluded at 
12:20 P.M. 
This information is available on the website of the Company www.saregama.com.

INR 1,180 Mn (39% YoY growth) and PBT at INR 858 Mn (43% YoY growth) 
  
 
Mumbai, 04th November 2026: Saregama, a RPSG Group company, announced its 
Financial Results for the quarter ended 30th September 2026.  
 
Q2 FY27 Financial Highlights: 
Music [ Licensing + Artiste Management + Retail] 
 Music Revenue at INR 2,513 Mn registered 35% YoY growth 
 Music EBITDA at INR 1,540 Mn registered 37% YoY growth 
 Music Net Margin at INR 1,165 Mn registered 46% YoY growth 
  
Live Events [Concert + Devotional + Stand-Up Comedy + Experiential] 
 Live Events Revenue at INR 447 Mn registered 101% YoY growth, supported by 
a higher number of events. The Company continued to strengthen its multi-
format live entertainment portfolio, leveraging its artiste relationships and music 
IP to engage audiences across geographies and create opportunities for 
monetisation 
 
Video [Films + TV +Digital Series + Short format] 
 Overall Video Revenue at INR 183 Mn registered a YoY moderation of 16%. The 
Company continues to pursue a calibrated approach to its video business 
focusing on selective content investments and monetisation opportunities as it 
pivots away from own film production to investment in Bhansali Productions. 
 
Key Quarterly Operational Highlights: 
 The Company released 650+ films & non-films tracks in Q2 FY27 spanning 
across Hindi, Bhojpuri, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, Kannada 
languages, etc.  
 
 Music releases this quarter includes the super hit release of Telugu film 
album “The Paradise” starring superstar Nani, Tamil film album “Meesaya 
Murukku 2” starring Hiphop Tamizha, chartbuster songs including songs from 
Indian pop music content “I-Popstar”, and other non-film songs like “Bari” in 
Punjabi, “Aa Fariyale” in Bhojpuri, etc.  
 
 The Company added 54 artistes in Q2 FY27, taking the total roster to 340 
artistes with an aggregate digital reach of over 450 million. 
 
 The Live Events business scaled up its concerts, experiential, devotional and 
stand-up comedy formats with shows of renowned artistes such as Ilaiyaraaja, 

Backstage Siblings, Manoj Muntashir, Manhar Seth, Carvaan Live’s Sing with 
Kishore, etc. 
 
 During the quarter, Saregama collaborated with marquee brands such as Google, 
Cadbury, Apple, Tanishq, Reliance, etc. for high-impact, integrated campaigns, 
leveraging its IPs to drive strong brand engagement. The other highlight of the 
quarter was the use of our songs in marquee projects including Hindi film Hai 
Jawani Toh Ishq Hona Hai, Tamil Film DC, Mess produced by HRX Films, etc.  
 
 Digital footprint across Saregama’s managed artistes, owned and controlled 
channels continue to improve beyond 700 Mn+ followers and subscribers 
across key social media platforms including YouTube, Instagram and Facebook 
 
Avarna Jain, Vice Chairperson, Saregama India, said, “We continued to build on our 
growth momentum during the quarter, supported by the performance of our music 
business and the expansion of our presence across live events and other entertainment 
formats. Our focus remains on maximising the value of our intellectual property through 
multiple monetisation avenues, while maintaining financial discipline and investing in 
opportunities that support sustainable long-term growth.” 
 
About Saregama India:  
Saregama India Ltd., part of the RPSG Group, is India’s leading Entertainment IP 
company with a legacy dating back to 1902. Its diverse portfolio includes film and non-
film music, digital series, television content, film production, short-format content, artiste 
and influencer management, live events, and retail products like Carvaan.  
  
About RPSG Group: 
RP-Sanjiv Goenka Group is one of India’s fastest growing conglomerates with a 
significant global presence. The Group’s businesses include power and energy, carbon 
black manufacturing, retail, IT enables services, FMCG, media and entertainment and 
agriculture.   
  
For further information, please contact:  
Janvi Seth | janvi.seth@mslgroup.com | 
Swapnali Morajkar | swapnali.morajkar@mslgroup.com |

Mumbai, 04th November 2026: Saregama, a RPSG Group company, announced its 
Financial Results for the quarter ended 30th September 2026.  
 
Q2 FY27 Financial Highlights: 
Music [ Licensing + Artiste Management + Retail] 
 Music Revenue at INR 2,513 Mn registered 35% YoY growth 
 Music EBITDA at INR 1,540 Mn registered 37% YoY growth 
 Music Net Margin at INR 1,165 Mn registered 46% YoY growth 
  
Live Events [Concert + Devotional + Stand-Up Comedy + Experiential] 
 Live Events Revenue at INR 447 Mn registered 101% YoY growth, supported by 
a higher number of events. The Company continued to strengthen its multi-
format live entertainment portfolio, leveraging its artiste relationships and music 
IP to engage audiences across geographies and create opportunities for 
monetisation 
 
Video [Films + TV +Digital Series + Short format] 
 Overall Video Revenue at INR 183 Mn registered a YoY moderation of 16%. The 
Company continues to pursue a calibrated approach to its video business 
focusing on selective content investments and monetisation opportunities as it 
pivots away from own film production to investment in Bhansali Productions. 
 
Key Quarterly Operational Highlights: 
 The Company released 650+ films & non-films tracks in Q2 FY27 spanning 
across Hindi, Bhojpuri, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, Kannada 
languages, etc.  
 
 Music releases this quarter includes the super hit release of Telugu film 
album “The Paradise” starring superstar Nani, Tamil film album “Meesaya 
Murukku 2” starring Hiphop Tamizha, chartbuster songs including songs from 
Indian pop music content “I-Popstar”, and other non-film songs like “Bari” in 
Punjabi, “Aa Fariyale” in Bhojpuri, etc.  
 
 The Company added 54 artistes in Q2 FY27, taking the total roster to 340 
artistes with an aggregate digital reach of over 450 million. 
 
 The Live Events business scaled up its concerts, experiential, devotional and 
stand-up comedy formats with shows of renowned artistes such as Ilaiyaraaja, 

Backstage Siblings, Manoj Muntashir, Manhar Seth, Carvaan Live’s Sing with 
Kishore, etc. 
 
 During the quarter, Saregama collaborated with marquee brands such as Google, 
Cadbury, Apple, Tanishq, Reliance, etc. for high-impact, integrated campaigns, 
leveraging its IPs to drive strong brand engagement. The other highlight of the 
quarter was the use of our songs in marquee projects including Hindi film Hai 
Jawani Toh Ishq Hona Hai, Tamil Film DC, Mess produced by HRX Films, etc.  
 
 Digital footprint across Saregama’s managed artistes, owned and controlled 
channels continue to improve beyond 700 Mn+ followers and subscribers 
across key social media platforms including YouTube, Instagram and Facebook 
 
Avarna Jain, Vice Chairperson, Saregama India, said, “We continued to build on our 
growth momentum during the quarter, supported by the performance of our music 
business and the expansion of our presence across live events and other entertainment 
formats. Our focus remains on maximising the value of our intellectual property through 
multiple monetisation avenues, while maintaining financial discipline and investing in 
opportunities that support sustainable long-term growth.” 
 
About Saregama India:  
Saregama India Ltd., part of the RPSG Group, is India’s leading Entertainment IP 
company with a legacy dating back to 1902. Its diverse portfolio includes film and non-
film music, digital series, television content, film production, short-format content, artiste 
and influencer management, live events, and retail products like Carvaan.  
  
About RPSG Group: 
RP-Sanjiv Goenka Group is one of India’s fastest growing conglomerates with a 
significant global presence. The Group’s businesses include power and energy, carbon 
black manufacturing, retail, IT enables services, FMCG, media and entertainment and 
agriculture.   
  
For further information, please contact:  
Janvi Seth | janvi.seth@mslgroup.com | 
Swapnali Morajkar | swapnali.morajkar@mslgroup.com |

Revenue from Operations at INR 3,143 Mn (37% YoY growth), Adjusted EBITDA at 
INR 1,180 Mn (39% YoY growth) and PBT at INR 858 Mn (43% YoY growth) 
  
 
Mumbai, 04th November 2026: Saregama, a RPSG Group company, announced its 
Financial Results for the quarter ended 30th September 2026.  
 
Q2 FY27 Financial Highlights: 
Music [ Licensing + Artiste Management + Retail] 
 Music Revenue at INR 2,513 Mn registered 35% YoY growth 
 Music EBITDA at INR 1,540 Mn registered 37% YoY growth 
 Music Net Margin at INR 1,165 Mn registered 46% YoY growth 
  
Live Events [Concert + Devotional + Stand-Up Comedy + Experiential] 
 Live Events Revenue at INR 447 Mn registered 101% YoY growth, supported by 
a higher number of events. The Company continued to strengthen its multi-
format live entertainment portfolio, leveraging its artiste relationships and music 
IP to engage audiences across geographies and create opportunities for 
monetisation 
 
Video [Films + TV +Digital Series + Short format] 
 Overall Video Revenue at INR 183 Mn registered a YoY moderation of 16%. The 
Company continues to pursue a calibrated approach to its video business 
focusing on selective content investments and monetisation opportunities as it 
pivots away from own film production to investment in Bhansali Productions. 
 
Key Quarterly Operational Highlights: 
 The Company released 650+ films & non-films tracks in Q2 FY27 spanning 
across Hindi, Bhojpuri, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, Kannada 
languages, etc.  
 
 Music releases this quarter includes the super hit release of Telugu film 
album “The Paradise” starring superstar Nani, Tamil film album “Meesaya 
Murukku 2” starring Hiphop Tamizha, chartbuster songs including songs from 
Indian pop music content “I-Popstar”, and other non-film songs like “Bari” in 
Punjabi, “Aa Fariyale” in Bhojpuri, etc.  
 
 The Company added 54 artistes in Q2 FY27, taking the total roster to 340 
artistes with an aggregate digital reach of over 450 million. 
 
 The Live Events business scaled up its concerts, experiential, devotional and 
stand-up comedy formats with shows of renowned artistes such as Ilaiyaraaja, 

Backstage Siblings, Manoj Muntashir, Manhar Seth, Carvaan Live’s Sing with 
Kishore, etc. 
 
 During the quarter, Saregama collaborated with marquee brands such as Google, 
Cadbury, Apple, Tanishq, Reliance, etc. for high-impact, integrated campaigns, 
leveraging its IPs to drive strong brand engagement. The other highlight of the 
quarter was the use of our songs in marquee projects including Hindi film Hai 
Jawani Toh Ishq Hona Hai, Tamil Film DC, Mess produced by HRX Films, etc.  
 
 Digital footprint across Saregama’s managed artistes, owned and controlled 
channels continue to improve beyond 700 Mn+ followers and subscribers 
across key social media platforms including YouTube, Instagram and Facebook 
 
Avarna Jain, Vice Chairperson, Saregama India, said, “We continued to build on our 
growth momentum during the quarter, supported by the performance of our music 
business and the expansion of our presence across live events and other entertainment 
formats. Our focus remains on maximising the value of our intellectual property through 
multiple monetisation avenues, while maintaining financial discipline and investing in 
opportunities that support sustainable long-term growth.” 
 
About Saregama India:  
Saregama India Ltd., part of the RPSG Group, is India’s leading Entertainment IP 
company with a legacy dating back to 1902. Its diverse portfolio includes film and non-
film music, digital series, television content, film production, short-format content, artiste 
and influencer management, live events, and retail products like Carvaan.  
  
About RPSG Group: 
RP-Sanjiv Goenka Group is one of India’s fastest growing conglomerates with a 
significant global presence. The Group’s businesses include power and energy, carbon 
black manufacturing, retail, IT enables services, FMCG, media and entertainment and 
agriculture.   
  
For further information, please contact:

Mumbai, 04th November 2026: Saregama, a RPSG Group company, announced its 
Financial Results for the quarter ended 30th September 2026.  
 
Q2 FY27 Financial Highlights: 
Music [ Licensing + Artiste Management + Retail] 
 Music Revenue at INR 2,513 Mn registered 35% YoY growth 
 Music EBITDA at INR 1,540 Mn registered 37% YoY growth 
 Music Net Margin at INR 1,165 Mn registered 46% YoY growth 
  
Live Events [Concert + Devotional + Stand-Up Comedy + Experiential] 
 Live Events Revenue at INR 447 Mn registered 101% YoY growth, supported by 
a higher number of events. The Company continued to strengthen its multi-
format live entertainment portfolio, leveraging its artiste relationships and music 
IP to engage audiences across geographies and create opportunities for 
monetisation 
 
Video [Films + TV +Digital Series + Short format] 
 Overall Video Revenue at INR 183 Mn registered a YoY moderation of 16%. The 
Company continues to pursue a calibrated approach to its video business 
focusing on selective content investments and monetisation opportunities as it 
pivots away from own film production to investment in Bhansali Productions. 
 
Key Quarterly Operational Highlights: 
 The Company released 650+ films & non-films tracks in Q2 FY27 spanning 
across Hindi, Bhojpuri, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, Kannada 
languages, etc.  
 
 Music releases this quarter includes the super hit release of Telugu film 
album “The Paradise” starring superstar Nani, Tamil film album “Meesaya 
Murukku 2” starring Hiphop Tamizha, chartbuster songs including songs from 
Indian pop music content “I-Popstar”, and other non-film songs like “Bari” in 
Punjabi, “Aa Fariyale” in Bhojpuri, etc.  
 
 The Company added 54 artistes in Q2 FY27, taking the total roster to 340 
artistes with an aggregate digital reach of over 450 million. 
 
 The Live Events business scaled up its concerts, experiential, devotional and 
stand-up comedy formats with shows of renowned artistes such as Ilaiyaraaja, 

Backstage Siblings, Manoj Muntashir, Manhar Seth, Carvaan Live’s Sing with 
Kishore, etc. 
 
 During the quarter, Saregama collaborated with marquee brands such as Google, 
Cadbury, Apple, Tanishq, Reliance, etc. for high-impact, integrated campaigns, 
leveraging its IPs to drive strong brand engagement. The other highlight of the 
quarter was the use of our songs in marquee projects including Hindi film Hai 
Jawani Toh Ishq Hona Hai, Tamil Film DC, Mess produced by HRX Films, etc.  
 
 Digital footprint across Saregama’s managed artistes, owned and controlled 
channels continue to improve beyond 700 Mn+ followers and subscribers 
across key social media platforms including YouTube, Instagram and Facebook 
 
Avarna Jain, Vice Chairperson, Saregama India, said, “We continued to build on our 
growth momentum during the quarter, supported by the performance of our music 
business and the expansion of our presence across live events and other entertainment 
formats. Our focus remains on maximising the value of our intellectual property through 
multiple monetisation avenues, while maintaining financial discipline and investing in 
opportunities that support sustainable long-term growth.” 
 
About Saregama India:  
Saregama India Ltd., part of the RPSG Group, is India’s leading Entertainment IP 
company with a legacy dating back to 1902. Its diverse portfolio includes film and non-
film music, digital series, television content, film production, short-format content, artiste 
and influencer management, live events, and retail products like Carvaan.  
  
About RPSG Group: 
RP-Sanjiv Goenka Group is one of India’s fastest growing conglomerates with a 
significant global presence. The Group’s businesses include power and energy, carbon 
black manufacturing, retail, IT enables services, FMCG, media and entertainment and 
agriculture.

Dear Sir/ Madam, 
Pursuant to Regulations 30, 33 and any other applicable Regulations of the Securities and Exchange 
Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (‘SEBI Listing 
Regulations’) as amended, we hereby inform you of the outcome of the meeting of the Board of 
Directors of the Company (‘the Board’), at its Meeting held today, i.e., Wednesday, 4th November, 
2026, inter-alia: 
1.
Approval of Unaudited Financial Results:
Considered, approved and took on record the Unaudited Financial Results (Standalone and
Consolidated) of the Company, for the quarter and half year ended on 30th September, 2026.
A copy of the said Results, along with Limited Review Report issued by the Statutory Auditors of
the Company are enclosed as Annexure-A herewith for your record.

owned subsidiary of the Company, in accordance with the applicable requirements of Jebel Ali
Free Zone Authority (JAFZA), United Arab Emirates and other relevant authorities in the United
Arab Emirates, subject to compliance with applicable Indian laws, including the Foreign Exchange
Management Act, 1999, the applicable Overseas Investment framework, and completion of all
requisite regulatory, tax and statutory formalities.

Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 read with SEBI Master Circular No.
HO/49/14/14(7)2025-CFD-POD2/I/3762/2026 dated 30th January, 2026 is enclosed as Annexure-

ABD Records Highest Ever Monthly Sales in Festive Season 
Highest ever monthly sales volumes reported in two consecutive months, with over 3.5 million 
cases in September 2026 and over 3.6 million cases in October 2026 
Officer's Choice Brandy and Sumo Whisky achieve millionaire brand status, bringing ABD’s 
tally to 6 millionaire brands 
Mumbai, 4th November, 2026: Allied Blenders and Distillers Limited (ABD), one of the leading 
spirits companies in India, today announced that the strong volume momentum seen through 
H1FY27 has continued in October 2026. 
Demonstrating sustained market demand and execution excellence, the Company recorded 
its highest-ever monthly sales on four occasions within seven months in current financial 
year, including consecutive record-breaking months in September and October 2026. 
Monthly sales volume exceeded 3.5 million cases in September and rose further to over 3.6 
million cases in October, driving combined volumes for the two months beyond the 7 million 
cases mark. 
The performance reflects consistent demand across the portfolio, with festive season-led 
demand providing additional momentum in both months. It builds on the strength of flagship 
millionaires brands – Officer’s Choice franchise and ICONiQ White, continued premiumisation 
and wider market reach. The growth was broad-based, with contributions from across regions 
and defence market. Additionally, international markets played important role in maintaining 
this momentum. 
Underpinning this growth is the enduring strength of the company’s core brands, highlighted 
by Officer's Choice Brandy joining the prestigious millionaire brands club. Driven by strong 
consumer response, the brand has achieved near double-digit market share in the key 
southern states within the Mass Premium category.  
Sumo Whisky, the Company’s latest brand in the Mass Premium and Others segment, also 
joined the millionaire brands club in October 2026. Led by strong consumer demand across 
key southern markets, the brand further strengthens ABD’s whisky portfolio. 
With this milestone, ABD now boasts six millionaire brands in its portfolio, further reinforcing 
its market presence and product depth across key categories. 
 
 

About Allied Blenders and Distillers Limited (www.abdindia.com) 
Allied Blenders and Distillers Limited (ABD) is one of India’s leading spirits companies and 
the country’s largest spirits exporter by volume, with a presence in 42 international markets. 
The Company operates across whisky, brandy, rum, vodka and gin. Its portfolio is anchored 
by "millionaire" brands, including the flagship Officer’s Choice, which remains among the 
largest-selling whiskies globally. This is complemented by Sterling Reserve and the rapidly 
scaling ICONiQ White, which has been the world’s fastest-growing millionaire whisky brand 
for 3 consecutive calendar years – CY2023, CY2024 and CY2025. As part of its 
premiumisation journey, ABD has expanded into the super-premium and luxury segments 
through its subsidiary- ABD Maestro Pvt Ltd. The company maintains a robust 
manufacturing footprint of 41 units including 10 owned bottling facilities, 2 owned ENA and 
1 malt distilleries, 1 owned PET bottle plant and 27 non-owned manufacturing units 
(including 1 in Malaysia), supported by a pan-India distribution network that ensures scale 
and supply chain flexibility. 
 
 
For more information contact: 
Anupama Soni 
Head - Public Relations and Communications, Allied Blenders and Distillers 
Limited 
Tel.: +91 22 4300 1111 | Email: anupamasoni@abdindia.com

optimizing resource utilization and enhancing operational efficiencies translated into margin 
expansion.

On November 21, 2025, the Government of India notified four Labour Codes - the Code on Wages, 2019, the Industrial Relations Code, 2020, the Code on Social Security, 2020, and the 
Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 - consolidating 29 existing labour laws. The Group had assessed the incremental impact of these changes and considered 
such incremental impact as past service cost and presented it under employee benefits expense in the consolidated financial results for the Year Ended March 31, 2026. The incremental 
impact consisting of gratuity of Rs. 881.92 lakhs and compensated absences of Rs. 78.78 lakhs primarily arises due to change in wages definition. 
Finance cost for the year ended March 31, 2026 includes interest of Rs. 1,281.81 lakhs paid on delayed refund of IGST by the Holding Company to the Maharashtra State GST authorities 
pursuant to their search and inspection of records in March 2026.
Exceptional items 
During the quarter ended September 30, 2026, the Group’s manufacturing facility located at Bhilad, Gujarat, was temporarily affected due to unprecedented rainfall and flooding. All 
factory assets and materials at the site, besides the business interruption losses, are adequately covered by comprehensive insurance policies.  
Post the survey of damages, the insurance company has, prima facie, admitted the claim. Pending the final assessment of claim amount, interim payment of Rs. 1,499.48 lakhs has been 
approved by the insurers subsequent to the quarter end. Based on the assessment performed of the losses due to floods and progress status of insurance claim, loss of inventory of Rs. 
4,501.88 lakhs (net of salvage value received) and insurance claim to the extent of Rs. 4,501.88 lakhs is recognised in Statement of Profit and Loss as exceptional items.
