The above results of Indo Count Industries Limited ('the Holding Company') and its Subsidiaries (together referred to as 'Group') were reviewed by the Audit Committee and approved by the 
Board of Directors at their meeting held on November 04, 2026.  The Statutory Auditors of the Company have conducted a Limited Review of above Consolidated Financial Results for the 
Quarter and Half Year ended September 30, 2026.
The above Financial Results are prepared in compliance with Indian Accounting Standard ("Ind AS") as notified under section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013 ("the Act") [Companies 
(Indian Accounting Standards) Rules, 2015], as amended.
The Group is primarily engaged in the activity of manufacture and trading of textile products. Information is reported to and evaluated regularly by the Chief Operating Decision Maker 
(CODM) for the purpose of resource allocation and assessing performance, focuses on the business as a whole and accordingly, there is a single reportable segment (i.e. Textile Business) in 
the context of the Operating Segment defined under lnd AS 108.
In line with the requirements of Regulation 47(2) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, the results are available on the Stock Exchanges 
website at www.bseindia.com and www.nseindia.com and on the Company's website at www.indocount.com.
The Statutory Auditors have digitally signed (Place: Mumbai) this Consolidated Financial 
results for identification purpose only and this Consolidated Financial results should be 
read in conjunction with their review report dated  November 4, 2026
Place: Mumbai 
Date: November 4, 2026
On November 21, 2025, the Government of India notified four Labour Codes - the Code on Wages, 2019, the Industrial Relations Code, 2020, the Code on Social Security, 2020, and the 
Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 - consolidating 29 existing labour laws. The Group had assessed the incremental impact of these changes and considered 
such incremental impact as past service cost and presented it under employee benefits expense in the consolidated financial results for the Year Ended March 31, 2026. The incremental 
impact consisting of gratuity of Rs. 881.92 lakhs and compensated absences of Rs. 78.78 lakhs primarily arises due to change in wages definition. 
Finance cost for the year ended March 31, 2026 includes interest of Rs. 1,281.81 lakhs paid on delayed refund of IGST by the Holding Company to the Maharashtra State GST authorities 
pursuant to their search and inspection of records in March 2026.
Exceptional items 
During the quarter ended September 30, 2026, the Group’s manufacturing facility located at Bhilad, Gujarat, was temporarily affected due to unprecedented rainfall and flooding. All 
factory assets and materials at the site, besides the business interruption losses, are adequately covered by comprehensive insurance policies.  
Post the survey of damages, the insurance company has, prima facie, admitted the claim. Pending the final assessment of claim amount, interim payment of Rs. 1,499.48 lakhs has been 
approved by the insurers subsequent to the quarter end. Based on the assessment performed of the losses due to floods and progress status of insurance claim, loss of inventory of Rs. 
4,501.88 lakhs (net of salvage value received) and insurance claim to the extent of Rs. 4,501.88 lakhs is recognised in Statement of Profit and Loss as exceptional items.

             Dear Sir/ Madam, महोदय/महोदया, 
 
This is to inform that the Board of Directors at its meeting held today i.e. Wednesday, 4th November, 
2026, inter-alia, considered and approved/noted the following: 
 
A. Unaudited Financial Results for the quarter and half year ended on 30th September, 2026:  
 
  Unaudited Financial Results (Standalone and Consolidated) for the quarter and half year ended 
30th September, 2026 (These results have been reviewed by the Audit Committee and approved 
by Board of Directors at its meeting held on Wednesday, 4th November, 2026). 
 
  Pursuant to Regulation 33 of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015, please find attached herewith the 
statements showing the Unaudited Financial Results (Standalone and Consolidated) for the 
quarter and half year ended 30th September, 2026 along with the Auditors’ Limited Review 
Report thereon as Annexure. 
 
B.  Board Comments on fine levied by the Exchanges for the quarter ended 30th June 2026:  
 
This is with reference to the National Stock Exchange of India Limited (“NSE”) letter and BSE 
Limited (“BSE”) email dated 25th August, 2026, regarding imposing fine on the Company for non-
compliance with Regulation 17(1), 18(1) and 19(1)/19(2) of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 i.e.

Nomination & Remuneration Committee for the quarter ended 30th June, 2026, to which the 
Company has sent clarification letter dated 25th August, 2026 to NSE and BSE. The same was 
also intimated to NSE and BSE vide our letter No. IRCON/SECY/STEX/124 dated 25h August, 
2026. 
 
As advised by the Exchanges, the aforesaid matter of non-compliance was placed before the 
Board in its meeting held on Wednesday, 4th November, 2026, wherein the Board deliberated 
and noted the position of non-compliances with respect to the composition of Board of Directors 
and its committees i.e., Audit committee and Nomination & Remuneration committee and the 
fine imposed by the Exchanges. In this regard, the Board noted that “Ircon International Limited 
(IRCON) is a Government Company as per provisions of Section 2(45) of the Companies Act, 
2013. As per provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 and Articles of Association of the Company, 
the President of India vests with the power to appoint Directors (including Independent 
Directors/Woman Director) on the Board of IRCON. All Directors in IRCON are appointed by the 
Government of India through its Administrative Ministry, Ministry of Railways (MoR) and IRCON 
has no role to play in the appointment of any Director including Independent Directors/Woman 
Director unless nominated by the Government of India. IRCON has been continuously 
requesting MoR for the appointment of requisite number of Independent Directors (including 
Woman Independent Director) on the Board of IRCON in order to ensure all compliances 
pertaining to Composition of the Board and its Committees. Accordingly, levy of fine is 
unreasonable and not applicable to IRCON. It was further informed that pursuant to MoR order 
dated 13th August, 2026, One Woman Independent Director has been appointed on the Board 
of IRCON w.e.f.17th August, 2026 and subsequently AC and NRC of the Company have been 
properly re-constituted w.e.f. 17th August, 2026, as per applicable provisions.” 
 
The Board Meeting commenced at 02:30 P.M. and ended at 4:00 P.M.

prep_items.text:
November 04, 2026                                                                             LTTL/L&S/2026-27/11/01 
 
To, 
The Listing Department, 
National Stock Exchange of India Limited, 
Exchange Plaza, C - 1, Block G, 
Bandra Kurla Complex, 
Bandra (E), Mumbai - 400 051 
Maharashtra, India 
 
The Listing Department, 
BSE Limited,

Dalal Street, 
Mumbai - 400 001 
Maharashtra, India 
 
Dear Sir/Madam, 
 
Sub : Disclosure under Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015 - Receipt of Order passed by the National 
Faceless Appeal Centre (NFAC) under Section 250 of the Income Tax Act, 1961 
Ref : Le Travenues Technology Limited (the “Company”) 
NSE Symbol: IXIGO and BSE Scrip Code: 544192 
 
In compliance with the provisions of Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and 
Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, as amended (the “SEBI Listing Regulations”), 
please note that, further to the Assessment Order dated March 26, 2024, details of which were 
disclosed in the Company’s Prospectus dated June 13, 2024, under the heading “Outstanding 
Litigation and Material Developments”, the Company has received a partially favourable Order 
dated November 03, 2026, passed by the National Faceless Appeal Centre (“NFAC”) under 
Section 250 of the Income Tax Act, 1961, in respect of the appeal filed against the said 
Assessment Order for the Assessment Year 2022-23. 
 
In the Order, the NFAC has partly allowed the appeal and granted relief of ₹29.53 crore against 
the total additions/disallowances of ₹46.25 crore made in the Assessment Order, while 
sustaining additions/disallowances of ₹16.72 crore. Consequently, the tax demand of ₹19.29 
crore raised by the authority pursuant to the Assessment Order dated March 26, 2024, is 
expected to reduce substantially. The revised tax liability will be determined by the Assessing 
Officer while giving effect to the Order passed by NFAC, after allowing credit for taxes already 
paid or adjusted. 
 
The Company believes it has a strong case on facts and merits and will be filing an appeal before 
the Hon’ble Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) against the sustained additions/disallowances 
within the prescribed time.  
 
The requisite details pursuant to Regulation 30 of the SEBI Listing Regulations read with SEBI 
Master Circular No. HO/49/14/14(7)2025-CFD-POD2/I/3762/2026 dated January 30, 2026, and 

 
 
Industry Standards Note on Regulation 30 of the SEBI Listing Regulations, are enclosed 
herewith and marked as Annexure A. 
 
In respect of the captioned matter, I, the undersigned, state and declare that the information and 
details provided in Annexure A, in compliance with Regulation 30(13) of the SEBI Listing 
Regulations, is true, correct and complete to the best of my knowledge and belief. 
 
This announcement will also be available on the website of the Company at www.ixigo.com. 
 
This is for your information and records. 
 
For Le Travenues Technology Limited 
 
 
Suresh Kumar Bhutani 
(Group General Counsel, Company Secretary & Compliance Officer) 
 
SURESH KUMAR 
BHUTANI

Sub: Outcome of Board Meeting held on November 3, 2026 
 
Dear Sir/Madam, 
 
Pursuant to Regulation 30 & 33 read with Schedule III of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015, the Board of Directors of the Company at its meeting held today i.e. 
November 3, 2026 have inter-alia approved and taken on record the following: 
 
1. The Un-audited Financial Results (Standalone and Consolidated) of the Company for the 
quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026 along with Limited review report issued by 
M/s SCV & Co. LLP, Chartered Accountants, Statutory Auditors of the Company is enclosed as 
Annexure-l. 
 
2. Formulation, adaption and implementation of the "HEG Advanced Materials Limited 
Employee Stock Option Plan 2026" for grant of Employee Stock options to the eligible 
employees of the Company and its subsidiaries under this plan, subject to the approval of 
shareholders and other regulatory authorities as may be applicable as per the provisions of 
the SEBI (Share Based Employee Benefit & Sweat Equity Shares) Regulations, 2021. The 
detailed disclosure is enclosed as Annexure – II. 
 
3. Based on the recommendation of the Nomination & Remuneration Committee, Shri Hiren 
Pravin Shah, Managing Director & CEO of Replus Engitech Private Limited, a subsidiary 
company and Shri Ankur Khaitan, Managing Director & CEO of TACC Limited, a wholly owned 
subsidiary company, have been designated as Senior Management Personnel. The detailed 
disclosure is enclosed as Annexure – III.  
 
4. Closure of LNJ Trading FZCO, a foreign wholly owned subsidiary of the Company situated in 
Dubai. The closure is being undertaken pursuant to a rationalization of the Group's overseas 
corporate structure. The Group's business interests and future opportunities in the 
jurisdiction will continue to be pursued through another subsidiary, enabling greater 
operational and administrative efficiency. The detailed disclosure is enclosed as Annexure – 
IV. 
 
5. Cessation of M/s. S.L. Chhajed & Co. Chartered Accountants, Internal Auditor: The detailed 
disclosure is enclosed as Annexure – V 
 

 
 
6. Based on the recommendation of Audit Committee, appointment of M/s BGJC & Associates 
LLP, Chartered Accountants (FRN.003304N/N500056) as an Internal Auditor of the Company 
for the Financial Year 2026-27. The detailed disclosure is enclosed as Annexure – V  
 
7. Alteration of the main object clause of Memorandum of Association (MOA) of the company 
by inserting the objects relating to Anode, Graphene, crucible, advanced carbon materials and 
other allied material, subject to the approval of shareholders.  
 
8. Approval for grant of additional loan of Rs. 50 crore (revolving) to Replus Engitech Private 
Limited, a subsidiary of the Company. The detailed disclosure is enclosed as Annexure – VI 
 
9. Approval relating to TACC Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary company. 
 
The Board of Directors of the Company have approved the following:  
 
a) Revised cost of completion of Phase-1 of 20,000 MT Anode project. The estimated revised 
cost is ~ Rs. 2,350 crore for Phase-1 capacity of 20,000 MT with target COD by June 27 of 
the anode project. 
 
b) Proposal for expansion plan by increasing the capacity from 20,000 MT to 44,000 MT. The 
estimated cost is ~ Rs. 1606 crore with target COD by March 2029. The detailed disclosure 
is enclosed as Annexure – VII 
 
c) Setting up of new plant to manufacture Crucible with capacity of 80,000 units P.A. The 
estimated cost is ~ Rs. 475 crore with target COD by September 2028. The detailed 
disclosure is enclosed as Annexure – VIII  
 
10. Approval relating to HEG Graphene Materials Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary company. 
 
a) Setting up of manufacturing plant of 500 MT Graphene in two phases at an estimated cost 
of ~ Rs. 500 crore with target COD by September 2028. The detailed disclosure is enclosed 
as Annexure – XI  
 
 

 
 
Disclosure under Regulation 30 of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulation, 
2015 read with SEBI Master Circular No. HO/49/14/14(7)2025-CFD-POD2/I/3762/2026 dated January 
30, 2026 are enclosed as annexures. 
 
The Board Meeting commenced at 02:30 P.M. and concluded at 08:30 P.M. 
 
Please take the above information on record. 
 
Yours truly,

Pursuant to Regulation 30 & 33 read with Schedule III of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015, the Board of Directors of the Company at its meeting held today i.e. 
November 3, 2026 have inter-alia approved and taken on record the following: 
 
1. The Un-audited Financial Results (Standalone and Consolidated) of the Company for the 
quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026 along with Limited review report issued by 
M/s SCV & Co. LLP, Chartered Accountants, Statutory Auditors of the Company is enclosed as 
Annexure-l. 
 
2. Formulation, adaption and implementation of the "HEG Advanced Materials Limited 
Employee Stock Option Plan 2026" for grant of Employee Stock options to the eligible 
employees of the Company and its subsidiaries under this plan, subject to the approval of 
shareholders and other regulatory authorities as may be applicable as per the provisions of 
the SEBI (Share Based Employee Benefit & Sweat Equity Shares) Regulations, 2021. The 
detailed disclosure is enclosed as Annexure – II. 
 
3. Based on the recommendation of the Nomination & Remuneration Committee, Shri Hiren 
Pravin Shah, Managing Director & CEO of Replus Engitech Private Limited, a subsidiary 
company and Shri Ankur Khaitan, Managing Director & CEO of TACC Limited, a wholly owned 
subsidiary company, have been designated as Senior Management Personnel. The detailed 
disclosure is enclosed as Annexure – III.  
 
4. Closure of LNJ Trading FZCO, a foreign wholly owned subsidiary of the Company situated in 
Dubai. The closure is being undertaken pursuant to a rationalization of the Group's overseas 
corporate structure. The Group's business interests and future opportunities in the 
jurisdiction will continue to be pursued through another subsidiary, enabling greater 
operational and administrative efficiency. The detailed disclosure is enclosed as Annexure – 
IV. 
 
5. Cessation of M/s. S.L. Chhajed & Co. Chartered Accountants, Internal Auditor: The detailed 
disclosure is enclosed as Annexure – V 
 

 
 
6. Based on the recommendation of Audit Committee, appointment of M/s BGJC & Associates 
LLP, Chartered Accountants (FRN.003304N/N500056) as an Internal Auditor of the Company 
for the Financial Year 2026-27. The detailed disclosure is enclosed as Annexure – V  
 
7. Alteration of the main object clause of Memorandum of Association (MOA) of the company 
by inserting the objects relating to Anode, Graphene, crucible, advanced carbon materials and 
other allied material, subject to the approval of shareholders.  
 
8. Approval for grant of additional loan of Rs. 50 crore (revolving) to Replus Engitech Private 
Limited, a subsidiary of the Company. The detailed disclosure is enclosed as Annexure – VI 
 
9. Approval relating to TACC Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary company. 
 
The Board of Directors of the Company have approved the following:  
 
a) Revised cost of completion of Phase-1 of 20,000 MT Anode project. The estimated revised 
cost is ~ Rs. 2,350 crore for Phase-1 capacity of 20,000 MT with target COD by June 27 of 
the anode project. 
 
b) Proposal for expansion plan by increasing the capacity from 20,000 MT to 44,000 MT. The 
estimated cost is ~ Rs. 1606 crore with target COD by March 2029. The detailed disclosure 
is enclosed as Annexure – VII 
 
c) Setting up of new plant to manufacture Crucible with capacity of 80,000 units P.A. The 
estimated cost is ~ Rs. 475 crore with target COD by September 2028. The detailed 
disclosure is enclosed as Annexure – VIII  
 
10. Approval relating to HEG Graphene Materials Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary company. 
 
a) Setting up of manufacturing plant of 500 MT Graphene in two phases at an estimated cost 
of ~ Rs. 500 crore with target COD by September 2028. The detailed disclosure is enclosed 
as Annexure – XI

HEG Advanced Materials Posts Consolidated EBITDA of ₹438 crore,  
Profit of ₹269 crore in H1 FY27 
 
 
● Company reports consolidated revenue of ₹429.94 crore, EBITDA of ₹312.78 crore in 
Q2 FY27 
 
● Board approves expansion of current 20,000 MT capacity anode plant to 44,000 MT 
at a capex of INR 1606 Cr ( 20,000 MT to come into operation by Jun 2027 and 
balance 24,000 MT by March 2029 ) 
 
● Board approves crucible project to have backward integration and cost optimisation 
with the anode plant , with a capex of INR 475 Cr 
 
● Board approves graphene project of 500 MTPA at a capex of INR 500 Cr 
 
● ESOP scheme implemented 
 
 
Noida, 3 November 2026: HEG Advanced Materials Limited (NSE: HEGAM | BSE: 509631), part 
of the LNJ Bhilwara Group, today announced its financial results for the quarter and half year 
ended 30 September 2026. 
For H1 FY27, consolidated revenue from continuing operations stood at ₹725.80 crore and total 
income at ₹870.77 crore, with EBITDA of ₹438.00 crore and profit after tax of ₹269.07 crore. As 
on 30 September 2026, consolidated cash and bank balances stood at ₹1322.84 crore. 
For Q2 FY27, the Company reported consolidated revenue from continuing operations of ₹429.94 
crore, total income of ₹546.59 crore, EBITDA of ₹312.78 crore and profit after tax of ₹208.89 
crore. 
Mr. Riju Jhunjhunwala, Chairman, MD & CEO, HEG Advanced Materials Limited, said, “Q2 FY27 
reflects our continued progress towards building HEG Advanced Materials into a technology-led, 
globally competitive advanced materials platform. Our focus is on strengthening R&D, 
developing proprietary technologies and creating differentiated, scalable businesses across 
anode materials, graphene, battery energy storage and green power. Our motto remains - 
research to revenue! As we move forward, our priorities remain disciplined capital allocation,  

 
 
 
 
timely execution, customer development and improving the long-term competitiveness of each 
business. We believe these initiatives will strengthen our growth potential, create multiple 
avenues for value creation and deliver sustainable returns for our shareholders over the long 
term” 
Ms. Neha Rajvanshi, President & CFO, HEG Advanced Materials Limited, said, “Q2 and H1 FY27 
performance reflects the evolving business mix and varying stages of development across our 
verticals, while our underlying fundamentals remain stable. Our Green Power Business, with its 
differentiated model, profitable operations, debt-free position and stable cash flows, provides 
a sound financial foundation for the Group. REPLUS is strengthening its presence in Battery 
Energy Storage Systems (BESS) and EV solutions, enabling the Group to participate in the 
evolving energy transition. We are particularly excited about the upcoming anode expansion,  
graphene and crucible projects, which will further strengthen our product portfolio and 
reinforce our position in the advanced materials industry. Our focus remains on building HEG 
Advanced Materials into a globally competitive company, diversifying revenues and creating 
sustainable value.” 
Business highlights 
● Advanced Materials (TACC): Global lithium-ion battery production is expected to grow from 
about 2.3 TWh in 2025 to about 8 TWh by 2035, with non-China anode demand set to exceed 
1 
Mn 
tons 
by 
2030 
as 
cell 
makers 
diversify 
their 
supply 
chains.  
 
To serve this demand, construction of the Phase I 20,000 MT anode materials facility has 
reached 61% overall progress, with the process building at 72.25 COD planned for June 2027.  
Phase II, an additional 24,000 MT plant targeting COD in March 2029 on the existing 
infrastructure, power connection and land at the Dewas site, will take total anode capacity 
to 44,000 MT. TACC's R&D pipeline includes next-generation silicon-doped and graphene-
based anodes for higher energy density and faster charging. TACC received the CII Award 
for Excellence in R&D 2026 in the Materials, Chemicals & Textiles - Large Enterprise category 
in October 2026. 
Battery Energy Solutions (REPLUS Engitech): REPLUS has deployed over 1 GWh of energy 
storage capacity across BESS, electric mobility, telecom power solutions and hybrid  

 
 
 
 
energy applications. Alongside its operational 1 GWh Giga Factory in Pune, a 5 GWh high-
speed, fully automatic prismatic line expansion facility is under construction, which will 
take total manufacturing capacity to 6 GWh on completion. 
 
● Green Power Businesses: The Green Power Businesses have a combined hydroelectric 
installed capacity of 278 MW in Himachal Pradesh, through the 86 MW Malana Power 
Company Limited project (MPCL) and the 192 MW AD Hydro Power Limited project, along 
with a 14 MW wind power project in Maharashtra (under HEGAM). Both operating hydro 
projects and the wind project are debt-free, and the existing hydro assets generate annually 
stable cash flows of over ₹300 crore. The 200 MWh BESS IPP in Gujarat for Gujarat Urja Vikas 
Nigam Limited, with a total capex of ₹227.8 crore, has reached 64% project progress and 
targets commissioning in Q3 FY27. 
The HEG Composite Scheme became effective on 1 September 2026. Under the Scheme, the 
graphite electrodes business was transferred to HEG Limited (earlier known as HEG Graphite 
Limited), and Bhilwara Energy Limited was amalgamated into the Company. The results 
accordingly present continuing and discontinued operations separately. Current financial figures 
are not comparable to previous financial figures owing to demerger of HEG Limited. 
About HEG Advanced Materials Limited 
HEG Advanced Materials Ltd., part of the LNJ Bhilwara Group is a new-age platform spanning 
advanced battery materials with a strong manufacturing, R&D, and innovation foundation, and 
also into the business of battery energy solutions & green power. Compounding on HEG’s 50+ 
years of expertise in graphitization and manufacturing know-how, the platform is developing a 
large-scale anode materials business and future material development, including silicon-based 
anodes. Its capabilities span research to revenue, from advanced research and product 
development to commercialization, serving the evolving EV, BESS, and energy-storage 
ecosystem. 
 
Forward-looking statements 
This release contains forward-looking statements, including statements relating to proposed 
capacity expansions and timelines, capital expenditure plans, market and demand projections  

 
 
 
 
and order pipelines. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and 
are subject to known and unknown risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially 
from those expressed or implied. The Company undertakes no obligation to publicly update or 
revise any forward-looking statement.

investments in manufacturing capabilities and the selective in-house production of key products have

Dear Sir/Madam, 
Sub: Board Meeting Outcome 
 
In continuation to our letter No. CSL/2026-27/154 dated 22nd October 2026, we would like to inform 
that the Board of Directors at their meeting held today i.e. on 4th November 2026 has Considered 
and approved: 
 
1. Unaudited Financial Results of the Company for the quarter and half year ended 30th September, 
2026, which were reviewed by the Audit committee at its meeting held on even date. 
 
2. Re-appointment of Mr. Vikram Somany (DIN: 00048827) as Chairman and Managing Director 
of the Company for the period of 5 years w.e.f. 1st July 2027, subject to the approval of members 
of the Company. 
 
3. Re-appointment of Mr. Anandh Sundar (DIN: 10409065) as an Independent Director of the 
Company for second term of five years w.e.f. 12th February 2027, subject to the approval of 
members of the Company. 
 
4. Approved the Postal Ballot Notice containing the Special Resolutions for seeking approval of the 
Members of the Company through remote e-voting for aforementioned two business regarding 
Re-appointment of Directors. Details of cut-off date, remote e-voting period and Postal Ballot 
Notice will be intimated later on separately. 
 
We enclose herewith the following: - 
 
A. Unaudited Financial Results along with Limited Review Report by Statutory Auditors of the 
Company for the quarter and half year ended 30th September 2026, Statement of Assets & 
Liabilities as at 30th September 2026 and Statement of Cash Flow for the half year ended 30th 
September 2026, are enclosed herewith. 
 
B. Disclosure pursuant to Regulation 30 of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 read with SEBI Master 
Circular dated 30th January 2026 is enclosed herewith as an Annexure. 
 
The meeting commenced at 11:40 a.m. and concluded at 12:15 p.m. 
 
We hope you will take the same on your records. 
 
Thanking You. 
For Cera Sanitaryware Limited

To the Board of Directors of CERA Sanitaryware Limited  
 
1. We have reviewed the accompanying Statement of Unaudited Financial Results of CERA Sanitaryware 
Limited (“the Company”) for the quarter and six months ended September 30, 2026 (“the Statement”) 
attached herewith, being submitted by the Company pursuant to the requirement of Regulation 33 of the 
SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, as amended. 
 
2. This Statement which is the responsibility of the Company’s Management and has been approved by the 
Company’s Board of Directors, has been prepared in accordance with the recognition and measurement 
principles laid down in the Indian Accounting Standards 34 “Interim Financial Reporting” (“Ind AS 34”), 
prescribed under section 133 of the Companies Act 2013 read with relevant rules issued thereunder and 
other accounting principles generally accepted in India. Our responsibility is to express a conclusion on the 
Statement based on our review. 
 
3. We conducted our review of the Statement in accordance with the Standard on Review Engagement (SRE) 
2410, “Review of Interim Financial Information Performed by the Independent Auditor of the Entity” issued 
by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India. This standard requires that we plan and perform the 
review to obtain moderate assurance as to whether the financial statements are free of material 
misstatement. A review of interim financial information consists of making inquiries, primarily of persons 
responsible for financial and accounting matters, and applying analytical and other review procedures. A 
review is substantially less in scope than an audit conducted in accordance with Standards on Auditing and 
consequently does not enable us to obtain assurance that we would become aware of all significant matters 
that might be identified in an audit. Accordingly, we do not express an audit opinion. 
4. Based on our review conducted as above, nothing has come to our attention that causes us to believe that 
the accompanying statement of unaudited financial results prepared in accordance with the applicable 
Indian Accounting Standards (‘IND AS’) prescribed under section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013, read 
with relevant rules issued thereunder and other recognized accounting practices and policies has not 
disclosed the information required to be disclosed in terms of Regulation 33 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations 
and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 as amended, including the manner in which it is to be 
disclosed, or that it contains any material mis-statement.

standalone and consolidated results for the quarter and half year ended September 26, as 
approved by the Board today, and an updated presentation have been uploaded at both the stock 
exchanges and company's website. 
We will now discuss the operations of the company on a stand-alone and consolidated basis. 
Standalone results half-yearly: sales at INR801.8 crores, including INR15.4 crores sales of solar 
kits, registered a rise of 12.8% versus INR710.7 crores in first half financial year '26. The 
EBITDA rose by 18.5% to INR258.3 crores from INR218 crores in first half year financial year 
25-26. 
Coming to the quarterly sales, total sales during the quarter stood at INR396.2 crores including 
solar kits which accounted for INR14.1 crores. Solar glass sales stood at INR382.1 crore versus 
INR378.4 crores in Q2 FY26 and INR405.7 crores in Q1 FY27.  
There was negligible EBITDA in sales of solar kits. EBITDA INR116.34 crores stood at 30.4% 
based on sales of solar glass versus INR125.5 crores in Q2 FY26 at 33% and INR142.0 crores 
in Q1 FY27 at 33.8%. There was a small drop in margins compared to Q2 FY26 due to lower 
production. I should inform our investors that in the quarter that went by, we had a decline in 
solar glass volumes which was because of furnace maintenance and also a price decline of 2.8% 
as collection of fuel surcharge on sales was reduced looking at the correction in gas prices. 
The production was also being adjusted by the production team to correct small anomalies and 
come to a finer tuning which would eventually result in higher production, which worked very 
well. And production has gradually increased from middle of September to levels which are 
higher than at any time before in the history of the company.

During the month of October, we have had exceptionally good production, which we hope is 
going to continue for the rest of the quarter. With more positive results in the current quarter, we 
feel it could be possible to make good the shortfall in the rest of the year.  
The average ex-factory selling price during Q2 FY27 was INR155.9 per millimeter as compared 
to INR147.5 per millimeter in Q2 FY26 and against INR160.3 per millimeter in Q1 FY27. The 
surcharge levied to offset the fuel cost increase after outbreak of West Asia war was partially 
rolled back in July, looking at decline in gas prices on the hope of improvement in war situation. 
However, this was short-lived. Disturbances resumed after a brief time, taking prices of oil and 
gas to higher levels as compared to before, putting an additional cost burden on the company 
operations. 
We have recently taken steps to raise the fuel surcharge to offset this. As production and selling 
prices have normalized in the current quarter, we expect the margins to move back to higher 
levels at the end of this quarter. Solar manufacturing continues to show strong growth on the 
back of government support. 
The module manufacturing capacity on the support by way of PLI, BCD, and ALMM-I has 
reached 233 gigawatts as against annual installations of about 62 gigawatts on DC basis. Solar 
cell manufacturing supported by ALMM-II is leading to speedy increase in capacity, which is 
expected to rise to about 75 gigawatts by 2027 from about 38 gigawatts currently, as significant 
capacities are under installation. 
We expect the annual solar installations to maintain at a level of 45 gigawatts on AC basis, which 
translates to 62 gigawatts on DC basis, while other emerging sectors like EV, data centers, and 
green hydrogen may take this to a higher level going forward. Thus, solar glass demand for 
domestic installations can be expected at least at 62 gigawatts, leaving a huge supply gap in 
glass. 
In view of supply gap and its customer relationships, the company does not foresee any 
challenges in selling the additional production. Work on an ongoing 60% capacity expansion by 
adding production facilities of 600 tons per day at our existing location is in full swing, and we 
expect the commissioning of the project towards the end of Q4 FY27. 
While the existing furnaces are operating at full capacity, we may have to take Furnace 1 and 2 
for a temporary shutdown of 75 days each for rebuild, which may happen in first half of the next 
financial year 27-28.  
The company is exploring further opportunities for the next round of growth. 
Now I come to the consolidated results for the quarter. The overseas subsidiaries, including the

EBITDA of INR 0.11 crores as against net revenue of INR 0.43 crores and negative EBITDA 
of INR 5.08 crores in Q2 FY26.

herewith is a copy of the Un-audited Financial Results for the quarter and half-year 
ended September 30, 2026, accompanied with the Limited Review Report by the 
Statutory Auditors of the Company. Refer Annexure A. 
2. 
Buyback of Equity Shares of Jyothy Labs Limited ("the Company") through tender 
offer route: 
The proposal to buyback up to 68,37,210 (Sixty Eight Lakhs Thirty- Seven Thousand 
Two Hundred and Ten) fully paid-up equity shares of the Company, having face value 
of ~1/- (Indian Rupees One only) each ("Equity Shares"), representing 1.86 % of the

as at March 31, 2026, at a price of~ 215 (Indian Rupees Two Hundred And Fifteen 
Only) per Equity Share ("Buyback Price"), payable in cash, for an aggregate amount 
of up to 147,00,00, 150 (Indian Rupees One Hundred Forty-Seven Crore One Hundred

buyback, such as, brokerage, turnover charges, filing fees to SEBI, stock exchange

The Buyback is proposed to be made from all eligible equity shareholders/beneficial

below), in accordance with the provisions contained in the Securities and Exchange 
Board of India (Buy-Back of Securities) Regulations, 2018, as amended ("Buyback 
Regulations") and the Companies Act, 2013, as amended and rules made thereunder; 
3. The Board has noted that the promoter and promoter group of the Company have vide 
a letter dated November 4, 2026 expressed their intention not to participate in the 
Buyback. 
4. The formation of a buyback committee ("Buyback Committee") and delegated its 
powers to the Buyback Committee to do all such acts, deeds, matters and things as it 
may, in its absolute discretion, deem necessary, expedient, usual or proper in 
connection with the Buyback; 
5. Wednesday, November 11, 2026 as the record date ("Record Date") for the purpose 
of determining the entitlement and the names of equity shareholders/ beneficial owners 
of Equity Shares who shall be eligible to participate in the Buyback, pursuant to 
Regulation 42 of the SEBI Listing Regulations, as amended, and Regulation 9(i) of the 
SEBI Buyback Regulations, as amended. 
In terms of Regulation 5(via) of the Buyback Regulations, the Board/Buyback Committee may, 
till 1 (one) working day prior to the Record Date, increase the Buyback Price and decrease 
the number of Equity Shares proposed to be bought back, such that there is no change in the 
Buyback Size. 
The pre-Buyback shareholding pattern as on October 30, 2026, is enclosed as Annexure 8.

PRESS RELEASE 
• 
Jyothy labs 
RESULTS FOR THE QUARTER AND HALF YEAR ENDED SEPTEMBER 30, 2026 
Jyothy Labs maintains growth momentum in Q2 FY27 despite input cost headwinds, prioritizes 
progressive margin recovery 
Mumbai, November 4, 2026: Jyothy Labs Limited, one of India's leading fast-moving consumer goods 
(FMCG) companies, today announced its unaudited financial results for the quarter and half year ended 
September 30, 2026. 
The Company's underlying business continued to demonstrate healthy growth, supported by strong performance 
in Fabric Care, sustained momentum in the Exo franchise, new product launches and improving contributions 
from emerging trade channels. Excluding the Pril and Fa businesses, revenue grew by 12.4% in value and 8.1 % 
in volume during the quarter, reflecting the strength of its core portfolio. 
The broader FMCG operating environment remained challenging, with uneven demand recovery and 
unprecedented inflation in crude derivatives, palm oil, chemicals and packaging materials. While rural 
consumption continued to outperform urban markets, signs of gradual urban recovery were encouraging. 
However, rising input costs and continued pressure on consumer affordability weighed on industry profitability. 
Despite healthy underlying growth, the Company's profitability was significantly impacted by elevated 
commodity costs and the consumption of higher cost inventories. Management remains focused on 
progressively restoring margins through calibrated pricing, procurement efficiencies, value engineering, 
improved product mix and cost discipline, while protecting consumer demand and brand competitiveness. The 
Company continues to strengthen its core brands, accelerate new product launches and expand distribution 
across traditional and emerging channels. 
FINANCIAL HIGHLIGHTS-Q2 FY27 (YoY) 
• Revenue from Operations at <760 crore, representing 3.3% reported value growth. 
• Excluding Pril and Fa, revenue growth of 12.4% in value and 8.1 % in volume. 
• Operating EBITDA at <19.2 crore, with an EBITDA margin of2.5%, reflecting significant input cost 
inflation. 
• Profit After Tax at <10.6 crore. 
FINANCIAL HIGHLIGHTS - Hl FY27 (Yo Y) 
• Revenue from Operations at <1,533 crore, representing 3.1% reported value growth. 
• Excluding Pril and Fa, revenue growth of 10.2% in value and 6.2% in volume. 
• Operating EBITDA at <83.9 crore, with an EBITDA margin of 5.5%. 
• Profit After Tax at <58.2 crore. 
SEGMENT PERFORMANCE: 
FABRIC CARE - Fabric Whitener, Fabric Enhancer, Fabric Conditioner, Bar Soap, Detergent Powder, 
Liquid Detergent and Laundry Service 
Fabric Care maintained its strong growth momentum, delivering 10.4% value growth and 6.4% volume growth 
during the quarter. Growth was broad-based across the portfolio, led by continued momentum in liquid

detergents and supported by healthy performance in detergent powders and bars. Liquid detergents continued to 
lead category growth, supported by sustained consumer adoption and strong performance across Henko, Ujala, 
Morelight and Mr. White. Detergent powders and bars maintained healthy momentum, while Ujala Young and 
Fresh fabric conditioner continued to gain traction. The Company remains focused on strengthening its position 
in core laundry formats through innovation, distribution expansion and sustained brand investments. 
HOME CARE - Dish Wash Bar, Liquid, Gel, Powder and Scrubbers, Mosquito Repellent Coil, Liquid 
Vaporiser, Racquet, Aerosol, Agarbatti, Incense Sticks 
The Home Care segment delivered healthy underlying growth of 15.3% in value and 13.1% in volume, 
excluding Pril sales. The Exo franchise continued to demonstrate strong momentum, supported by expanding 
distribution. The recently launched bio enzyme-based Exo Dishwash Liquid, endorsed by Yami Gautam and 
Keerthy Suresh, has received an encouraging consumer response across markets and channels. The Company 
remains focused on further scaling the Exo portfolio to strengthen its presence in the Dishwash category. 
In Household Insecticides, the Company expanded its Maxo portfolio with the introduction ofMaxo Agarbatti, 
featuring a government approved mosquito control formulation. The launch addresses consumer demand for 
regulated mosquito repellent solutions and strengthens the Company's presence across key product formats. The 
strategic focus remains on scaling newer formats, improving product mix and progressively restoring 
profitability in Household Insecticides. 
PERSONAL CARE-Body Soap, Hand Wash and Toothpaste. 
Personal Care recorded 11.2% value growth during the quarter, while volumes declined marginally reflecting 
the impact of pricing actions and a favourable comparative base following last year's GST transition. The Margo 
franchise continued to benefit from focused brand investments and improved market visibility. The Company 
introduced Margo Gentle, a glycerine bathing soap, in Argan Oil and Moringa Oil variants in select markets, 
expanding the brand's presence in differentiated personal cleansing formats. 
Commenting on the financial performance of Q2 FY27, Ms. M. R. Jyothy, Chairperson and Managing 
Director, Jyothy Labs Limited said: 
"Q2 demonstrated the strength of our underlying business, delivering 12.4% value growth and 8.1% volume 
growth, excluding Pril and Fa, supported by healthy momentum in Fabric Care, Exo and new product launches. 
However, unprecedented inflation in raw material and packaging costs significantly impacted profitability, 
despite our pricing and cost efficiency measures. While near term margin pressures may persist, we remain 
confident of sustaining double digit underlying value growth in the coming quarters. Our priorities are to 
accelerate new launches, strengthen core brands and progressively restore margins through calibrated pricing, 
operational efficiencies and disciplined cost management. Our strong balance sheet provides us the financial 
flexibility to pursue both organic and selective inorganic growth opportunities, while maintaining discipline in 
capital allocation and a clear focus on long term shareholder value creation. " 
About Jyothy Labs Limited: Founded in 1983, Jyothy Labs Limited (JLL) has grown from a single-brand company with its 
flagship brand Ujala to a multi-brand FMCG listed on both BSE and NSE. Today, Jyothy Labs is a household name across India, 
producing and marketing a diverse range of products in Fabric Care, Home Care, and Personal Care Segments. The company's 
portfolio includes popular brands such as Ujala, Exo, Henka, Margo, Maxo, Mr. White, Morelight, Neem toothpaste, Jovia, Dr. Wool 
and Maya, each with a strong presence in its respective category and reco

MINING
The mining segment's performance remained healthy in 
Q2FY27, despite the seasonally slow monsoon period. 
Manganese ore production was 6% higher YoY, with some 
decline in sales volumes during the quarter. Iron ore 
production and sales grew 30% and 59% YoY respectively, with 
sales volumes also rising 29% on a sequential basis. 
From a realisations standpoint, manganese ore realisations 
improved further by 7% sequentially, building on the 15% 
improvement in Q1FY27, and now stand 43% higher YoY 
compared to Q2FY26. Iron ore realisations, on the other hand, 
saw a marginal 4% sequential decline, following the 9% 
improvement in Q1FY27. On an overall basis, the quarter 
marks a healthy performance for the mining segment.
On the compensatory afforestation requirement for the 
extension of the validity of our forest lease beyond December 
2026, we are taking the necessary steps to meet the 
compliance requirement.
GROWTH INITIATIVES IN MINING
We continue to invest in strengthening and growing our core 
mining business, with two key projects underway at the mines. 
The Downhill Conveyor System (DCS) project at the mines 
stands completed, and the asset has been capitalised in our 
books in Q1FY27. We await the approval from the Department 
of Mines and Geology (DMG) for the integration of the 
weighbridge with the ILMS portal. Once operational, the 
project will enable environment-friendly transportation of ore 
and is expected to fetch better realisations, as the ore will then 
be delivered directly to the railway siding, for the ease of our 
customers.
The Beneficiation Plant project at the mines, which we had 
commenced in Q1FY27, is progressing as per plan, with 
commissioning scheduled in Q2FY28. Civil works are underway 
and all critical equipment has been ordered.
Further, in a significant step towards our mining expansion, we 
have applied for an enhancement in the Environmental 
Clearance (EC) for Run-of-Mine (RoM) iron ore production 
from 7.85 MTPA to 9.42 MTPA, along with a reconfiguration of 
the proposed beneficiation plant from a single plant of 7.00 
MTPA to two plants of 3.5 MTPA each.
COKE AND ENERGY
2 of our 4 Coke Oven batteries continue to operate at 
optimum capacity utilisation, with steady offtake under the 
contract manufacturing agreement with our customer. For the 
remaining 2 batteries, we have already commenced work to 
restart them, and we expect to commence commercial 
production from these batteries in Q4FY27.
FERROALLOYS
The Ferroalloys segment continued to operate at steady state, 
with healthy throughput from our 2 operational furnaces and 
production up 8% sequentially. Realisations remained largely 
flat during the quarter, with a marginal 1% sequential decline, 
following two consecutive quarters of improvement. Once the 
remaining 2 Coke Oven batteries recommence production, the 
higher energy generation will support higher volumes for the 
Ferroalloys business, and in turn, better profitability for this 
segment.
ROYAL SANDUR METALS
An important update for our steel business has been the 
change in name and brand identity of our material subsidiary, 
from the erstwhile Arjas Steel Private Limited to Royal Sandur 
Metals Private Limited, in line with the Group's new brand 
architecture. Similarly, our step-down subsidiary, the erstwhile 
Arjas Modern Steel Private Limited, has been renamed Royal 
Sandur Green Steel Private Limited.
Royal Sandur Metals has delivered yet another quarter of 
healthy performance across all key parameters. Production 
and sales volumes grew 8% and 11% YoY respectively, with 
sales volumes also up 7% sequentially. Realisations improved 
5% sequentially, and profitability from the Steel business 
continues to remain robust, driven by a mix of internal cost 
optimisation and efficiency initiatives, a better operating 
environment and the growing scale of the business.
Further, in line with our focus on a value-added product 
portfolio, Royal Sandur Metals has undertaken a value-add 
project with a capital outlay of ₹100 crore towards setting up a 
new Bright Bar Facility and a Heat Treatment Facility, built as 
one integrated complex under a shared pre-engineered 
building (PEB) shed, which is expected to be commissioned 
within 20 months from project commencement.
ROYAL SANDUR GREEN STEEL
In a significant step for our steel business, a CAPEX of ₹220 
crore has been approved towards the expansion of our Punjab 
plant under step-down subsidiary Royal Sandur Green Steel 
Private Limited. The project will enhance the plant’s capacity 
from 1.20 LTPA to 1.70 LTPA of Special Bar Quality (SBQ) steel. 
The Electric Arc Furnace (EAF) is expected to be commissioned 
within 18 months and the rolling mill within 22 months from 
the start of the project, followed by a 6-month ramp-up to full 
production. This expansion also strengthens the Group’s 
presence in green steel, with the Punjab plant operating on the 
EAF route.
NEW FRONTIERS
In line with the unified Group identity adopted last quarter, 
which enables us to explore business opportunities beyond 
our existing segments, we have incorporated Royal Sandur 
Hospitality Private Limited (Hospitality sector) and Royal 
Sandur Academy Private Limited (Academy sector). The most 
significant step this quarter has been our Medical Devices and 
Consumables project.
ROYAL SANDUR MEDTECH
Following the opportunity we had highlighted last quarter, we 
have taken a decisive step towards our foray into the Medical 
Devices and Consumables business. In October 2026, Royal 
Sandur MedTech Private Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of 
the Company, executed a lease deed for 6.2 acres of 
developed land at the Andhra Pradesh MedTech Zone (AMTZ), 
Visakhapatnam, India's premier medical technology park, for 
setting up a manufacturing unit. This marks a concrete first 
step as part of our diversification strategy. Subsequently, the 
Board of Royal Sandur MedTech has approved a CAPEX of 
₹390 crore towards this project to start the commercial 
production by December 2027. The facility will target the 
manufacturing of products including catheters, IV cannula, 
syringes and IV sets.

MINING
The mining segment's performance remained healthy in 
Q2FY27, despite the seasonally slow monsoon period. 
Manganese ore production was 6% higher YoY, with some 
decline in sales volumes during the quarter. Iron ore 
production and sales grew 30% and 59% YoY respectively, with 
sales volumes also rising 29% on a sequential basis. 
From a realisations standpoint, manganese ore realisations 
improved further by 7% sequentially, building on the 15% 
improvement in Q1FY27, and now stand 43% higher YoY 
compared to Q2FY26. Iron ore realisations, on the other hand, 
saw a marginal 4% sequential decline, following the 9% 
improvement in Q1FY27. On an overall basis, the quarter 
marks a healthy performance for the mining segment.
On the compensatory afforestation requirement for the 
extension of the validity of our forest lease beyond December 
2026, we are taking the necessary steps to meet the 
compliance requirement.
GROWTH INITIATIVES IN MINING
We continue to invest in strengthening and growing our core 
mining business, with two key projects underway at the mines. 
The Downhill Conveyor System (DCS) project at the mines 
stands completed, and the asset has been capitalised in our 
books in Q1FY27. We await the approval from the Department 
of Mines and Geology (DMG) for the integration of the 
weighbridge with the ILMS portal. Once operational, the 
project will enable environment-friendly transportation of ore 
and is expected to fetch better realisations, as the ore will then 
be delivered directly to the railway siding, for the ease of our 
customers.
The Beneficiation Plant project at the mines, which we had 
commenced in Q1FY27, is progressing as per plan, with 
commissioning scheduled in Q2FY28. Civil works are underway 
and all critical equipment has been ordered.
Further, in a significant step towards our mining expansion, we 
have applied for an enhancement in the Environmental 
Clearance (EC) for Run-of-Mine (RoM) iron ore production 
from 7.85 MTPA to 9.42 MTPA, along with a reconfiguration of 
the proposed beneficiation plant from a single plant of 7.00 
MTPA to two plants of 3.5 MTPA each.
COKE AND ENERGY
2 of our 4 Coke Oven batteries continue to operate at 
optimum capacity utilisation, with steady offtake under the 
contract manufacturing agreement with our customer. For the 
remaining 2 batteries, we have already commenced work to 
restart them, and we expect to commence commercial 
production from these batteries in Q4FY27.
FERROALLOYS
The Ferroalloys segment continued to operate at steady state, 
with healthy throughput from our 2 operational furnaces and 
production up 8% sequentially. Realisations remained largely 
flat during the quarter, with a marginal 1% sequential decline, 
following two consecutive quarters of improvement. Once the 
remaining 2 Coke Oven batteries recommence production, the 
higher energy generation will support higher volumes for the 
Ferroalloys business, and in turn, better profitability for this 
segment.
ROYAL SANDUR METALS
An important update for our steel business has been the 
change in name and brand identity of our material subsidiary, 
from the erstwhile Arjas Steel Private Limited to Royal Sandur 
Metals Private Limited, in line with the Group's new brand 
architecture. Similarly, our step-down subsidiary, the erstwhile 
Arjas Modern Steel Private Limited, has been renamed Royal 
Sandur Green Steel Private Limited.
Royal Sandur Metals has delivered yet another quarter of 
healthy performance across all key parameters. Production 
and sales volumes grew 8% and 11% YoY respectively, with 
sales volumes also up 7% sequentially. Realisations improved 
5% sequentially, and profitability from the Steel business 
continues to remain robust, driven by a mix of internal cost 
optimisation and efficiency initiatives, a better operating 
environment and the growing scale of the business.
Further, in line with our focus on a value-added product 
portfolio, Royal Sandur Metals has undertaken a value-add 
project with a capital outlay of ₹100 crore towards setting up a 
new Bright Bar Facility and a Heat Treatment Facility, built as 
one integrated complex under a shared pre-engineered 
building (PEB) shed, which is expected to be commissioned 
within 20 months from project commencement.
ROYAL SANDUR GREEN STEEL
In a significant step for our steel business, a CAPEX of ₹220 
crore has been approved towards the expansion of our Punjab 
plant under step-down subsidiary Royal Sandur Green Steel 
Private Limited. The project will enhance the plant’s capacity 
from 1.20 LTPA to 1.70 LTPA of Special Bar Quality (SBQ) steel. 
The Electric Arc Furnace (EAF) is expected to be commissioned 
within 18 months and the rolling mill within 22 months from 
the start of the project, followed by a 6-month ramp-up to full 
production. This expansion also strengthens the Group’s 
presence in green steel, with the Punjab plant operating on the 
EAF route.
NEW FRONTIERS
In line with the unified Group identity adopted last quarter, 
which enables us to explore business opportunities beyond 
our existing segments, we have incorporated Royal Sandur 
Hospitality Private Limited (Hospitality sector) and Royal 
Sandur Academy Private Limited (Academy sector). The most 
significant step this quarter has been our Medical Devices and 
Consumables project.
ROYAL SANDUR MEDTECH
Following the opportunity we had highlighted last quarter, we 
have taken a decisive step towards our foray into the Medical 
Devices and Consumables business. In October 2026, Royal 
Sandur MedTech Private Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of 
the Company, executed a lease deed for 6.2 acres of 
developed land at the Andhra Pradesh MedTech Zone (AMTZ), 
Visakhapatnam, India's premier medical technology park, for 
setting up a manufacturing unit. This marks a concrete first 
step as part of our diversification strategy. Subsequently, the 
Board of Royal Sandur MedTech has approved a CAPEX of 
₹390 crore towards this project to start the commercial 
production by December 2027. The facility will target the 
manufacturing of products including catheters, IV cannula, 
syringes and IV sets.

FINANCIAL 
HIGHLIGHTS
Q2 & H1 FY27

Key Highlights of the Quarter 
Q2 FY27 reflected resilient execution and steady progress on our strategic priorities. On a 
consolidated basis, Total Revenue grew 36% year-on-year to ₹472 crore, EBITDA rose 58% 
to ₹106 crore with a margin of 22%, and PAT increased 82% to ₹67 crore. For H1 FY27, 
consolidated PAT nearly doubled to ₹146 crore.
Volumes were dented by external factors, including raw material availability and delayed 
supply chains, yet our stable product portfolio kept the top line resilient, with standalone 
volumes improving 11% over Q1. Commercial production commenced at our upgraded 
Acetonitrile facility, and with PESO approval of DME road tanker valves, we are now building 
our DME customer network.
N-Methyl Morpholine is our next product for commercialisation, while BSCL's Unit-I 
brownfield expansion is on track for commissioning by end-FY27 and the Unit-II HCN, 
NaCN and EDTA project is targeted for Q4 FY27. With a visible expansion roadmap and 
disciplined execution, we remain confident of driving sustainable growth and long-term 
shareholder value.

Key Highlights of the Quarter 
Q2 FY27 reflected resilient execution and steady progress on our strategic priorities. On a 
consolidated basis, Total Revenue grew 36% year-on-year to ₹472 crore, EBITDA rose 58% 
to ₹106 crore with a margin of 22%, and PAT increased 82% to ₹67 crore. For H1 FY27,

supply chains, yet our stable product portfolio kept the top line resilient, with standalone 
volumes improving 11% over Q1. Commercial production commenced at our upgraded 
Acetonitrile facility, and with PESO approval of DME road tanker valves, we are now building

Moderator: 
Good afternoon, everyone. Welcome to the Q2 FY27 Earnings call of OnEMI Technology 
Solutions Limited.  
We have with us today Mr. Ranvir Singh, Chairman, Director, and Chief Executive Officer, Mr. 
Krishnan Vishwanathan, Director and Chief Financial Officer, and the Senior Management 
Team. I shall now hand over the call to the management for their opening remarks. Over to 
you, gentlemen. 
Ranvir Singh: 
Thank you, Mehak. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to Kissht’s Q2 FY27 Earnings call. 
Let me start with a simple thought. Lending is one of the oldest businesses in the world, but 
the way we practice it, is decidedly new. We have compressed what traditionally took days into 
a matter of minutes. Today, a customer can go from the first tap on a phone to money in their 
bank account in just a few minutes. Behind that simplicity sits years of investment, across data 
science, AI, machine learning, underwriting intelligence, and technology-led collections. What 
looks effortless to the customer is enormous complexity behind the scenes. And that, in many 
ways, is the essence of what we have built at Kissht. In lending, one good quarter proves very 
little. Growth is remarkably easy to achieve: just lower your standards, and the applause comes 
immediately, but the reckoning comes later. So the only honest measure of a lender is 
consistency, which means growing without loosening credit standards, and earning without 
shortcuts… quarter after quarter. This quarter for us, registered users reached 79.5 million, up 
32.6% year-on-year. We have now served 12.8 million customers, up 22.5%. AUM reached Rs. 
9,317 crore, up 68.4% year-on-year, and 16.4% quarter on quarter. Profit after tax was Rs. 125 
crore, double of what we earned a year ago, and 31.6% above last quarter. Return on average 
AUM was 5.78%. We believe growth without profitability is, expensive ambition, while 
profitability without growth is comfortable stagnation. The real achievement is to deliver both 
-  not at the expense of tomorrow, but on the strength of what we built today.  
On the macro picture, India's economy remains remarkably resilient, despite an unsettled 
world. GDP grew 7.8% in the first quarter, and the RBI has raised its FY27 growth forecast to 
7.1%. Despite a below-average monsoon and some softness in urban discretionary spends, 
consumption is turning up. FMCG value growth hit a six-quarter high of 8.6% in Q2. The festive 
season and industry tell the same story. E-commerce festive season sales are up 20-22%. 
Electricity consumption rose 11.4% in September, a strong signal of industrial activity. Further, 
GST collection is up 14% year-on-year. At the same time, the RBI has raised the repo rate by 25 
basis points to 5.50%, in what is clearly a calibrated tightening. The message is clear : Growth 
remains robust, but money is getting dearer. Even as borrowing costs rise across the system, 
our cost of borrowing has fallen by approximately 70 basis points, from 14.45% to 13.76%. The 
total finance cost, as a share of average AUM, has also fallen by 100 basis points quarter on 
quarter. Policy tightening may slow this improvement, but we do not expect it to reverse the 
trend, and we will continue to see reduction in our cost of fund for future. On regulation, the 
proposed IRDAI changes on insurance commissions and loan-link insurance have drawn a lot 
of attention. Insurance is less than 1.4% of our total income, our offerings have always been 
voluntary, and we expect no material impact on earnings.  

  
 
 
 
 
    OnEMI Technology Solutions Limited  
 
 
October 29, 2026 
 
Page 3 of 18 
 
We also welcome the RBI's move to make account aggregators interoperable by December 
2026. In lending, better information is not merely an advantage, it is the foundation of better 
judgment. Consent-based access to verified financial data will make our underwriting both 
faster and more precise. The macro environment offers reasons for confidence, but none for 
complacency. Our priorities remain unchanged, which is basically disciplined underwriting, 
prudent funding, and sustainable growth.  
Let me turn to what we are seeing in the retail credit market. Across the industry, retail loan 
sanctions are up by nearly 20% year-on-year. Lenders are favoring larger loans and better 
quality borrowers, and the share of below-prime and new-to-credit customers is falling. Yet, as 
per Bureau, the industry Retail credit balances have grown 19%, while the number of 
borrowers has grown less than 9%. The implication is clear, indebtedness is rising far faster 
than the borrower base. That warrants close attention. At Kissht, we have been moving 
deliberately in the opposite direction, which is going after less leveraged customers. The share 
of new loans to customers with 3 or more live loans has fallen more than 35% over the past 12 
months, and more than 7% quarter on quarter. While the industry's borrowers are getting 
more leveraged, we are steadily lending less to leveraged borrowers. Our shift towards higher 
quality borrowers continues. Loans to customers with bureau scores above 760 has risen from 
20.8% to 24.8%. And only about 4% of our loans go to customer scoring Below 700. Gold loans 
are another example. We flagged rising gold loan exposure as a risk in September 2025, and 13 
months back began restricting lending to consumers carrying gold loan. Which has now come 
down to as low as sub 8% of the total book, with tighter curbs in the North than in the South. 
We've acted well before the industry began worrying about stress in gold loans. Our machine-
learning models continuously flag early signs of stress, and the segments where exposure 
needs to be cut. The objective is simple… act before the stress reaches the balance sheet. And 
let me tell you, this is business as usual for us, not an occasional intervention. This is something 
that we do daily, day in, day out. Our underwriting discipline doesn't depend on a kind credit 
cycle. We tighten early, grow selectively, and lend only where the numbers earn it.  
Talking about key numbers, AUM grew to Rs. 9,317 crore, up 68% year-on-year, 16% quarter-
on-quarter. Disbursements were Rs. 4,612 crore, up 56% year-on-year. AUM is growing faster 
than the disbursement, and that is by design. Our better customers take longer-tenure loans, 
so each rupee we lend stays on the book longer, and with a better quality outcome. Average 
tenure has risen to 17.8 months, and the average ticket to Rs. 43,380. We have a high latitude 
to increase our ticket size. Let me repeat, we have a high latitude to increase our ticket size; 
however, given our overall prudence in limiting customer-level exposure, we have kept it 
deliberately moderate.  
Our base keeps broadening. We have served 12.8 million customers, up 22% year-on-year, and 
active customers grew 58% year-on-year to 3.61 million. Total income was Rs. 740 crore, up 
43% year-on-year. As a share of average AUM, it moved from 35.9% to 34.2% quarter on 
quarter. That reflects our relentless focus on better-credit worthy customers. And as our own 
costs fall, we share part of the gain with our customers, which attracts even better borrowers. 

  
 
 
 
 
    OnEMI Technology Solutions Limited  
 
 
October 29, 2026 
 
Page 4 of 18 
 
It's a virtuous cycle : lower costs, better customers, and then lower risk. Pre-provisioning 
operating profit was Rs. 287 crores, up 40% year-on-year, and 12% quarter on quarter. Profit 
after tax was Rs. 125 crore, which has doubled year on year, and is up 32% quarter on quarter. 
Return on average AUM rose 73 basis points to 5.78%, and return on average equity was 
21.65%.  
Talking about asset quality. It improved on almost every measure, rather emphatically and 
unambiguously. Credit costs fell to 6.2% of average AUM, from 6.8% last quarter and 9.3% a 
year ago. Last quarter, we said the rise in Stage-2 was seasonal. It has reversed, as we said it 
would. Stage-2 is back to 2.37%, from 3.15% in June, and 4.11% a year ago. The Stage-2, we 
expect to remain constant throughout the year. Gross NPA improved to 2.18%, down 7 basis 
points over the quarter, and 75 basis points over the year. Net NPA was 0.34%, better by 2 
basis points compared with last quarter. The earliest signal of loan quality is improving, too. 
First EMI 90+ delinquency fell to 0.69%, from 0.73% last quarter and 1.16% a year ago. 
Collection efficiency was 97.12%, which is better by 30 bps compared with last quarter. We 
continue to provide conservatively, with Stage-3 coverage at 84.6% and Stage-2 coverage at 
77.6%. As far as asset quality goes, we would rather be accused of caution than caught without 
it. Talking about our LAP business, we continue to scale steadily. AUM is Rs. 737 crore, or 7.9% 
of the total, up from 4.1% a year ago. We now operate across 107 branches in 9 states and 
union territories. More than 40% of LAP customers are existing Kissht customers. One 
important thing on LAP is, LAP has turned positive this quarter, a quarter ahead of the break-
even we guided, which is in Q2, it has happened, as against Q3, what we had mentioned in the 
past.  
Talking about the balance sheet, net worth stood at Rs. 2,377 crore as on September 2026. 
Capital adequacy is 34.76%, down from 40.19% last quarter. That is exactly what should happen 
as IPO capital is put to work, and it remains well above what regulation requires. On book debt 
to equity is a conservative 0.94X. Our average cost of borrowing is 13.76%. Finance cost fell 
12% over the quarter, even as borrowings grew, that is the roll-off of legacy borrowings at 
work, rather. Funding remains well spread… on-book AUM of Rs 4,199 crore, and off-book AUM 
of Rs. 5,118 crore, a 45:55 split with more than 45 lending partners. Our NBFC subsidiary is 
rated A-/stable by CRISIL and India Ratings, and A/stable by Acuite, which upgraded us this 
quarter. 
We also completed a preferential allotment of Rs. 832 crore, approved by shareholders at the 
EGM on 14th October, and subsequently received in-principle approval from the exchanges. 
The benefit of this net worth, we will only see from next quarter onwards. It drew large 
marquee investors, a clear vote of confidence in the long road ahead, for us. Talking about 
technology, rather than walk you through our architecture again, let me tell you what changed 
this quarter. I believe AI is easy to talk about and much harder to put in motion, where it 
delivers a strong P&L impact. The only claim worth making is one you can measure. On 
underwriting, I would say AI improves our decision in two ways, very, very emphatic ways, 
rather. First, better models, now in their 42nd iteration, with an AUC (Area Under the Curve) 

  
 
 
 
 
    OnEMI Technology Solutions Limited  
 
 
October 29, 2026 
 
Page 5 of 18 
 
of 75%, up from 66% in 2023. AUC measures how well a model separates those who will repay 
from those who will not. The higher it goes, the fewer good customers we turn away, and the 
fewer bad loans we make. Transformer-based sequence models alone added 2.5 points of that 
gain… trained on more than 10 million data points, by a team of over 50 data scientists. The 
second benefit is, the faster feedback… monitoring agents watch the portfolio, and the models 
themselves, for drift. They flag deterioration by location, by customer profile, and in model 
performance. And they do it in real time, not months later when defaults show up. Mind you, 
I reiterate real time, not a month later, not a week later, now. Our risk team acts on each flag 
tightening policy for a region, or a segment, or recalibrating a model. Last quarter, that meant 
7 such actions. And for us, that is simply business as usual. Our job, every single day, as I 
mentioned, is to catch every signal, big or small, and to act on it before it becomes a loss. On 
collections, our voice agents in early buckets now recover at more than 85% of a human caller's 
rate. This is up from 80% last quarter, and 70% before that.  
On fraud management, we use specialist AI agents for documents and images, text, data 
patterns, and networks. The AI agent proposes new fraud rules on its own as patterns emerge. 
In LAP, AI now reads and verifies income proofs, bank statements, property documents of 
myriad types with vernacular fluency, and flags any anomaly in valuation. Each of these AI 
initiatives, I should say, lowers a cost or lowers a risk, because for us, AI is not at the periphery, 
not at the boundaries, but it is very much at the core. On cybersecurity, all our systems are fully 
patched against PHP2Shell, the critical PHP weakness flagged by cybersecurity agencies last 
week.  
Moving on to the guidance for the future. Given the momentum in the first half, we are raising 
our FY27 AUM growth guidance from 40% plus to 60% plus. We are also raising our target for 
reduction in impairment cost, we had said it will come down by 10-15%. We are now saying it 
will be emphatically more than 15% reduction year on year. The rest of our guidance stands : 
return on average equity would be above 20%, and the gross NPA below 2.25%. I reiterate, we 
remain firmly on track on all other profitability-related guidance. 
As closing remarks, I should say two quarters as a listing company is a short period, but even a 
short record can tell you a great deal. What it tells you is a bigger book and a cleaner one, rising 
profits and a falling cost. In lending, these pairs are not supposed to travel together. When they 
do, it is because the hard work was done long before the numbers showed it. In the models we 
built, in the collections we ran, and in the loans we had the discipline to refuse. I should say 
ambition is easy to announce, discipline has to be demonstrated. And here, trust is not asked 
for, it is earned, one quarter at a time. The opportunity in India is vast, and we intend to pursue 
it with conviction as much as with care. With that, my thanks to our lending partners, our team, 
our investors, including all those who have joined us on this call for this quarter. We are happy 
to take your questions now. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. The first question comes from 
the line of Meet Trivedi. Please go ahead. 

  
 
 
 
 
    OnEMI Technology Solutions Limited  
 
 
October 29, 2026

Meet Trivedi: 
Thank you for giving me the opportunity. So, I just had, one question that, like, if I'm, correct, 
the AUM for this quarter has grown by 68% year-on-year, whereas the customers that we cater 
to have only grown by 21-22, odd percentages. So, like, just wanted to ask that what… where 
is this growth coming from in the AUM? Like, is there an average ticket size increasing, or is 
there something else? 
Ranvir Singh: 
Yeah, absolutely. The growth is coming from three big sources. Number one, it is coming on 
account of deepening the existing customer base. When I say, deepening the existing customer 
base, if you look at our repeat customer rate, it has gone up. Not only the repeat customer… 
so the deepening reflects not only in the share of repeat increasing, but more importantly, the 
ticket size of the repeat has also increased. So that's one big driver of growth.  
The second big driver of growth, where I think one of the strategies we have tried 
communicating unambiguously without any scruples, that with every passing day, we are going 
after high-quality customers. When I say high-quality customers, it simply means the 
probability of default I attach to them is significantly lower. And when I do that, these 
customers come at a higher ticket size. So because they are high quality, their requirement is 
high, their income levels justify a higher income, etc. So that's the second, part, you know, 
which is adding to the growth, because the ticket size is increasing.  
Last but not the least, there is an overall growth that we see, which is also happening on 
account of our tenure increasing. We have been extremely prudent in increasing the tenure. 
But, if you compare it with, you know, say, last one year, there has been a slight increase in the 
tenure. It is actually linked to point 1 and 2 only, because when you cater to high-quality 
customers, their expectation is higher. You want to give them at a lower rate to make the

have done two fundraises since, you know, the rating, since, the, A- was given by CRISIL, and A

Good afternoon, everyone. Welcome to the Q2 FY27 Earnings call of OnEMI Technology 
Solutions Limited.  
We have with us today Mr. Ranvir Singh, Chairman, Director, and Chief Executive Officer, Mr. 
Krishnan Vishwanathan, Director and Chief Financial Officer, and the Senior Management
